exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with the kettlebell placed on the floor about a foot in front of you. Hinge at your hips with a flat back and grasp the kettlebell handle firmly with both hands.

Execution:
1. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs like a center passing a football.
2. Explosively snap your hips forward and contract your glutes and hamstrings to swing the kettlebell up to chest/eye level.
3. Guide the kettlebell as it falls back down, absorbing the weight into your hips, and repeat in a fluid rhythm.

Notes:
The movement is an explosive hip hinge, not a squat. Do not lift the weight with your arms or shoulders.
exercises.author: deusinvictus

exercises.name: Seated Hip Adduction
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit upright on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest and the pads resting against the inside of your thighs/knees. Grab the side handles for stability.

Execution:
1. Squeeze your thighs together against the resistance pads in a controlled movement by contracting your adductors.
2. Hold the peak contraction briefly as the pads come close together.
3. Slowly reverse the movement and open your legs, controlling the weight stack without letting the plates crash.

Notes:
Keep your torso stable and back flat against the pad throughout the movement.
exercises.author: flori

exercises.name: Arnold Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit upright on a bench with back support. Hold two dumbbells in front of your chest at shoulder height, palms facing your body (supinated) with elbows tucked under your wrists.

Execution:
1. Press the dumbbells overhead while smoothly rotating your hands outward so that your palms face forward (pronated) at the top of the lift.
2. Fully extend your arms without locking out your elbows.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back along the same path, rotating your palms back toward your chest to return to the starting position.

Notes:
Perform the rotation smoothly throughout the upward and downward press. Maintain a tight core and neutral spine against the backrest.
exercises.author: trzr23

exercises.name: Axe Hold
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and your core braced. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

Execution:
1. Raise both dumbbells out to your sides (lateral abduction) with arms straight or slightly bent at the elbows until they are parallel to the floor at shoulder height.
2. Hold this static isometric position for as long as prescribed or until failure, keeping your lateral deltoids contracted.
3. Lower the weights slowly and under control once time expires.

Notes:
Do not shrug your shoulders toward your ears or arch your lower back. Maintain a steady breathing rhythm during the hold.
exercises.author: GrosseHund

exercises.name: Barbell Ab Rollout
exercises.description:
Kneel on the mat and place a barbell on the floor in front of you.
Grip the barbell shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
With a slow, controlled motion, roll the bar forward until your body is extended and your back is straight.
Pull the barbell back using your abdominal muscles to return to the starting position.
exercises.author: sevae

exercises.name: Barbell Hack Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place a barbell on the floor directly behind your heels. Stand with feet hip-width to shoulder-width apart. Squat down keeping your chest up and back flat, and grasp the barbell behind your legs with an overhand grip (palms facing backward).

Execution:
1. Drive through your heels and feet to extend your knees and hips, lifting the barbell up along the backs of your legs until you are standing fully erect.
2. Squeeze your quadriceps and glutes at the top.
3. Lower the barbell back down under control along the same path until the plates touch the floor.

Notes:
Keep your torso as upright as possible throughout the movement to emphasize the quadriceps.
exercises.author: BePieToday

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Lunge
exercises.description:
Put barbell on the back of your shoulders. Stand upright, then take the first step forward. Step should bring you forward so that your supporting legs knee can touch the floor. Then stand back up and repeat with the other leg.
Remember to keep good posture.
exercises.author: Mikko Ruohola

exercises.name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Sitting on a bench, grab a barbell with your palms facing down and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.
Curl your knuckles towards your face, lifting the barbell. Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.
exercises.author: burenl

exercises.name: Barbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Position barbell overhead with narrow overhand grip.
Lower forearm behind upper arm with elbows remaining overhead. Extend forearm overhead. Lower and repeat.
exercises.author: sevae

exercises.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Sitting on a bench, grab a barbell with your palms facing up and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees. Perform the movement by curling your palms and wrists towards your face.
Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.
exercises.author: burenl

exercises.name: Abdominal Stabilization
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie lengthwise on a foam roller placed along your spine, ensuring your head, back, and tailbone are all supported. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.

Execution:
1. Engage your deep core muscles (transverse abdominis) by gently flattening your lower back toward the roller.
2. Maintain balance and stability using core contraction. Keep your fingertips lightly resting on the floor for support, or cross your arms over your chest to increase the challenge.
3. Hold the position for the prescribed duration while maintaining slow, deep breaths.

Notes:
Do not let your lower back arch off the roller. Keep your pelvis neutral and stable.
exercises.author: andikeller

exercises.name: Bear Walk
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Get down on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Tuck your toes and lift your knees a few inches off the floor, keeping your back flat.

Execution:
1. Step forward by simultaneously moving your right hand and left foot.
2. Follow by stepping forward with your left hand and right foot, crawling in a cross-body contralateral pattern.
3. Move at a controlled, steady pace over a set distance (e.g., 20–30 meters) or duration (e.g., 45 seconds).

Notes:
Keep your hips low and parallel to the floor, avoiding excessive side-to-side sway. Keep your core and quads engaged.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: Single Leg Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit in the leg extension machine with your back firmly supported by the backrest. Position the padded lever against the lower shin of one leg, just above the ankle. The non-working leg remains relaxed.

Execution:
1. Extend your working leg upward by contracting your quadriceps until the knee is nearly straight.
2. Hold the peak contraction at the top for one second.
3. Lower the weight slowly and under control back to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch down.

Notes:
Complete all repetitions on one leg before switching to the other. Keep your hips and back pressed firmly into the seat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.description:
Lay down on a bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.
If you train with a high weight it is advisable to have a spotter that can help you up if you can't lift the weight on your own.
With the width of the grip you can also control which part of the chest is trained more:

wide grip: outer chest muscles
narrow grip: inner chest muscles and triceps
exercises.author: sistab2

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description:
Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.


The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.


Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.


Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45–60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.


Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Bench Press Narrow Grip
exercises.description:
Setup: Lie flat on the bench and grip the bar at shoulder-width (closer than a standard bench press).
Descent: Lower the bar with control to your lower chest.
Form: Keep your elbows tucked in tight against your torso—do not let them flare out.
Ascent: Press the bar straight back up, squeezing your triceps at the top.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Bent High Pulls
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a pair of dumbbells in front of your thighs. Hinge forward at the hips with slightly bent knees and a flat back until your torso is angled forward, arms hanging straight down.

Execution:
1. Pull the dumbbells up vertically toward your chest/armpits, flaring your elbows high and wide.
2. Squeeze your rear deltoids and upper back at the top of the movement.
3. Lower the dumbbells slowly and under control back to the starting hang position.

Notes:
Keep your back straight and core tight throughout. The movement should be driven by the elbows pulling high.
exercises.author: lakerbeezel

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Place one knee on a flat bench and brace yourself with the hand on the same side. Hold a dumbbell in the free hand, pull it close to your body, lower it under control, then repeat on the other side.
exercises.author: sebk

exercises.name: Bent-Over Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Sit on bench while holding weights. Bend forward as far as possible, with arms slightly bent at the elbow. Perform a lateral raise while maintaining the bend in your elbow.
exercises.author: apeschel

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description:
Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description:
The same as regular rowing, but holding a reversed grip (your palms pointing forwards):
Grab the barbell with a wide grIp (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise.
Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Barbell Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Hold the Barbell shoulder-wide, the back is straight, the shoulders slightly back, the arms are streched. Bend the arms, bringing the weight up, with a fast movement. Without pausing, let down the bar with a slow and controlled movement.
Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Hold two dumbbells, the arms are streched, the hands are on your side, the palms face inwards. Bend the arms and bring the weight with a fast movement up. At the same time, rotate your arms by 90 degrees at the very beginning of the movement. At the highest point, rotate a little the weights further outwards. Without a pause, bring them down, slowly.
Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Hold the EZ-bar shoulder-wide, the back is straight, the shoulders slightly back, the arms are streched. Bend the arms, bringing the weight up, with a fast movement. Without pausing, let down the bar with a slow and controlled movement.
Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.description: Stand around 30 - 40cm away from the cable, the feet are firmly on the floor. Take the bar and lift the weight with a fast movements. Lower the weight as with the dumbbell curls slowly and controlled.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Body-Ups
exercises.description:
Assume a plank position on the ground. You should be supporting your bodyweight on your toes and forearms, keeping your torso straight. Your forearms should be shoulder-width apart. This will be your starting position.
Pressing your palms firmly into the ground, extend through the elbows to raise your body from the ground. Keep your torso rigid as you perform the movement.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the ground by allowing the elbows to flex.
Repeat as needed.
exercises.author: cal.zabel

exercises.name: Braced Squat
exercises.description:
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, while standing as tall as you can.
Grab a weight plate and hold it out in front of your body with arms straight out. Keep your core tight and stand with a natural arch in your back.
Now, push hips back and bend knees down into a squat as far as you can. Hold for a few moments and bring yourself back up to the starting position.
exercises.author: sevae

exercises.name: Chest Press
exercises.description:
Adjust the seat height so that the grips are parallel to your chest.
Use your legs to push the foot forward pedal.
Bring the handles to the start position.
Keep your back in contact with the back pad, press outwards.
Press the handles away from your chest and exhale.
Allow the handles to come in gently until they reach your chest.
Allow the handles to return to your chest as you inhale.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Burpees
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.

Execution:
1. Drop your hips into a squat and place your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet.
2. Jump both feet back simultaneously into a high plank position.
3. Lower your body and perform a full push-up, touching your chest to the floor.
4. Push back up, then jump your feet forward toward your hands to return to the deep squat position.
5. Explosively jump straight up into the air, reaching your arms overhead, and land softly on the balls of your feet to immediately begin the next repetition.

Notes:
Keep your core braced during the plank and push-up phase to avoid sagging your hips.
exercises.author: er0355

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly (Butterfly)
exercises.description: Sit on the butterfly machine, the feet have a good contact with the floor, the upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press your arms together till the handles are practically together (but aren't!). Go slowly back. The weights should stay all the time in the air.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Butterfly Narrow Grip
exercises.description:
The movement is the same as with a regular butterfly, only that the grip is narrow:
Sit on the butterfly machine, the feet have a good contact with the floor, the upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press your arms together till the handles are practically together (but aren't!). Go slowly back. The weights should stay all the time in the air.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck (Rear Delt Fly)
exercises.description: Sit at the reverse butterfly machine with your chest against the pad. Pull the handles back by moving your arms out to the sides, then return them under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Cable External Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set the cable pulley to elbow height. Stand sideways to the cable tower and grasp the handle with your outside hand (the hand furthest from the cable). Bend your elbow to a 90-degree angle and keep it pinned against your flank (you may place a small rolled towel between your elbow and torso).

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbow securely tucked against your side, rotate your forearm outward away from your body as far as comfortable.
2. Squeeze your rotator cuff muscles at the end range of motion and pause for a second.
3. Slowly return the handle back across your torso to the starting position under control.

Notes:
Keep your torso stationary without twisting your spine or hips. The rotation must originate purely from the shoulder joint.
exercises.author: lauroernesto

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper
exercises.description: Set cable pulley slightly lower than chest height. Keep body facing forward with hips stable. Grab the pulley handle, fully extend your arms and bring your arms forward and across your body. Hold for 1 second at the end of the movement and slowly return to starting position.
exercises.author: robhoyt

exercises.name: Calf Press Using Leg Press Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit in the leg press machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the sled/footplate, allowing your heels to hang free off the bottom. Disengage the safety stops with your knees slightly bent (not locked).

Execution:
1. Lower your heels backward by flexing your ankles to get a full stretch in your calf muscles.
2. Push through the balls of your feet and toes to press the platform away, achieving full plantarflexion.
3. Squeeze your calves at the peak contraction for one second, then slowly lower back to the stretched position.

Notes:
Keep your knees slightly unlocked throughout the entire set to focus the tension entirely on the gastrocnemius.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: Hack Squat Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Place yourself on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest, the feet are on the platform for calf raises. Check that the feet are half free and that you can completely stretch the calf muscles down.
With straight knees pull up your weight as much as you can. Go with a fluid movement down till the calves are completely stretched. Repeat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Chin Up
exercises.description: The chin-up (also known as a chin or chinup) is a strength training exercise. People frequently do this exercise with the intention of strengthening muscles such as the latissimus dorsi and biceps, which extend the shoulder and flex the elbow, respectively. In this maneuver, the palms are faced towards the body. It is a form of pull-up in which the range of motion is established in relation to a person's chin.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Grip the pull-down bar with your hands closer than shoulder width apart, with your palms facing away from you. Lean back slightly. Pull the bar down towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides as you come down. Pull your shoulders back at the end of the motion.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Cross-Bench Dumbbell Pullovers
exercises.description: Grasp a moderately weighted dumbbell so your palms are flat against the underside of the top plates and your thumbs are around the bar. Lie on your back across a flat bench so only your upper back and shoulders are in contact with the bench. Your feet should be set about shoulder-width apart and your head should hang slightly downward. With the dumbbell supported at arm's length directly about your chest, bend your arms about 15 degrees and keep them bent throughout the movement. Slowly lower the dumbbell backward and downward in a semicircle arc to as low a position as is comfortably possible. Raise it slowly back along the same arc to the starting point, and repeat for the required number of repetitions.
exercises.author: powerade69

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Knee Tuck
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a high plank / push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor and your shins resting on top of a Swiss ball. Keep your body in a straight line from shoulders to ankles with your core braced.

Execution:
1. Contract your abdominals and hip flexors to pull your knees forward toward your chest, rolling the ball forward onto your toes.
2. Squeeze your core at the peak contraction for one second.
3. Slowly extend your legs back out, rolling the ball backward until you return to the straight plank position.

Notes:
Do not let your lower back sag or your hips drop below parallel. Keep your shoulders locked directly over your wrists.
exercises.author: Konsumopfer

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Place your hands lightly behind your head (without interlocking fingers) or cross them over your chest.

Execution:
1. Contract your abdominal muscles to curl your upper spine, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor toward your pelvis.
2. Pause and hold the peak contraction for one second at the top while exhaling.
3. Slowly lower your upper back down under control, keeping tension on your abs throughout.

Notes:
Do not pull on your neck with your hands. Keep your lower back in contact with the mat; this is a spinal curl, not a full sit-up.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.description: Lay down on your back on a inclined bench, feet are on one end of the bench. Ask a partner or use some other help (barbell, etc.) to keep them fixed, your hands are behind your head. From this position move your upper body up till your head or elbows touch your knees. Do this movement by rolling up your back.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
exercises.description: The procedure is very similar as for regular crunches, only with the additional weight of the machine. Sit on the machine, put both feet firmly on the ground. Grab the to the weights, cables, etc. and do a rolling motion forwards (the spine should ideally lose touch vertebra by vertebra). Slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Cable Kneeling Crunch
exercises.description: Grasp the cable attachment (rope) with both hands and hold it next to your temples. Kneel down facing or facing away from the cable stack with your torso upright and slightly hinged forward. Crunch down by rolling your spine inward, bringing your elbows toward your knees. Pause briefly, then slowly return under control to the starting position.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Vertical Leg Crunch
exercises.description: On your back, legs extended straight up, reach toward your toes with your hands and lift your shoulder blades off the ground and back.
exercises.author: krisbbb

exercises.name: Cycling
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Adjust your bicycle or stationary bike saddle height so that when the pedal is at the bottom of the stroke, your knee has a slight bend (about 25–35 degrees). Position the handlebars so you can grip them comfortably with relaxed shoulders and a neutral spine.

Execution:
1. Pedal in smooth, continuous circles with a steady cadence.
2. Apply force through the balls of your feet, pressing down and pulling through the rotation.
3. Maintain an even pace and adjust resistance according to your workout target.

Notes:
Keep your core stable to prevent your hips from rocking side-to-side in the saddle. Maintain regular, rhythmic breathing.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Deadbug
exercises.description: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and arms extended toward the ceiling. Press your lower back flat against the floor. Slowly lower one leg and tap the heel to the floor while keeping your lower back pressed to the floor. Return the knee to the starting position and repeat on the other side. To increase difficulty, lower the opposite arm and leg simultaneously.
exercises.author: Metin

exercises.name: Deadhang
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Grasp a pull-up bar or hangboard edge with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart. Hang freely with your arms extended and feet off the floor.

Execution:
1. Secure a firm grip around the bar.
2. You can perform either a passive hang (shoulders fully relaxed to decompress the spine) or an active hang (drawing shoulder blades slightly down and back to engage scapular stabilizers).
3. Hold the suspended position for the designated duration.

Notes:
Breathe steadily and keep your body still without swinging. Adjust difficulty by hanging from narrower edges, thicker bars, or adding weight.
exercises.author: 2dPREtEZP221u68Akf0JImv5L48

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell positioned over the middle of your feet (about 1 inch from your shins). Hinge at your hips and bend your knees until you can grasp the bar just outside your legs using an overhand or mixed grip. Keep your back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly ahead of the bar.

Execution:
1. Take a deep breath into your belly and brace your core. Push the floor away through your mid-foot and heels, extending your knees and hips simultaneously.
2. Keep the barbell in close contact with your shins and thighs as it rises.
3. Lock out by standing tall and squeezing your glutes, keeping a neutral spine without leaning back or hyperextending your lower back.
4. Return the barbell to the floor in a controlled manner by hinging at the hips first, then bending the knees once the bar clears them.

Notes:
Never round your spine under load. Keep your lats engaged to keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press Barbell
exercises.description: Lay down on a decline bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press Dumbbell
exercises.description: Take two dumbbells and sit on a decline bench, the feet are firmly on the floor, the head is resting the bench. Hold the weights next to the chest, at the height of your nipples and press them up till the arms are stretched. Let the weight slowly and controlled down.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
exercises.description:
Preparation
Stand on weight plate, bumper plate, or shallow elevated platform with loaded bar above feet. Squat down and grasp bar with shoulder width or slightly wider overhand or mixed grip.
Execution
Lift bar by extending hips and knees to full extension. Pull shoulders back at top of lift if rounded. Return weights to floor by bending hips back while allowing knees to bend forward, keeping back straight and knees pointed same direction as feet. Repeat.
Comments
Throughout lift, keep hips low, shoulders high, arms and back straight. Knees should point same direction as feet throughout movement. Keep bar close to body to improve mechanical leverage. Grip strength and strength endurance often limit ability to perform multiple reps at heavy resistances. Gym chalk, wrist straps, grip work, and mixed grip can be used to enhance grip. Mixed grip indicates one hand holding with overhand grip and other hand holding with underhand grip. Lever barbell jack can be used to lift barbell from floor for easier loading and unloading of weight plates.
Barbell Deficit Deadlift emphasizes building strength through lowest portion of Deadlift. Target muscle is exercised isometrically. Heavy barbell deadlifts significantly engages Latissmus Dorsi. See Barbell Deficit Deadlift under Gluteus Maximus. Also see Deadlift Analysis.
exercises.author: bobbyprince89

exercises.name: Diagonal Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
You sit at the bench press device, back slightly tilted to the back. The bar should be about 20 cm in front of you. Then you push the bar and take it back again, as you would with a bench press.
In this position you strain your chest muscles a lot less, which is nice if you want to train, but your chest hasn't recovered yet.
exercises.author: oboema

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.description: A dip is an upper-body strength exercise. Narrow, shoulder-width dips primarily train the triceps, with major synergists being the anterior deltoid, the pectoralis muscles (sternal, clavicular, and minor), and the rhomboid muscles of the back (in that order). Wide arm training places additional emphasis on the pectoral muscles, similar in respect to the way a wide grip bench press would focus more on the pectorals and less on the triceps.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Dips Between Two Benches
exercises.description: Put two benches so far appart, that you can hold onto one with your hands and are just able to reach the other with your feet. The legs stay during the exercise completely stretched. With your elbows facing back, bend them as much as you can. Push yourself up, but don't stretch out the arms.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
exercises.description: Sit on bench. Grasp dumbbell between feet. Place back of upper arm to inner thigh. Lean into leg to raise elbow slightly.
exercises.author: http://www.exrx.net/WeightExercises/Brachialis/DBC

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.description:
Grasp dumbbell with both hands at the sides of the upper plates. Hold dumbbell in front of chest, close to torso. Place feet about shoulderwide apart, keep knees slightly bent.
Squat down until thighs are parallel to floor. Keep back straight, bend and move hips backward to keep knees above feet. Return, keep knees slightly flexed. Repeat.
Keep bodyweight on heels and look ahead or slightly above to keep back straight.
exercises.author: ataraxie67

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
exercises.description:
Setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 45 to 60 degrees.
Starting Position: Sit back against the bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor with your palms facing forward (supinated grip).
The Curl: Keeping your upper arms stationary and shoulders pinned back against the bench, exhale and curl the weights upward toward your shoulders.
Peak Contraction: Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows do not swing forward.
The Descent: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining full control and feeling the stretch in the biceps.
exercises.author: ExRx

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lunges Standing
exercises.description: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides and perform alternating forward lunges.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lunges Walking
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands either on your hips or holding dumbbells at your sides.
The Stride: Take a wide step forward with your right leg.
The Descent: Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90-degree angles.
The Transition: Drive through your front heel to stand up, bringing your back foot forward to step directly into the next lunge.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbells on Scott Machine
exercises.description: Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arms supported on the pad. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, curl the weights by bending your elbows, then lower them under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Position one dumbbell over head with both hands under inner plate (heart shaped grip).
With elbows over head, lower forearm behind upper arm by flexing elbows. Flex wrists at bottom to avoid hitting dumbbell on back of neck. Raise dumbbell over head by extending elbows while hyperextending wrists. Return and repeat.
exercises.author: tuninx

exercises.name: Facepull
exercises.description:
Attach a rope to a pulley station set at about chest level.
Step back so you're supporting the weight with arms completely outstretched and assume a staggered (one foot forward) stance. Bend the knees slightly for a stable base.
Retract the scapulae (squeeze your partner's finger with your shoulder blades) and pull the center of the rope slightly up towards the face. A good cue is to think about pulling the ends of the rope apart, not just pulling back.
As you near your face, externally rotate so your knuckles are facing the ceiling.
Hold for one second at the top position and slowly lower.
exercises.author: abeworld

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description:
Lie on your back and lift both legs slightly off the floor, keeping them straight.
Alternately kick your legs up and down in a fluttering motion without letting your feet touch the floor.
Keep your core tight and your lower back firmly pressed against the floor throughout the movement.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: Fly With Cable
exercises.description: cable machine, two steps forward, straight back
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Fly With Dumbbells
exercises.description: Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description:
The exercise is the same as with a regular bench:
Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
exercises.description:
Hold the dumbbells and lie down on a flat bench in such a way that around 1/4 of your head is over the edge. Stretch arms straight up and then lean dumbbells away from your toes to a 10-20 degree angle. Keep upper arm at this angle throughout exercise. Dumbbells shall not be aimed at your head, but away over your head. This will maximise gain from exercise with load on triceps all the time.
Pay attention to your elbows and arms: only the triceps are doing the work, the rest of the arms should not move.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Skullcrusher EZ-Bar
exercises.description:
Hold the EZ-bar and lie down on a flat bench in such a way that around 1/4 of your head is over the edge. Stretch your arms with the bar and bend them so that the bar is lowered. Just before it touches your forehead, push it up.
Pay attention to your elbows and arms: only the triceps are doing the work, the rest of the arms should not move.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Front Raises with Plates
exercises.description:
The plate front raise is a variation of the dumbbell front raise where the lifter holds a weight plate between two hands, rather than using a dumbbell, barbell, or other weight. It can provide variety in a shoulder-focused muscle-building workout, or as part of an upper body or full-body circuit.

While standing straight, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended and locked with a slight bend at the elbows and the plate should be down near your waist in front of you as far as you can go. Tip: The arms will remain in this position throughout the exercise. This will be your starting position.
Slowly raise the plate as you exhale until it is a little above shoulder level. Hold the contraction for a second. As you inhale, slowly lower the plate back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
exercises.author: Marius

exercises.name: Front Raises
exercises.description:
To execute the exercise, the lifter stands with their feet shoulder width apart and weights or resistance handles held by their side with a pronated (overhand) grip.
The movement is to bring the arms up in front of the body to eye level and with only a slight bend in the elbow. This isolates the anterior deltoid muscle (front of the shoulder) and uses the anterior deltoid to lift the weight.
When lifting it is important to keep the body still so the anterior deltoid is fully utilised; if the weight cannot be lifted by standing still then it is too heavy and a lower weight is needed. It is important to keep a slight bend in the elbow when lifting as keeping the elbow locked will add stress to the elbow joint and could cause injury.
A neutral grip, similar to that used in the hammer curl, can also be used. With this variation the weight is again raised to eye level, but out to a 45 degree angle from the front of the body. This may be beneficial for those with shoulder injuries, particularly those related to the rotator cuff.
exercises.author: Manu, wikipedia

exercises.name: Front Squats
exercises.description: This variation of the squat trains the hamstrings and gluteus maximus. It also works the back extensors and abductors.
exercises.author: sistab2

exercises.name: Front pull wide
exercises.description: Sit or stand at a high cable pulley with a wide grip. Pull the handle toward your upper chest by drawing your elbows down, then return it under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Front Pull narrow
exercises.description: Sit or stand at a high cable pulley with a narrow grip. Pull the handle toward your upper chest by drawing your elbows down, then return it under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Full Sit-Out
exercises.description: (A) Get in high plank position on your hands and toes. (B) Shift your weight to your left hand as you turn your body to the right; bend your right leg behind you and extend your right arm up. Return to the center and repeat on the opposite side. Continue, alternating sides. Make it easier: Don’t raise your arm after you bend your leg behind you. Make it harder: Balance with your arm and leg extended for two counts.
exercises.author: http://www.realsimple.com/health/fitness-exercise/

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on you back with your hips and knees flexed, feet on the ground. From this position, raise your butt off of the ground to a height where your body makes a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. To make the exercise more intense, you can add weight by letting a barbell rest on your hips as you complete the motion, or you can put your feet on a slightly higher surface such as a step or a bench.
exercises.author: tdprice12

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.description:
Start: Hold dumbbells at your sides with palms facing your torso.
Curl: Lift the weights toward your shoulders while maintaining the neutral grip (like holding a hammer).
Squeeze: Contract the biceps at the top without moving your elbows forward.
Lower: Slowly return to the starting position with full control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Hammercurls on Cable
exercises.description:
Take a cable in your hands (palms parallel, point to each other), the body is straight. Bend the arms and bring the weight up with a fast movement. Without any pause bring it back down with a slow, controlled movement, but don't stretch completely your arms.
Don't swing your body during the exercise, the biceps should do all the work here. The elbows are at your side and don't move.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Hand Grip
exercises.description: chrome Hand Flex Grip to build up forearms muscles
exercises.author: vince63

exercises.name: Handstand Pushup
exercises.description: The handstand push-up (press-up) - also called the vertical push-up (press-up) or the inverted push-up (press-up) also called commandos- is a type of push-up exercise where the body is positioned in a handstand. For a true handstand, the exercise is performed free-standing, held in the air. To prepare the strength until one has built adequate balance, the feet are often placed against a wall, held by a partner, or secured in some other way from falling. Handstand pushups require significant strength, as well as balance and control if performed free-standing.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms straight. Keeping your core tight, raise your legs until they are parallel to the floor (or higher) with knees straight or slightly flexed, then lower them slowly under control.
exercises.author: robhoyt

exercises.name: Hercules Pillars
exercises.description: Grab two cables stand in the middle so both have tension and hold
exercises.author: GrosseHund

exercises.name: High Knee Jumps
exercises.description:
Start with legs slightly wider than shoulder width.
Drop into a bodyweight squat.
As you hit the bottom of the squat, explode upwards into a jump while simultaneously tucking your knees into your chest midflight. Remain tucked until the apex of your jump.
Land on both feet, making sure your knees are not locked so as to avoid excessive strain upon your joints. Collect yourself into the next rep as quickly but under control as possible.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: High Pull
exercises.description: Use a light barbell, perform explosive lift up starting from underneath knee cap level. Lift/raise explosively using hips, at shoulder level. Tempo: 2111
exercises.author: Mahoney

exercises.name: Hindu Squats
exercises.description:
Start with your feet shoulder width apart and arms slightly behind your back.
As you descend towards the floor, raise your heels off the ground, while keeping your back as vertical as possible.
Upon attaining the bottom position, touch the hands to the heels.
Then stand up ending with the heels on the ground, arms extended in front of the chest then rowing into the start position.
exercises.author: Vilhelmo

exercises.name: Lying Hip Raise
exercises.description: Lying down on your back, with your feet flat on the floor. Raise your hips up evenly as high as you can and hold for as long as you can.
exercises.author: James Mackay

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: The bar should go directly on your upper thigh, directly below your crotch. Your feet should be directly under your knees. Push your hips up so that you form a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Use a pad for comfort.
exercises.author: Bret Contreras

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
exercises.description: Get on a mat and lie on your back. Contract your abs, stretch your arms and legs and raise them (your head and shoulders are also be raised). Make sure your lower back remains in contact with the mat.
exercises.author: Behrooz

exercises.name: Hyperextensions
exercises.description: Lie on the hyperextension pillow with your navel at the front edge, allowing your upper body to hang freely. Tighten all your back muscles and raise your torso until you're horizontal, but no higher. Lower yourself slowly, maintaining a steady flow of muscles.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: Use inclined bench. Hold dumbbells straight out to your sides, elbows slightly bent. Bring arms together above you, keeping angle of elbows fixed.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Row
exercises.description:
Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.
exercises.author: cal.zabel

exercises.name: Decline Swiss Ball Plank with Alternating Toe Tap
exercises.description:
Perform the plank with legs elevated, feet on a gymball. Once stabilised, slowly move one foot sideways off the ball, then make it touch the floor, then come back to starting position. Alternate with the other foot.
This is a core exercise.
exercises.author: Mahoney

exercises.name: Isometric Wipers
exercises.description:
Assume push-up position, with hands slightly wider than shoulder width.
Shift body weight as far as possible to one side, allowing the elbow on that side to flex.
Reverse the motion, moving completely over to the other side.
Return to the starting position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
exercises.author: cal.zabel

exercises.name: Jogging
exercises.description: Get your shoes on, go outside and start running at a moderate pace.
exercises.author: Papazit

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.description: A jumping jack or star jump, also called side-straddle hop in the US military, is a physical jumping exercise performed by jumping to a position with the legs spread wide and the hands going overhead, sometimes in a clap, and then returning to a position with the feet together and the arms at the sides
exercises.author: student1234

exercises.name: Cable Cross-over
exercises.description: Begin with cables at about shoulder height, one in each hand. Take a step forward so that one foot is in front of the other, for stability, and so that there is tension on the cables. Bring hands together in front of you. Try to make your hands overlap (so that the cables cross) a few inches.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swings
exercises.description:
Hold the kettlebell securely in both hands. Keep your back flat throughout the move, avoiding any rounding of the spine.Keeping your knees "soft", hinge your hips backwards, letting the kettlebell swing between your knees.
You want to bend from the hips as far as you can without letting your back round forwards. Then, snap your hips forwards quickly and standing up straight, locking your body in an upright posture.
The speed you do this will cause your arms and the kettlebell to swing up in front of you. Don't try to lift the kettlebell with your arms. The snapping forwards of your hips will cause the kettlebell to swing forwards through momentum. Depending on the weight of the kettlebell and the speed of your hip movement, your arms will swing up to about shoulder height. At the top of this swing, let your hips hinge backwards again as the kettlebell swings back down to between your legs and the start of the next repetition.
exercises.author: J120290,cerin

exercises.name: Squats on Multipress
exercises.description: Set the bar of a Smith machine at shoulder height and stand with a narrow stance beneath it. Lower into a squat, then press through your feet to stand back up.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Landmine press
exercises.description: Hold the free end of a barbell fixed in a landmine with one hand. Press it away from your body without moving it toward your midline, keeping your body straight and braced.
exercises.author: Torsten Linnecke

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: This exercise works the deltoid muscle of the shoulder. The movement starts with the arms straight, and the hands holding weights at the sides or in front of the body. Body is in a slight forward-leaning position with hips and knees bent a little. Arms are kept straight or slightly bent, and raised through an arc of movement in the coronal plane that terminates when the hands are at approximately shoulder height. Weights are lowered to the starting position, completing one rep. When using a cable machine the individual stands with the coronal plane in line with the pulley, which is at or near the ground.[9] The exercise can be completed one shoulder at a time (with the other hand used to stabilize the body against the weight moved), or with both hands simultaneously if two parallel pulleys are available.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Set cable at waist height, start with arm across your belly and raise hand up and out to the side, one arm at a time.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Lateral-to-Front Raises
exercises.description:
- Perform a lateral raise, pausing at the top of the lift at shoulder height.
- Instead of lowering the weight, bring the dumbbells together in front of your body with straight arms, ending in the top position of a front raise.
- Lower the dumbbells down in front of your thighs as in a front raise.
- Reverse the movement: Raise the dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height, open your arms out to the sides into the top position of a lateral raise, and lower the weights back to your sides. This completes one repetition.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: Lat Pull Down (Leaning Back)
exercises.description: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width. Lean your torso back slightly (approximately 20–30 degrees) and pull the bar down toward your upper chest, focusing on driving your elbows down and squeezing your lats. Return the bar upward under control to full extension.
exercises.author: drthurlow

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Straight Back)
exercises.description: The lat pull down is an exercise used to build the muscles of the back. While the exercise will primarily target the lats, you will also notice a fair amount of bicep and middle back activation.
exercises.author: drthurlow

exercises.name: Leg Curl
exercises.description: The leg curl, also known as the hamstring curl, is an isolation exercise that targets the hamstring muscles. The exercise involves flexing the lower leg against resistance towards the buttocks. Other exercises that can be used to strengthen the hamstrings are the glute-ham raise and the deadlift.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Leg Curls (laying)
exercises.description: Lay on a bench and put your calves behind the leg holder (better if they are hold on around the lower calves). Hold a grip on the bars to make sure the body is firmly in place. Bend your legs bringing the weight up, go slowly back. During the exercise the body should not move, all work is done by the legs.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Leg Curls (sitting)
exercises.description: Sit in the leg curl machine and position your lower legs behind the pad. Bend your knees to pull the pad down, then return to the starting position under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Leg Curls (standing)
exercises.description: Perform the movement one leg at a time in the standing leg curl machine. Place your lower leg behind the pad, bend the knee until it reaches a right angle, then lower the weight under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: The leg extension is a resistance weight training exercise that targets the quadriceps muscle in the legs. The exercise is done using a machine called the Leg Extension Machine. There are various manufacturers of these machines and each one is slightly different. Most gym and weight rooms will have the machine in their facility. The leg extension is an isolated exercise targeting one specific muscle group, the quadriceps. It should not be considered as a total leg workout, such as the squat or deadlift. The exercise consists of bending the leg at the knee and extending the legs, then lowering them back to the original position.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: The leg press is a weight training exercise in which the individual pushes a weight or resistance away from them using their legs.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Narrow Stance Leg Press
exercises.description:
Sit on the leg press machine with your back firmly against the pad. Place your feet on the platform in a narrow stance (a few inches apart, roughly hip-width or narrower) with toes pointing slightly outward or forward.
Release the safety bars and lower the sled under control until your knees bend to approximately 90 degrees. Press through your entire foot to push the platform back up, without locking out your knees at the top.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Wide Stance Leg Press
exercises.description:
Sit on the leg press machine with your back firmly against the pad. Place your feet high and wide on the platform, wider than shoulder-width, with your toes pointed slightly outward.
Release the safety bars and lower the sled under control until your knees reach approximately a 90-degree angle, tracking in line with your toes. Drive through your heels and midfoot to return to the starting position without locking your knees.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Leg Press on Hackenschmidt Machine
exercises.description: Sit in the Hackenschmidt machine with your shoulders against the pads and your feet about shoulder-width apart. Lower into the squat, then press back up without fully locking your knees.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: The leg raise is a strength training exercise which targets the iliopsoas (the anterior hip flexors). Because the abdominal muscles are used isometrically to stabilize the body during the motion, leg raises are also often used to strengthen the rectus abdominis muscle and the internal and external oblique muscles.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: Lay down on a bench and hold onto the recliner with your hands to keep you stable. Hold your legs straight and lift them till they make an angle of about 45°. Make a short pause of 1 sec. and go slowly down to the initial position. To increase the intensity you can make a longer pause of 7 sec. every 5th time.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dip Station Leg Raise
exercises.description: Put your forearms on the pads on the leg raise machine, the body is hanging freely. Lift now your legs with a fast movement as high as you can, make a short pause of 1sec at the top, and bring them down again. Make sure that during the exercise your body does not swing, only the legs should move.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Leverage Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: Be sure to adjust seat height so that the handles are towards the bottom of your pectorals.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Leverage Machine Iso Row
exercises.description: Adjust seat height so that the handles are at the bottom of your pectorals or just below.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Hanging L-Sit Hold
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar and raise your legs straight until there is a 90-degree angle between legs and torso (L-shape). Hold this position.
exercises.author: bizyguy

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.description:
Start: Get into a high plank position. Place your hands close together directly beneath your chest so that your thumbs and index fingers form a diamond shape.
Lower: Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows tucked close to your ribs and your core braced.
Push: Press firmly through your palms to return to full arm extension.
exercises.author: notdefine

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip)
exercises.description: Sit down, put your feet on the supporting points and grab the bar with a wide grip. Pull the weight with a rapid movement towards your belly button, not upper. Keep your arms and elbows during the movement close to your body. Your shoulders are pulled together. Let the weight slowly down till your arms are completely stretched.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (Narrow Grip)
exercises.description:
The exercise is the same as the regular long pulley, but with a narrow grip:
Sit down, put your feet on the supporting points and grab the handle with a narrow grip. Pull the weight with a rapid movement towards your belly button, not upper. Keep your arms and elbows during the movement close to your body. Your shoulders are pulled together. Let the weight slowly down till your arms are completely stretched.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Low Box Squat - Wide Stance
exercises.description: Unrack the bar and set your stance wide, beyond your hips. Push your hips back and sit down to a box that takes you below parallel. Sit completely down, do not touch and go. Then explosively stand up. Stay tight in your upper back and torso throughout the movement.
exercises.author: taylorbarbell

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Shoulder Rotation
exercises.description: Lie on your side on a mat, holding a light dumbbell in your top hand. Keep your top elbow bent at a 90-degree angle and pressed lightly against your side/waist. Rotate your forearm upward toward the ceiling against gravity, engaging the infraspinatus and teres minor, then lower slowly under control. Do not let your body roll backward.
exercises.author: Trix

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Military Press
exercises.description: Stand tall holding an EZ-curl bar at shoulder level in front of your upper chest with an overhand grip. Brace your core and press the bar vertically overhead until your arms are fully extended. Lower the bar smoothly under control back to your upper chest and repeat.
exercises.author: mbozi1

exercises.name: Muscle-Up
exercises.description:
From a dead hang on a pull-up bar, pull your body up explosively in an arcing motion. As your chest clears the bar, lean your torso forward over the bar and roll your wrists and forearms on top of the bar (the transition). Press through your palms and extend your elbows to push your body up until your arms are fully locked out and the bar is at waist level.
Lower yourself back down under control through the dip and pull-up phases to the starting dead hang. Advanced athletes perform this strictly without a kip, while developing athletes often use a moderate kip for momentum.
exercises.author: arson

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.description: Sit yourself on the decline bench and fix your legs. Cross your arms over the chest and bring with a rolling movement your upper body up, go now without a pause and with a slow movement down again. Don't let your head move during the exercise.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Overhand Cable Curl
exercises.description: Stand facing a cable pulley adjusted to shoulder or chest height. Grasp the attachment with an overhand (pronated) grip. Keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor, curl the attachment in toward your face or upper chest, contracting the brachioradialis and forearm muscles. Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position under tension.
exercises.author: ThisGirl0819

exercises.name: Overhead Squat
exercises.description: The barbell is held overhead in a wide-arm snatch grip; however, it is also possible to use a closer grip if balance allows.
exercises.author: geraldbaeck

exercises.name: Pause Bench
exercises.description: Lower the bar to your chest and pause (but do not rest) there for 2 seconds. Press back up. use the same weight you would on bench press, but perform only single reps. Total the number of reps you did in one set of bench press (if you did 3 sets of 8 do 8 sinlge pause bench reps.
exercises.author: Mens Fitness

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.description:
A barbell back exercise performed from a bent-over stance with your torso parallel to the ground. The barbell starts at rest on the floor for every repetition.
Grip the barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip, brace your core, and pull the bar explosively to your lower chest or upper abdomen without altering your hip angle. Lower the bar completely back to the floor before starting the next rep.
exercises.author: Nallitnas

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Get into a downward-facing dog / pike position with your hands shoulder-width apart, hips raised high, and body forming an inverted V-shape.
Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head forward toward the floor between or slightly ahead of your hands.
2. Press firmly through your palms to push yourself back up to the starting pike position.
3. Keep your core braced and legs as straight as possible throughout. Feet can optionally be elevated on a bench or box for increased difficulty.
exercises.author: Nash

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.description:
Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointed forward, and chest tall.
Extend your leg straight out; extend both arms in front of you, at shoulder level. Brace your core and look straight ahead.
Slowly squat down.
(optional) pause at the bottom.

Keep your (free) leg and arms extended for the whole duration.
exercises.author: minifigmaster125

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description:
Get into a position on the floor supporting your weight on your forearms and toes. Arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
Keep your body straight at all times and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty an arm or leg can be raised while performing this exercise.
exercises.author: YYCfit / BFad07

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
exercises.description:
Place an EZ-curl bar on the rest cradles in front of the preacher bench. Lean over the bench and grasp the inner angled grips with an underhand (supinated) grip. Sit down firmly on the seat with your triceps resting flush against the slanted pad and your chest pressed comfortably against it.
Lower the bar slowly under control until your elbows are fully extended without hyperextending. Curl the weight upward by contracting your biceps, stopping just short of vertical to maintain tension. Repeat.
exercises.author: cgoob883

exercises.name: Prone Scapular Retraction - Arms at Side
exercises.description:
Lying on stomach with head on towel.
Stretch arms straight out to your sides.
Slowly lift your arms, pulling your shoulderblades together, hold for 3 seconds.
exercises.author: donaddon

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: Grab the pull up bar with a wide grip, the body is hanging freely. Keep your chest out and pull yourself up till your chin reaches the bar or it touches your neck, if you want to pull behind you. Go with a slow and controlled movement down, always keeping the chest out.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Assisted Machine Pull-Up
exercises.description:
Adjust the counterweight on the assisted pull-up machine to provide the desired assistance. Place your knees or feet on the pad and grip the overhead handles with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull yourself upward until your chin clears the bar, focusing on driving your elbows down and back. Lower your body slowly under control until your arms are fully extended, and repeat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push Press
exercises.description: Clean two dumbbells to shoulder height with palms facing in (neutral grip) or slightly forward. Take a breath and brace your core. Dip slightly at the knees and hips, then explosively extend your legs and drive through your heels to help propel the dumbbells overhead to full arm extension. Lower the weights under control back to your shoulders and repeat.
exercises.author: sistab2

exercises.name: Rack Deadlift
exercises.description:
A deadlift variation performed from safety pins in a power rack or Smith machine, typically with the barbell set just below or at knee level.
Stand with a hip-width stance, hinge at your hips, and grip the bar just outside your legs. Pull by extending your hips and knees, driving through your heels and squeezing your glutes at lockout. Lower the bar under control back onto the pins. This exercise emphasizes the upper and lower back as well as the glutes.
exercises.author: Mahoney

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise
exercises.description: Sit on the end of a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and a pair of dumbbells. Hinge forward at your hips, resting your torso close to your thighs. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, squeezing your rear deltoids. Lower the weights slowly under control.
exercises.author: YYCfit

exercises.name: Renegade Row
exercises.description: Get into a high plank or push-up position with your hands gripping a pair of hex dumbbells resting on the floor. Spread your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width for stability. Perform one push-up, then row one dumbbell upward by driving your elbow toward your ribcage while keeping your hips square. Lower the dumbbell under control, perform another push-up, and row with the opposite arm to complete one repetition.
exercises.author: fletchgraham

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Reverse Curl
exercises.description:
Stand upright holding an EZ-curl bar with a shoulder-width overhand (pronated) grip, palms facing down. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso.
Curl the bar upward toward your chest by flexing your elbows, emphasizing the brachialis and brachioradialis in your forearms. Squeeze at the top and lower the weight slowly under control to full extension.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.description: The reverse-grip barbell curl is a variation on the biceps curl where the palms face downward. The switch from an underhand to an overhand grip brings the forearm and brachialis muscles more into the exercise.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Bench Press
exercises.description:
Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Grip the barbell with a reverse (supinated/underhand) grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, keeping wrists aligned.
Unrack the bar and lower it under control to your lower chest while keeping your elbows tucked at a comfortable angle. Press the bar upward to full arm extension, strongly engaging the upper chest (clavicular head) and triceps.
exercises.author: bl0sh

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.description:
Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight out in front of you. Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing forward toward your toes.
Press down through your palms and heels to lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your glutes, hamstrings, and upper back, keeping your chest lifted and hips high. Hold this position statically.
exercises.author: spacetowaste

exercises.name: Ring Dips
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Support yourself on the gymnastics rings with fully extended arms. Keep your core tight, body stable, and slightly turn the rings outward (support hold).
Execution: Lower your body in a controlled manner by bending your elbows until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows (roughly a 90-degree bend), keeping the rings close to your sides.
Return: Press powerfully back up to the starting position until your arms are fully extended.
Cues: Actively stabilize the rings throughout the entire range of motion to prevent them from drifting outward.
exercises.author: Nash

exercises.name: Roman Chair Crunch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Position yourself on the Roman chair with your feet securely locked under the roller pads and your torso aligned.
Execution: Flex your torso forward by contracting your abdominal muscles. Avoid coming all the way up to vertical or lying flat back to keep continuous tension on the abs.
Return: Return in a controlled motion to the starting position without hyperextending the lower back.
exercises.author: MaddieBeasley

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip in front of your thighs. Keep your shoulders back and down with a tight core.
Execution: Push your hips backward and hinge forward at the hips, maintaining a flat back and a slight, fixed bend in your knees. Lower the barbell close along your thighs and shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Return: Drive your hips forward to return to the fully upright position, contracting your glutes and hamstrings powerfully at the top.
Cues: Keep the bar close to your body at all times and avoid rounding your spine. The movement is a pure hip hinge, not a squat.
exercises.author: pjwirth

exercises.name: Row
exercises.description: In strength training, rowing (or a row, usually preceded by a qualifying adjective — for instance a seated row) is an exercise where the purpose is to strengthen the muscles that draw the rower's arms toward the body (latissimus dorsi) as well as those that retract the scapulae (trapezius and rhomboids) and those that support the spine (erector spinae). When done on a rowing machine, rowing also exercises muscles that extend and support the legs (quadriceps and thigh muscles). In all cases, the abdominal and lower back muscles must be used in order to support the body and prevent back injury.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Barbell Row on Bench
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie face down on a flat elevated bench. Grasp the barbell placed beneath the bench with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Execution: Pull the barbell upward toward your torso by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return: Lower the barbell under control back to the fully extended starting position.
Cues: The bench supports your torso, eliminating spinal load and allowing pure isolation of the latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and upper back.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (Wide Grip)
exercises.description:
The execution of this exercise is very similar to the regular bent over rowing, only that the bar is fixed here.
Grab the barbell with a wide grip (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise. Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Front Wood Chop
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. Extend your arms straight overhead (optionally holding a towel or light ball with light tension).
Execution: Extend your spine and shoulders upward and slightly back while simultaneously lifting one leg backward, contracting your erector spinae and gluteus maximus.
Return: Lower your leg under control back to the floor and alternate legs with each repetition.
Cues: Focus on spinal extension and balance, maintaining core stability throughout without overarching the lumbar spine.
exercises.author: Konsumopfer

exercises.name: Run
exercises.description: Running or jogging outdoors on a track, road, or trail at a steady or varied pace to develop cardiovascular fitness and endurance.
exercises.author: BeLikeWater

exercises.name: Run - Interval Training
exercises.description: Interval running training alternating between high-intensity efforts (such as hill repeats, fartlek, or track sprints) and active recovery intervals (jogging or walking) to boost aerobic and anaerobic capacity.
exercises.author: BeLikeWater

exercises.name: Treadmill Running
exercises.description: Running on a treadmill is an effective cardio exercise that elevates heart rate and trains endurance, primarily working the calf, thigh, and gluteal muscles.
exercises.author: foguinho.peruca

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press - Dumbbell
exercises.description:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.


Bench Adjustment and Preparation: Set the bench to an incline of between 30 and 45 degrees (an incline greater than 45° will place too much strain on the shoulders and reduce the stimulus to the chest). Sit down with a dumbbell on each thigh.


Starting position: Lean back, resting your back against the bench, while using your knees one after the other to push the dumbbells upward to shoulder height.


Anatomical Stabilization: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your scapulas (bring your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench) to protect your shoulders and stabilize the load.


Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells slowly and in a controlled manner toward the upper part of your chest. Your elbows should not splay out to the sides (90°); maintain a safe angle of about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.


Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the dumbbells vertically upward as you exhale. Follow a slightly converging path (without letting them touch at the top). Stop the movement just before locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension in the upper pectoral.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press - Barbell
exercises.description: Sit on the incline bench with your feet firmly on the floor for stability and your head resting on the bench. Unrack the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and press it upward. Lower the barbell until it briefly touches your chest, then press the weight back up. Perform slowly (tempo: 4010).
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Set an incline bench to 30–45 degrees inside the Smith machine. Sit down with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unhook the safety latches.
Execution: Lower the bar smoothly until it gently touches your upper chest.
Return: Press the bar upward by engaging your upper pectorals until your arms are extended without locking the elbows.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit down on the shoulder press machine and adjust the seat height so that the handles align with your shoulders. Keep your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Execution: Press the handles upward overhead in a controlled motion until your arms are extended without locking your elbows.
Return: Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position at shoulder level.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Scissors
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your legs extended and hands supporting your lower back or by your sides. Lift your legs slightly off the floor. Scissor your legs horizontally or vertically by crossing one leg over the other in an alternating rhythm, keeping your core engaged and your lower back pressed to the floor throughout the movement.
exercises.author: vkylamba

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Press
exercises.description: Sit down on a bench (better with back support). Take a dumbbell firmly with both hands and hold it with extended arms over your head. With your palms facing upward and holding the weight of the dumbbell, slowly lower the weight behind your head.
exercises.author: richmr2174

exercises.name: Roman Chair Side Bends
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Position yourself sideways on a Roman chair or 45-degree hyperextension bench, with your hip resting on the pad and feet securely anchored.
Execution: Lower your torso sideways toward the floor until your body is roughly parallel to the ground or you feel a stretch in the obliques.
Return: Contract your upper obliques to raise your torso back to the aligned starting position.
Cues: Keep your hands across your chest or behind your head, and avoid rotating your torso forward or backward.
exercises.author: klabautermann

exercises.name: Shotgun Row
exercises.description:
Attach a single handle to a low cable.
After selecting the correct weight, stand a couple feet back with a wide-split stance. Your arm should be extended and your shoulder forward. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by retracting the shoulder and flexing the elbow. As you pull, supinate the wrist, turning the palm upward as you go.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
exercises.author: cal.zabel

exercises.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Sit on a bench, the back rest should be almost vertical. Take a barbell with a shoulder wide grip and bring it up to chest height. Press the weight up, but don't stretch the arms completely. Go slowly down and repeat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Sit on a bench, the back rest should be almost vertical. Take two dumbbells and bring them up to shoulder height, the palms and the elbows point during the whole exercise to the front. Press the weights up, at the highest point they come very near but don't touch. Go slowly down and repeat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
