The exercise is basically the same as with a free barbell:
Sit on a bench, the back rest should be almost vertical. Take a bar with a shoulder wide grip and bring it down to chest height. Press the weight up, but don't stretch the arms completely. Go slowly down and repeat.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrug
exercises.description: The shoulder shrug (usually called simply the shrug) is an exercise in weight training used to develop the upper trapezius muscle. The lifter stands erect, hands about shoulder width apart, and raises the shoulders as high as possible, and then lowers them, while not bending the elbows, or moving the body at all. The lifter may not have as large a range of motion as in a normal shrug done for active flexibility. It is usually considered good form if the slope of the shoulders is horizontal in the elevated position.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.description:
Take a barbell and stand with a straight body, the arms are hanging freely in front of you. Lift from this position the shoulders as high as you can, but don't bend the arms during the movement. On the highest point, make a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds before returning slowly to the initial position.
When training with a higher weight, make sure that you still do the whole movement!
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.description:
Stand with straight body, the hands are hanging freely on the side and hold each a dumbbell. Lift from this position the shoulders as high as you can, but don't bend the arms during the movement. On the highest point, make a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds before returning slowly to the initial position.
When training with a higher weight, make sure that you still do the whole movement!
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shrug
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart in front of the Smith machine bar. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, arms hanging straight down.
Execution: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears without bending your elbows. Hold the peak contraction at the top for 1-2 seconds.
Return: Lower your shoulders slowly back to the starting position under control.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Side Crunch
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in one hand at your side. Slowly bend your torso sideways toward that knee, then pull back up to an upright position using your obliques. Repeat and switch sides.
exercises.author: kwrindy

exercises.name: Side Dumbbell Trunk Flexion
exercises.description: AKA dumbbell side bends. Stand in line with the hips with slightly bent knees, maintain the natural curvature of the spine, hand stretched by the body, grip the dumbbell with one hand. Make slow and controlled torso side flexions till you reach the angle of approximately 45°.
exercises.author: GiglioRosso

exercises.name: Side-lying External Rotation
exercises.description:
With a weight in one hand, lie on your side opposite the weight. Keep your knees slightly bent. Hold your elbow against your side, and extend your forearm straight ahead of you. While continuing to hold your elbow against your side, rotate your forearm 90 degrees upwards.
It is helpful to place a towel under your armpit to help with the form on this exercise. Placing a support under your head for the duration of the exercise is also a good idea.
exercises.author: apeschel

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on your side with your legs extended and your forearm directly under your shoulder, perpendicular to your body.
Execution: Contract your obliques and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to ankles.
Return / Hold: Hold this rigid position for the designated duration, keeping your hips elevated without sagging.
exercises.author: http://www.bodybuilding.com/

exercises.name: Side to Side Push Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin in a high plank / push-up position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and body forming a straight line.
Execution: Lower your chest toward one hand as you bend your elbows, shifting the majority of your body weight to that side.
Return: Push powerfully back to the starting position and repeat, shifting toward the opposite side on the next repetition.
exercises.author: nate303303

exercises.name: Single-arm Preacher Curl
exercises.description: Sit on the preacher curl bench and perform a bicep curl with a dumbbell in one hand. Your other hand can be at rest, or beneath your curling arm's elbow.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Sitting Calf Raises
exercises.description: Sit on a bench for calf raises and check that the feet are half free and that you can completely stretch the calf muscles down. Pull your calves up, going as far (up) as you can. Make at the highest point a short pause of 1 or 2 seconds and go down.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Bench-Elevated Sit-up
exercises.description: Sit on a mat, your calves are resting on a bench, the knees make a right angle. Hold your hands behind your neck. Go now up with a rolling movement of your back, you should feel how the individual vertebrae lose contact with the mat. At the highest point, contract your abs as much as you can and hold there for 2 sec. Go now down, unrolling your back.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Skipping - Standard
exercises.description:
Do a single, double footed jump for each swing of the rope.
Work on a smooth, rhythmical movement, bouncing lightly on the balls of your feet.
exercises.author: Cerin

exercises.name: Smith Machine Close-grip Bench Press
exercises.description: Perform a standard bench press on the smith machine, but have your hands on the bar about shoulder width apart, and keep your elbows close to your body.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Snatch
exercises.description: Stand with your feet at hip width and your shins against the bar. Grasp the bar at double shoulder width and, keeping your lower back flat, drive your heels into the floor to begin lifting the bar. When it's above your knees, explosively extend your hips and shrug your shoulders. Let the momentum carry the weight overhead.
exercises.author: Mens Fitness

exercises.name: Speed Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Set up at a barbell loaded to approximately 50–70% of your 1RM, adopting your standard deadlift stance with a rigid, braced spine.
Execution: Pull the barbell off the floor with maximal acceleration and explosive bar speed, driving forcefully through your hips and legs to lockout.
Return: Return the barbell quickly and under control to the floor.
Cues: Focus on maximal velocity and intent. Rest intervals are intentionally brief (typically under 60 seconds) to train explosive power and rate of force development.
exercises.author: MrSteele

exercises.name: Sprinter Sit-up
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your legs straight and arms at your sides, keeping your elbows bent at 90 degrees. As you sit up, twist your upper body to the right and bring your left knee toward your right elbow while you swing your left arm back. Lower your body to the starting position, and repeat to your right. That's 1 rep.
exercises.author: djblitzd

exercises.name: Squat Jumps
exercises.description: Jump explosively from a wide stance and land in a narrow stance, alternating between wide and narrow foot positions.
exercises.author: OGhTebfCxhexZXuf35mUxV9C--A

exercises.name: Squats
exercises.description: Place a barbell in a rack just below shoulder-height. Dip under the bar to put it behind the neck across the top of the back, and grip the bar with the hands wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift the chest up and squeeze the shoulder blades together to keep the straight back throughout the entire movement. Stand up to bring the bar off the rack and step backwards, then place the feet so that they are a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Sit back into hips and keep the back straight and the chest up, squatting down so the hips are below the knees. From the bottom of the squat, press feet into the ground and push hips forward to return to the top of the standing position.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Squat Thrust
exercises.description: The burpee, or squat thrust, is a full body exercise used in strength training and as an aerobic exercise. The basic movement is performed in four steps and known as a four-count burpee: Begin in a standing position. Move into a squat position with your hands on the ground. (count 1) Kick your feet back into a plank position, while keeping your arms extended. (count 2) Immediately return your feet into squat position. (count 3) Stand up from the squat position (count 4)
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Standing Bicep Curl
exercises.description: Stand holding dumbbells at shoulder width apart. Face forearm upward and keep upper arm still while raising each dumbbell up to your shoulder.
exercises.author: BFad07

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.description: Get onto the calf raises machine, you should able to completely push your calves down. Stand straight, don't make a hollow back and don't bend your legs. Pull yourself up as high as you can. Make a small pause of 1 - 2 seconds and go slowly down.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Standing Wrist Roller
exercises.description: Grab a wrist roller tool with both hands while standing with your feet about shoulder width apart. If your gym does not have a wrist roller tool, you can easily put one together. All you need is a 5 or 10 pound weight plate, a strong thin rope about 3 feet long and a 6-8 inch stick or bar. Securely fasten the rope to the middle of the bar/stick and tie the other end of the rope to the weight plate. To begin this exercise, grab the bar/stick with both hands using an overhand grip. Extend both arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor. Next, roll the weight up from the floor by rapidly twisting the bar/stick with your hands and wrists. Once the weight reaches the top, slowly lower the plate back to the floor by reversing the motion of your hands and wrists. Repeat (if you can!).
exercises.author: pwiltrout

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Adjust the stationary bike seat height so that your knees have a slight bend (around 25–30 degrees) at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Execution: Pedal at a steady cadence and adjust the resistance to match your training intensity.
Cues: Keep your core lightly engaged, back neutral, and hands comfortably resting on the handlebars without leaning heavily.
exercises.author: intelman

exercises.name: Stiff-legged Deadlifts
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width overhand grip. Keep your knees nearly straight, with only a very slight unlock to protect the joints.
Execution: Hinge forward at the hips while pushing your glutes backward, keeping your back completely flat and neutral. Lower the barbell close to your legs until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Return: Contract your hamstrings and glutes powerfully to return to the fully upright position.
Cues: Do not allow your lower back to round. The knees remain fixed and nearly straight throughout the movement.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown with Straight Bar
exercises.description: Use the straight bar attachment on a high pulley. Grasp the two ends of the bar with your palms facing downward and your arms straight out in front of you. Pull your hands down towards your hips, while keeping your arms straight, then raise them back up to the starting position.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown with Rope
exercises.description: Use the rope attachment on a high pulley. Grasp the two ends of the rope with your arms straight out in front of you. Pull your hands down towards your hips, while keeping your arms straight, then raise them back up to the starting position.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description:
Begin with a bar loaded on the ground. Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip. Relax the shoulders, which in effect lengthens your arms.
Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.
exercises.author: magdy

exercises.name: Sumo Squats
exercises.description:
Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders, with your toes pointed out at a 45-degree angle.
While keeping your back straight, descend slowly by bending at the knees and hips as if you are sitting down (squatting).
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Return to the starting position by pressing upwards and extending your legs while maintaining an equal distribution of weight on your forefoot and heel.
exercises.author: sophialj

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description:
Lie flat on your stomach with your legs straight and arms extended overhead on the floor.
Simultaneously raise your arms, chest, and thighs a few inches off the floor by contracting your lower back, glutes, and upper back muscles.
Hold the peak contraction for 2 to 5 seconds while breathing smoothly, then slowly lower back down under control.
exercises.author: baldurmen

exercises.name: Thruster
exercises.description:
- Hold a barbell in the front-rack position across the front of your shoulders, standing with feet shoulder-width apart.
- Descend into a deep front squat until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
- Drive explosively up through your heels, using the momentum from your legs to push the barbell overhead in one fluid motion.
- Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders and transition smoothly into the next squat repetition.
exercises.author: BeLikeWater

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.description:
Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso. Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor. Make sure to keep your head up. Your upper arms should be close to your torso and parallel to the floor. Your forearms should be pointed towards the floor as you hold the weights. There should be a 90-degree angle formed between your forearm and upper arm. This is your starting position.
Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and use your triceps to lift the weights until the arm is fully extended. Focus on moving the forearm.
After a brief pause at the top contraction, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

Variations: This exercise can be executed also one arm at a time much like the one arm rows are performed.
Also, if you like the one arm variety, you can use a low pulley handle instead of a dumbbell for better peak contraction. In this case, the palms should be facing up (supinated grip) as opposed to the torso (neutral grip).
exercises.author: http://www.bodybuilding.com/

exercises.name: Cable Rope Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Grab the rope attachment on the cable, stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your back straight and lean forward a little. Push the rope down, making sure the elbows don't move during the exercise. Rotate your hands outwards at the very end and return to the initial position in a controlled manner.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Cable Straight-Bar Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Grab the bar, stand with your feet shoulder wide, keep your back straight and lean forward a little. Push the bar down, making sure the elbows don't move during the exercise. Without pause go back to the initial position.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Machine Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
- Sit at the triceps machine and adjust the seat height so that your elbows align with the machine's pivot point.
- Grip the handles firmly and rest your upper arms securely on the support pad.
- Press the handles downward by extending your elbows, fully contracting your triceps without aggressively locking your joints.
- Slowly return the weight to the starting position under control, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Trunk Rotation With Cable
exercises.description:
- Stand or sit perpendicular to the cable pulley set at chest height, holding the handle with both hands.
- Keep your arms slightly bent and rotate your torso smoothly across your body, engaging your obliques.
- Keep your hips and pelvis stable facing forward, then slowly return to the starting position under control.
exercises.author: Robertcoop

exercises.name: TRX Row
exercises.description:
- Grasp the suspension trainer handles with a neutral grip and lean back with your arms fully extended.
- Maintain a straight body alignment from head to heels by bracing your core and glutes.
- Pull your chest up toward the handles by driving your elbows backward and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
- Lower yourself back down under control until your arms are fully extended.
exercises.author: Skadi

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.description: Starting on back, move to the standing position holding a kettlebell overhead in one hand. Switch hands between reps.
exercises.author: dookie1481

exercises.name: Power Clean
exercises.description:
- Stand over the barbell with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width using a hook grip.
- Keep your back flat and chest lifted as you initiate the first pull by extending your knees and hips smoothly to knee level.
- Explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) while shrugging and pulling the bar upward close to your torso.
- Drop quickly into a partial squat, rotating your elbows forward to catch the bar across your front deltoids (front-rack position), then stand tall.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
- Sit at the lat pulldown station and adjust the thigh pads to secure your lower body firmly.
- Grip the bar with an underhand (supinated) grip at shoulder width or slightly narrower.
- Pull the bar smoothly down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, contracting your lats and biceps.
- Slowly extend your arms back to the top position under full control while maintaining tension in your back.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description:
- Unrack the barbell from shoulder height with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, resting it on your anterior deltoids.
- Brace your core and glutes, tilt your head slightly back, and press the bar vertically in a straight path.
- As the bar passes your forehead, bring your head slightly forward and lock out your arms overhead over midfoot.
- Lower the barbell under control back to your upper chest and shoulders.
exercises.author: Vazco

exercises.name: Upper External Oblique
exercises.description:
- Assume a side plank position or hang firmly from a pull-up bar with core engaged.
- Perform a controlled lateral torso flexion or side leg raise to contract the upper external oblique muscles.
- Hold the peak contraction briefly, then return smoothly to the starting position before repeating on the opposite side.
exercises.author: http://www.carinatum.com/

exercises.name: Smith Machine Upright Row
exercises.description:
The movements are basically the same as with an SZ-bar, but you use the bar on the multi press:
Stand straight, your feet are shoulder-width apart. Hold the bar with an overhand grip on your thighs, the arms are stretched. Lift the bar close to the body till your chin. The elbows point out so that at the highest point they form a V. Make here a short pause before going slowly down and repeating the movement.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Upright Row
exercises.description: Stand straight, your feet are shoulder-width apart. Hold the SZ-bar with an overhand grip on your thighs, the arms are stretched. Lift the bar close to the body till your chin. The elbows point out so that at the highest point they form a V. Make here a short pause before going slowly down and repeating the movement.
exercises.author: wger.de

exercises.name: Dumbbell Upright Row
exercises.description:
- Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with palms facing your body.
- Pull the dumbbells vertically up along your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping the weights close to your body.
- Lift until the dumbbells reach mid-chest level and your elbows are elevated, then slowly lower them back down under control.
exercises.author: koreyhinton

exercises.name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
- Attach a close-grip V-bar handle to the lat pulldown station and adjust the thigh pad to secure your legs.
- Grip the handles with palms facing each other (neutral grip) and sit upright with chest lifted.
- Pull the handle smoothly down toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and close to your ribs.
- Squeeze your lats firmly at the bottom, then slowly return the handle to full extension under complete control.
exercises.author: apeschel

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description:
- Stand on the ball of one foot on a step or sturdy elevated platform, keeping the other foot lifted off the floor.
- Lightly hold onto a wall or railing for balance.
- Lower your heel as far down as comfortable to achieve a full stretch in the calf muscle.
- Press explosively through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as possible into peak contraction.
- Pause briefly at the top, then lower under slow control before switching to the other leg.
exercises.author: McMarcel13

exercises.name: Wall Handstand
exercises.description:
- Kick up or walk your feet up against a sturdy wall into a handstand position, with hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
- Keep your arms fully extended and actively push the floor away through your shoulders, keeping core and glutes tight.
- Maintain a rigid, straight body line without over-arching your lower back, breathing steadily throughout the isometric hold.
exercises.author: Nash

exercises.name: Wall Pushup
exercises.description:
- Stand about an arm's length away from a flat wall with feet hip-width apart.
- Place your palms flat against the wall at shoulder height and slightly wider than shoulder width.
- Keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels, bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the wall under control.
- Press firmly through your hands to return to the starting position without arching your lower back or sagging your hips.
exercises.author: Dexter

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.description: Stand with heels, shoulders, back of head, and hips touching the wall. Start with upper arms straight out to the sides and elbows at a 90-degree angle. Straighten the arms while remaining against the wall without arching the back off of the wall, mimicking a shoulder press movement.
exercises.author: Whythebigpaws

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.description:
- Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet shoulder-width apart, placed roughly two feet away from the wall.
- Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor, forming a 90-degree angle at both your hips and knees.
- Ensure your knees are directly above your ankles, brace your core, and hold the isometric squat position for the target duration.
exercises.author: Blablabla

exercises.name: Weighted Step-Ups
exercises.description:
- Place a barbell across your upper back (or hold a dumbbell in each hand) and stand upright facing a sturdy box or bench.
- Step firmly onto the platform with one foot, ensuring your entire foot is supported.
- Drive through your front heel to extend your hip and knee, stepping up onto the box until standing fully upright.
- Step back down with control under full eccentric tension before repeating or alternating legs.
exercises.author: jigglychipmunk

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
- Sit down at the lat pulldown station and secure your thighs firmly under the padded rollers.
- Grasp the wide bar with an overhand (pronated) grip wider than shoulder width.
- Pull the bar smoothly down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back while keeping your chest lifted.
- Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position under full control.
exercises.author: tuckerm

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push-Up
exercises.description:
- Place two flat-sided dumbbells on the floor about shoulder-width apart and grip the handles with a neutral grip.
- Assume a push-up plank position with your body forming a rigid, straight line from head to heels.
- Lower your chest down between the dumbbells, taking advantage of the elevated height for a deeper range of motion.
- Press firmly through your chest and triceps to return to the starting plank position.

exercises.name: Walking Barbell Lunge
exercises.description:
- Rest a barbell across your upper back (trapezius) and stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
- Take a controlled step forward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
- Drive through your front heel to stand up and immediately step forward with your trailing leg into the next lunge.
- Continue walking forward in a smooth, alternating rhythm while keeping your torso upright and core engaged.

exercises.name: One-Arm Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
- Stand facing or slightly angled to a high cable pulley, holding a single handle or rope end with one hand.
- Pin your upper arm securely to your side with your elbow bent at roughly 90 degrees.
- Press the attachment downward by extending your elbow until your triceps is fully contracted.
- Return the handle upward in a slow and controlled motion without shifting your elbow or shoulder.

exercises.name: Fingerboard Sloper Hang
exercises.description:
- Place both hands with an open hand position flat onto the sloper holds of a hangboard/fingerboard.
- Engage your shoulders actively (pulling them down and back) and maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
- Lift your feet off the ground and rely on open-hand friction and forearm flexor strength to hang steadily for the prescribed duration.
- Keep your core engaged and body steady without swinging.
exercises.author: marcelbader

exercises.name: Cable Rope Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: The cable rope push-down is a popular exercise targeting the triceps muscles. It's easy to learn and perform, making it a favorite for everyone from beginners to advanced lifters. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more per set, as part of an upper-body or arm-focused workout.
exercises.author: cshep442

exercises.name: Fingerboard 20 mm Edge Hang
exercises.description:
- Grip the 20 mm edge of the fingerboard with both hands using an open-hand or half-crimp grip.
- Engage your shoulders actively (pulling them down away from your ears) and maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
- Lift your feet off the floor and hang steadily for the prescribed time (e.g., 10 seconds), maintaining full body tension.
exercises.author: marcelbader

exercises.name: Fingerboard Pull-Up
exercises.description:
- Grip a suitable symmetric edge or hold on the fingerboard using an open-hand or half-crimp grip.
- Hang with arms fully extended and shoulders actively engaged.
- Pull your body upward smoothly by engaging your lats and arms until your chin clears your hand level.
- Lower yourself down slowly under full control (taking 2 to 3 seconds) back to the starting position without abruptly dropping.
exercises.author: marcelbader

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description:
- Set the cable pulleys to approximately head or eye level.
- Grasp the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand, crossing the cables in front of you.
- Pull your arms out and back in a wide horizontal arc while keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
- Squeeze your rear deltoids at the end of the range, then slowly return the handles back across your chest under control.
exercises.author: cshep442

exercises.name: Incline Bench Reverse Fly
exercises.description:
- Lie chest-down on an incline bench set to a 30- to 45-degree angle, holding a pair of dumbbells hanging down with palms facing each other.
- Keeping a slight, rigid bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your upper arms are level with your shoulders.
- Squeeze your rear deltoids and upper back muscles firmly at the top.
- Lower the dumbbells back down slowly and under control without using momentum.
exercises.author: cshep442

exercises.name: Zone 2 Running
exercises.description:
- Run at a steady, conversational pace corresponding to Zone 2 cardio (typically 60-70% of maximum heart rate).
- Maintain an intensity where you can comfortably speak in full sentences or breathe primarily through your nose (the talk test).
- Keep your heart rate consistent throughout the duration of the run to develop your aerobic base and metabolic efficiency.
exercises.author: karly

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
exercises.description:
- Kneel upright on a padded mat with your toes pointed behind you and hips fully extended in a straight line from knees to head.
- Lean your torso backward slowly under control by bending only at your knees.
- Resist gravity using your quadriceps, descending as far back as your strength allows without breaking at the hips.
- Contract your quadriceps powerfully to pull yourself back up to the starting tall-kneeling position.
exercises.author: karly

exercises.name: Nordic Curl
exercises.description:
- Kneel on a padded surface and secure your ankles firmly under a stationary barbell or have a training partner anchor them down.
- Keep your torso upright and brace your glutes and core to form a rigid line from your knees to your head.
- Lower your torso forward toward the floor as slowly and controlled as possible, resisting gravity solely with your hamstrings.
- Catch yourself lightly on the floor with your hands at the bottom, then push off gently to assist your hamstrings in pulling you back to the starting upright position.
exercises.author: karly

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Skull Crusher
exercises.description:
- Lie back on an incline bench set to roughly 30 to 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended overhead.
- Keep your upper arms angled slightly backward and stationary throughout the movement.
- Bend your elbows smoothly to lower the dumbbells down past the sides of your head until your triceps are fully stretched.
- Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up to the starting position, squeezing your triceps firmly at the top.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Straight-Bar Cable Curl
exercises.description:
- Stand upright facing a low cable pulley and grasp the straight bar attachment with an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart.
- Keep your elbows pinned closely to your sides and your torso steady.
- Curl the bar upward toward your chest by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary.
- Squeeze your biceps at the peak of the curl, then lower the bar slowly under control back to full extension.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Reverse Preacher Curl (Close Grip)
exercises.description:
- Sit at a preacher bench and position your upper arms flat against the angled arm pad.
- Grasp an EZ-bar with a close overhand (pronated) grip with knuckles facing upward.
- Curl the bar upward by flexing your elbows while keeping your upper arms firmly planted on the pad, targeting the brachioradialis and brachialis.
- Lower the bar slowly and with control until your arms are nearly fully extended, avoiding hyperextending your elbows at the bottom.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Reverse EZ-Bar Cable Curl
exercises.description:
- Attach an EZ-curl bar to the low pulley of a cable station and stand facing the machine.
- Grasp the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip on the inner angled curves of the bar.
- Keeping your elbows tucked tightly against your sides, curl the bar upward until your forearms approach your chest.
- Lower the bar slowly under full control back to the starting position, keeping constant tension on your forearms and brachialis.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Bus Drivers
exercises.description:
- Sit upright on a bench or floor and hold a weight plate with both hands at the 9 and 3 o'clock positions.
- Extend your arms forward with slightly bent elbows, holding the plate out just below eye level.
- Rotate the plate smoothly from side to side in a controlled steering motion, turning one hand on top and then the other.
- Keep your arms elevated at shoulder height and your core braced throughout the set.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Smith Machine Overhead Press
exercises.description:
- Position an incline bench set to an 80-85 degree angle directly beneath the Smith machine bar.
- Sit back on the bench, grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip, and unrack it at chin level.
- Press the bar upward in the fixed track until your arms are extended overhead without aggressively locking out your elbows.
- Lower the bar slowly under control back down to chin or upper-chest level before pressing again.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Straight Bar Cable Front Raise
exercises.description:
- Attach a straight bar to the low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the cable stack with the cable running between your legs.
- Grasp the straight bar with an overhand (pronated) grip at shoulder-width in front of your thighs.
- Raise the bar straight out in front of you with slightly bent elbows until it reaches shoulder or eye level.
- Pause briefly at the top to contract your anterior deltoids, then lower the bar slowly under control without swinging your hips.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
- Sit on the edge of a flat bench with feet firmly planted and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
- Lean your torso slightly forward and maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
- Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your elbows and weights reach shoulder height.
- Pause briefly at the top of the lift, then lower the dumbbells slowly under full control without swinging.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Straddle the T-bar or landmine bar with feet shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips at roughly a 45-degree angle with a flat back and slightly bent knees. Grasp the V-grip handles with arms fully extended.
Execution: Pull the weight smoothly toward your upper abdomen, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Return: Lower the weight under control until your arms are extended, keeping your spine in a neutral position throughout.
Cues: Keep your chest lifted and avoid using excessive momentum or rounding your lower back.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Seated Cable Mid Trap Shrug
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit upright at a cable row station with feet secured against the footrests. Grasp the cable attachment with arms fully extended in front of you.
Execution: Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades straight back toward each other (scapular retraction). Squeeze your mid-traps and rhomboids firmly at the peak contraction for 1–2 seconds.
Return: Slowly allow your shoulder blades to protract forward under control back to the starting position.
Cues: Keep your torso still and upright; do not lean backward to move the weight.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Row and Seated Shrug
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie face down (prone) on a slight incline bench (around 30–45 degrees), holding a pair of dumbbells with arms hanging straight toward the floor in a neutral grip.
Execution:
1. Lying Dumbbell Row: Pull the dumbbells upward by driving your elbows back past your torso, squeezing your lats and mid-back at the peak. Lower under control. Complete the prescribed row repetitions.
2. Seated Shrug: Immediately sit upright on the bench and perform dumbbell shrugs, elevating your shoulders straight up toward your ears to target the upper and middle traps.
Return: Lower the dumbbells smoothly with control after each repetition.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Smith Machine Slight Incline Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on a slight incline bench (15–30 degrees) positioned inside a Smith machine. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Unrack the bar and hold it above your upper chest with arms extended.
Execution: Lower the bar smoothly toward your upper chest and collarbones, keeping your shoulder blades retracted and elbows angled at roughly 45–60 degrees from your torso.
Return: Press the bar straight up along the guided track until your arms are nearly fully extended, focusing on the contraction of the clavicular (upper) pectorals.
Cues: Keep your feet flat on the floor and maintain a stable arch in your upper back without lifting your glutes off the bench.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Machine Chest Fly
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the chest fly machine with your back and head firmly against the backrest. Adjust seat height so that handles or pads are level with your mid-chest. Grasp the handles with a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Execution: Contract your pectoral muscles to bring the handles together in front of your chest in a smooth, hugging arc. Squeeze firmly at the peak contraction.
Return: Slowly reverse the motion, allowing your chest muscles to stretch under control without letting the weight stack touch down between reps.
Cues: Keep your shoulders depressed and retracted; do not let your shoulders roll forward.
exercises.author: novadani

exercises.name: Suspension Chest Fly
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Grasp the suspension trainer handles with a neutral grip and lean forward into an incline plank, arms extended straight in front of your chest and body in a rigid line from head to heels.
Execution: Maintaining a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a deep, comfortable stretch across your pectorals.
Return: Engage your chest muscles to bring the handles back together in front of your body, keeping your core braced and hips aligned.
Cues: Adjust your body angle relative to the floor to scale difficulty (more horizontal increases resistance).

exercises.name: Quadruped Arm and Leg Raise (Bird Dog)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin on all fours (quadruped position) with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Keep your head and spine in a neutral alignment.
Execution: Simultaneously extend your right arm forward and your left leg backward until both are parallel to the floor, actively squeezing your glute and lower back muscles.
Return: Hold for 1–2 seconds at full extension, then slowly lower your hand and knee back to the floor. Alternate sides on each repetition.
Cues: Keep your core braced and your hips square to the ground; do not allow your pelvis to rotate or your lower back to hyperextend.
exercises.author: utkb

exercises.name: TRX Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Grasp the TRX handles with an underhand (supinated) grip and face the anchor point. Lean backward with your arms extended and feet positioned forward, keeping your body in a rigid plank line.
Execution: Keeping your elbows high at shoulder height and pointed forward, flex your elbows to pull your forehead toward your hands using biceps strength.
Return: Slowly lower your body backward under control by extending your arms back to the starting position.
Cues: Do not drop your elbows or use hip thrusting momentum; maintain full core tension throughout.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: TRX Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Face the anchor point, grasp the TRX handles with a neutral grip, and lean backward with arms extended. Walk your feet forward to achieve the desired body incline, keeping your body in a straight plank line from head to heels.
Execution: Pull your chest up toward the handles by driving your elbows backward and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return: Lower your body under control until your arms are fully extended, maintaining a tight core throughout.
Cues: The closer your body is to horizontal, the greater the difficulty. Do not allow your hips to sag.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, with the kettlebell placed on the floor about a foot in front of you. Hinge at your hips with a flat back and grip the handle with both hands.
Execution: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs like a center in football. Snap your hips forward explosively, driving through your heels and contracting your glutes to swing the kettlebell up to chest height.
Return: Let the kettlebell float back down and hinge at your hips to guide it back between your legs, immediately transitioning into the next repetition.
Cues: The movement is a pure hip hinge, not a squat. Power comes from your hips and glutes, not your shoulders or arms.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: 50m Swim Sprints
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Position yourself in the pool at the starting wall, ready for an explosive push-off.
Execution: Sprint 50 meters at maximum effort using freestyle (front crawl), focusing on high stroke cadence, powerful kick, and streamlined body position.
Structure: Performed on a fixed interval (e.g. on 1 minute). Rest for the remainder of the interval after touching the wall before launching the next sprint.
Cues: Maximize speed and power while maintaining efficient stroke mechanics throughout the entire 50-meter distance.
exercises.author: abuono

exercises.name: Elliptical Trainer
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles or stationary bar. Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged.
Execution: Push through your feet in a smooth, continuous elliptical gliding motion while pushing and pulling the handles in opposition to your leg drive.
Cues: Keep your entire foot in contact with the pedals to reduce calf strain and engage glutes and hamstrings. Maintain an upright posture without slouching.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Two-Handed Kettlebell Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, gripping the horn handles of the kettlebell with both hands in front of your thighs, arms extended.
Execution: Keeping your elbows stationary at your sides, curl the kettlebell upward toward chest height by flexing your biceps.
Return: Lower the kettlebell slowly and smoothly back to full arm extension.
Cues: Avoid using torso swing or hip drive to move the weight; focus on pure biceps contraction.

exercises.name: One-Handed Kettlebell Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart. Hold the kettlebell by the handle in one hand with your arm extended at your side.
Execution: Curl the kettlebell upward toward shoulder height by flexing your elbow, maintaining a stable wrist and neutral spine.
Return: Lower the weight under control back to full extension. Complete all reps before switching sides.
Cues: Keep your elbow pinned close to your ribcage and resist leaning or twisting your torso.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Medicine Ball V-Up Crunch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie flat on your back on a mat with legs extended straight and arms extended overhead holding a medicine ball with both hands.
Execution: Simultaneously raise your straight legs and torso off the floor, bringing the medicine ball toward your shins/feet into a "V" shape crunch. Squeeze your abdominal muscles firmly at the top.
Return: Slowly lower your torso and legs back to the floor under control without letting your lower back hyperextend.
Cues: Keep the movement smooth and controlled; avoid throwing the ball or utilizing uncontrolled momentum.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.description:
Set up the box: Position the box behind you, about 3 feet from a squat rack if you're using a barbell. Choose a height that allows you to squat down and gently tap your glutes on the box with your back straight.
Stand with proper form: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward. Engage your core and keep your back neutral. If using a barbell, rack it at shoulder height.
Lower down: Sit back as if going to sit on a chair, bending your knees and lowering your hips towards the box. Keep your core tight and back straight throughout the movement.
Controlled descent: Descend in a controlled manner until your glutes gently touch the box. Don't plop down.
Pause and press up: Briefly pause at the bottom with your back straight and core engaged. Then, press through your heels to drive yourself back up to the starting position.

Improvements in coordination, balance and endurance, toning of the leg and buttock muscles and an overall increase in bone density eliminating the risk of osteoporosis.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended and shoulders packed. Keep your legs together and body still.
Execution: Engage your abs and curl your knees up toward your chest, flexing your spine and tucking your pelvis upward to maximize abdominal contraction.
Return: Lower your legs back down under control to the starting position without swinging.
Cues: Avoid swinging your legs or using momentum. Focus on posteriorly tilting your pelvis at the top.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Hang from a pull-up bar with a firm shoulder-width grip, body elongated and shoulders engaged to protect the joints.
Execution: Keeping your legs straight, contract your abdominal muscles to raise your legs until they are at least parallel to the floor (a 90-degree angle with your torso) or higher.
Return: Lower your legs slowly and smoothly back to the vertical hanging position without swinging.
Cues: Initiate the movement from your core and pelvis, not by swinging through the shoulders or arching your back.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Commando Pull-Up
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand directly beneath the pull-up bar aligned with its length. Grip the bar with one hand facing forward (prone) and one hand facing backward (supine) in a close staggered grip. Hang with arms extended.
Execution: Pull your body upward while keeping your torso straight and preventing rotation, bringing your head to one side of the bar until your shoulder touches it.
Return: Lower yourself smoothly back to a full hang, then repeat by pulling up with your head passing on the opposite side of the bar. Alternate sides with each repetition.
Cues: Maintain core tightness to resist rotational forces. Switch hand positions between sets for balanced development.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright facing a sturdy bench, box, or step with feet hip-width apart.
Execution: Place your entire right foot firmly onto the step. Drive through your right heel to lift your body onto the platform until your right leg is fully extended. Tap your left foot on the surface or bring your left knee up.
Return: Step back down under control with the left foot, followed by the right foot, returning to the starting position.
Cues: Keep your torso upright and do not push off excessively with the trailing leg.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Execution: Run in place dynamically, driving one knee up toward your chest until your thigh is parallel to the ground, then rapidly switch to the other leg. Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs.
Cues: Stay light on the balls of your feet, maintain an upright posture, and keep a rapid, rhythmic cadence.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Lunge
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest lifted, and hands on your hips or held together in front of your chest.
Execution: Take a controlled, generous step forward with one leg. Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90-degree angles, with the back knee hovering just above the floor.
Return: Push through the front heel to drive yourself back up to the starting standing position.
Cues: Keep your torso upright throughout and ensure the front knee tracks in line with your toes without caving inward.

exercises.name: Push-up with Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Assume a standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulders and body in a rigid plank line.
Execution: Lower your chest toward the floor into a push-up. As you press back up, rotate your torso and raise one arm straight toward the ceiling, forming a "T" shape with your body.
Return: Lower your hand back to the floor under control, perform another push-up, and rotate to the opposite side.
Cues: Keep your hips elevated and core tight; do not let your lower back sag during the rotation.

exercises.name: Side Lunge (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly outward.
Execution: Shift your weight toward your left side, bending your left knee and sitting your hips back while keeping your right leg straight and foot flat on the floor. Lower until your left thigh is nearly parallel to the ground.
Return: Drive through your left heel to return to the wide standing position.
Cues: Keep your chest up, your left knee tracking over your left foot, and do not let your heel lift off the ground.

exercises.name: Side Lunge (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly outward.
Execution: Shift your weight toward your right side, bending your right knee and sitting your hips back while keeping your left leg straight and foot flat on the floor. Lower until your right thigh is nearly parallel to the ground.
Return: Drive through your right heel to return to the wide standing position.
Cues: Keep your chest up, your right knee tracking over your right foot, and do not let your heel lift off the ground.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand about two feet in front of a sturdy bench or chair. Place the top of your right foot onto the bench behind you, with your left foot firmly planted forward.
Execution: Lower your hips by bending your left knee until your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground and your right knee hovers just above the floor.
Return: Push through the heel and midfoot of your left leg to return to the starting upright position.
Cues: Keep your torso slightly leaned forward from the hips with a flat back; do not let your front knee collapse inward.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand about two feet in front of a sturdy bench or chair. Place the top of your left foot onto the bench behind you, with your right foot firmly planted forward.
Execution: Lower your hips by bending your right knee until your right thigh is roughly parallel to the ground and your left knee hovers just above the floor.
Return: Push through the heel and midfoot of your right leg to return to the starting upright position.
Cues: Keep your torso slightly leaned forward from the hips with a flat back; do not let your front knee collapse inward.

exercises.name: Kneeling Glute Kickback
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin on all fours (quadruped) on a mat with your hands beneath your shoulders and knees beneath your hips.
Execution: Keeping your core tight and maintaining a 90-degree bend in your knee (or extending the leg straight), drive the sole of one foot upward and backward toward the ceiling, contracting your glute intensely.
Return: Hold for a second at the top, then slowly lower your knee back toward the floor without letting it rest completely.
Cues: Avoid arching your lower back or shifting your weight heavily to one side.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Take a long stride forward with your left leg, keeping your feet hip-width apart for balance. Keep your torso upright with your weight distributed between both feet.
Execution: Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees until your left thigh is parallel to the ground and your right knee hovers just above the floor.
Return: Drive upward through your left front heel and right forefoot to return to the starting position.
Cues: Keep your torso vertical and avoid leaning forward or letting your front knee track past your toes.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Take a long stride forward with your right leg, keeping your feet hip-width apart for balance. Keep your torso upright with your weight distributed between both feet.
Execution: Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground and your left knee hovers just above the floor.
Return: Drive upward through your right front heel and left forefoot to return to the starting position.
Cues: Keep your torso vertical and avoid leaning forward or letting your front knee track past your toes.

exercises.name: Jump Rope (Basic Jumps)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand with feet close together, holding a jump rope handle in each hand with the rope resting behind your heels. Keep elbows tucked in close to your ribs.
Execution: Turn the rope with small, controlled wrist rotations and jump slightly off the ground (about 1–2 inches) as the rope passes beneath your feet. Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Cues: Keep your knees softly bent and maintain a relaxed, rhythmic cadence. Power the rope from your wrists, not your whole arms.

exercises.name: Forward Arm Circles
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Execution: Make small, controlled circular motions with your arms rotating forward. Gradually increase the size of the circles as your shoulders warm up.
Cues: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and avoid shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.

exercises.name: Backward Arm Circles
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Execution: Make small, controlled circular motions with your arms rotating backward, opening up your chest and engaging your upper back.
Cues: Keep your torso stable and avoid excessive arching in your lower back.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, core braced, and body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Execution: Drive your right knee forward toward your chest without letting your hips pike or your foot touch down. Quickly return the right leg while simultaneously driving the left knee forward in a rhythmic running cadence.
Cues: Keep your hips down, shoulders stacked over your wrists, and back flat throughout the movement.

exercises.name: 4-Count Burpees
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
Execution:
1. Drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
2. Kick your feet back into a high plank position.
3. Jump your feet back up to your hands into the squat position.
4. Stand straight up explosively to complete the rep (omitting the push-up and overhead jump).
Cues: Keep your core tight during the plank phase to protect your lower back.

exercises.name: No-Push-Up Burpees
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Execution: Drop into a squat and place your hands flat on the floor. Jump your feet backward into a strong high plank without performing a push-up. Immediately jump your feet forward outside your hands, then leap explosively into the air, reaching overhead.
Return: Land softly with bent knees and seamlessly transition into the next repetition.
Cues: Maintain a rigid core line when kicking back into the plank.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, chest lifted and hands on hips or in front of your chest.
Execution: Take a controlled step backward with one leg, landing on the ball of your foot. Lower your hips until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee hovers just above the floor.
Return: Drive through your front heel to return to the standing starting position.
Cues: Keep your torso upright and front knee tracking over your front toes.

exercises.name: Floor Dips
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat on the ground. Place your hands on the floor just behind your hips with fingers pointing forward toward your feet. Lift your hips a few inches off the floor.
Execution: Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor, keeping your elbows tracking backward and close to your body.
Return: Press through the palms of your hands to extend your arms and raise your hips back up, contracting your triceps at the top.
Cues: Keep the movement centered at your elbow joint rather than merely rocking your hips up and down.

exercises.name: High Plank
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Place your hands on the floor directly beneath your shoulders with arms fully extended. Step your feet back and balance on your toes, holding your body in a straight plank line from head to heels.
Execution: Maintain isometric tension across your entire body: contract your abdominals, squeeze your glutes, and push the floor away to keep your upper back broad.
Cues: Do not let your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. Keep your neck in a neutral line looking slightly ahead of your hands.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Kneel on a mat with your knees spread wide, big toes touching, and sit back onto your heels.
Execution: Fold forward at your hips, resting your torso between your thighs. Extend your arms long in front of you on the mat, palms down, and gently lower your forehead to the floor.
Cues: Breathe deeply into your back and ribcage, allowing your spine, hips, and shoulders to relax and lengthen with each exhalation.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, with a kettlebell centered between your feet in line with your ankles.
Execution: Hinge at your hips, pushing your glutes back and bending your knees slightly while maintaining a flat back. Grip the kettlebell handle firmly with both hands. Drive through your feet and push your hips forward to stand up tall, contracting your glutes at the top.
Return: Reverse the motion by hinging at the hips and lowering the kettlebell under control back to the floor between your feet.
Cues: Keep your shoulders packed down and your spine neutral throughout; do not round your back.

exercises.name: Forward Shoulder Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand tall with a neutral spine and relaxed shoulders. Place the fingertips of each hand lightly on top of your shoulders.
Execution: Draw smooth, large circles forward with your elbows, rotating your shoulder joints in a continuous and controlled rhythm.
Cues: Keep your neck relaxed and chest open; focus on mobilizing the glenohumeral joint and scapulae without straining.

exercises.name: Backward Shoulder Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand tall with a neutral spine and relaxed shoulders. Place the fingertips of each hand lightly on top of your shoulders.
Execution: Draw smooth, large circles backward with your elbows, opening up your chest and gently squeezing your shoulder blades together as you rotate.
Cues: Keep your neck relaxed and breathe evenly throughout the mobility movement.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders back and down, eyes looking straight ahead at eye level.
Execution: Without tilting your head down, draw your chin horizontally backward as if making a subtle "double chin," aligning your ears directly over your shoulders.
Return: Hold the retracted position for 3–5 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch at the base of the skull, then release back to neutral.
Cues: Do not bend your neck down toward your chest; the movement is purely horizontal retraction.

exercises.name: Head Turns
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed and down, looking straight forward.
Execution: Slowly turn your head to one side until you feel a gentle stretch along the opposite side of your neck. Hold for 1–2 seconds, return smoothly to center, and repeat to the opposite side.
Cues: Move within a pain-free range of motion without tilting your head or forcing the turn.

exercises.name: Neck Stretch (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand upright with shoulders relaxed and down.
Execution: Gently tilt your head to the right, bringing your right ear toward your right shoulder to stretch the left side of your neck and upper trapezius. Optionally place your right hand lightly over your head to deepen the stretch with minimal pressure.
Return: Hold for 15–30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then slowly return your head to the neutral center.
Cues: Keep your left shoulder depressed; do not shrug either shoulder upward.

exercises.name: Neck Stretch (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit or stand upright with shoulders relaxed and down.
Execution: Gently tilt your head to the left, bringing your left ear toward your left shoulder to stretch the right side of your neck and upper trapezius. Optionally place your left hand lightly over your head to deepen the stretch with minimal pressure.
Return: Hold for 15–30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then slowly return your head to the neutral center.
Cues: Keep your right shoulder depressed; do not shrug either shoulder upward.

exercises.name: Back Neck Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit upright on a chair or stand tall with shoulders relaxed and down. Place your hands lightly behind your head with fingers interlaced.
Execution: Exhale and gently tilt your head forward, tucking your chin toward your chest. Allow the natural weight of your hands to provide light guidance until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back of your neck and upper spine.
Return: Hold for 15–30 seconds, then slowly and gently lift your head back to neutral.
Cues: Do not force or pull hard on your head; let gentle gravity and relaxed breathing deepen the stretch.

exercises.name: Front Neck Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.

Execution:
1. Open your mouth wide.
2. Slowly tilt your head backward with your mouth open until you feel a gentle stretch along the front of your neck.
3. Very slowly close and open your mouth a few times to deepen the stretch of the anterior neck muscles and platysma.
4. Slowly return your head to the neutral starting position and close your mouth.

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Bicep Curls
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended down by your sides and palms facing inward. Keep your shoulders back and core engaged.

Execution:
1. Bend one arm at the elbow, rotating your forearm upward (supination) so your palm faces your shoulder at the top.
2. Curl the dumbbell up until your bicep is fully contracted, keeping your upper arm still and tucked close to your torso.
3. Slowly lower the weight back down to the starting position under full control.
4. Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides smoothly.

exercises.name: Left Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight. Turn your head approximately 45 degrees to the left. Place your right hand behind your back or under your thigh to anchor the right shoulder down. Place your left hand on the back of your head and gently tuck your chin toward your left armpit.

Execution:
1. Maintain gentle downward guidance with your left hand until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back and right side of your neck.
2. Optionally apply a very light isometric pressure with your head backward into your hand for a few seconds, then relax deeper into the stretch.
3. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply, then slowly release.

exercises.name: Right Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight. Turn your head approximately 45 degrees to the right. Place your left hand behind your back or under your thigh to anchor the left shoulder down. Place your right hand on the back of your head and gently tuck your chin toward your right armpit.

Execution:
1. Maintain gentle downward guidance with your right hand until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back and left side of your neck.
2. Optionally apply a very light isometric pressure with your head backward into your hand for a few seconds, then relax deeper into the stretch.
3. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply, then slowly release.

exercises.name: Clockwise Neck Circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight and shoulders relaxed and down. Lower your chin gently toward your chest.

Execution:
1. In a slow, controlled, and fluid motion, roll your head in a clockwise direction: tilt toward your right shoulder, gently roll back, continue to the left shoulder, and return to your chest.
2. Keep your neck relaxed and avoid compressing the cervical spine when passing through the back.
3. Repeat for the desired number of smooth, continuous repetitions.

exercises.name: Counterclockwise Neck Circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight and shoulders relaxed. Lower your chin gently toward your chest.

Execution:
1. In a slow, fluid, and controlled motion, roll your head in a counterclockwise circle: tilt toward your left shoulder, roll gently back, continue toward the right shoulder, and return to the chest.
2. Keep the movement smooth and relaxed without hyperextending or straining the neck.
3. Repeat continuously for the recommended repetitions.

exercises.name: Neck Half Circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your back straight and shoulders relaxed. Gently tilt your head toward one shoulder (e.g. right ear toward right shoulder).

Execution:
1. Slowly roll your head forward and down, letting your chin trace a smooth arc across your chest toward the opposite shoulder.
2. Reverse the motion, rolling your chin back across your chest to the starting side.
3. Continue alternating side to side in a gentle, controlled crescent motion without rolling your head backward.

exercises.name: Head Tilts (Lateral Neck Stretch)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit or stand tall with your spine neutral and shoulders relaxed and drawn down.

Execution:
1. Slowly tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear toward your shoulder until you feel a gentle stretch along the opposite side of your neck.
2. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds while keeping both shoulders down.
3. Return to the neutral center position, then repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Side Plank Right
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie on your right side with your legs extended and feet stacked or staggered. Place your right elbow directly beneath your right shoulder with your forearm resting flat on the floor.

Execution:
1. Contract your core, obliques, and glutes, then lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
2. Keep your neck neutral and your top hand resting on your hip or extended toward the ceiling.
3. Hold this static position for the target duration while breathing steadily without letting your hips sag.

exercises.name: Pistol Squats Right
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall on your right leg with your left leg extended straight out in front of you, slightly off the floor. Extend your arms forward for balance.

Execution:
1. Slowly bend your right knee and sit your hips back and down into a deep single-leg squat.
2. Keep your back straight, chest up, and your left leg elevated off the ground throughout the movement.
3. Descend until your right thigh is at least parallel to the floor (or deeper if mobility permits).
4. Drive firmly through your right heel to stand back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: Right-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Stand on the floor or on the edge of a step to increase the range of movement.
Raise one foot.
Lift your heel until you're standing on your toes.
(variable) Stay in this position for three seconds
Slowly lower your foot until you almost touch the ground with your heel - don't slam your foot!

exercises.name: Single-Arm Plank to Row (Renegade Row)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a high plank position supporting your weight on your hands (holding a pair of dumbbells or with one hand on the floor and the other gripping a dumbbell). Position your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider for stability.

Execution:
1. Brace your core, glutes, and hips to prevent your pelvis from rotating or swaying.
2. Pull the dumbbell upward toward your hip in a controlled rowing motion, keeping your elbow tucked closely along your side.
3. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze your latissimus dorsi and upper back.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the ground under control.
5. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the opposite arm, or alternate as programmed.

exercises.name: Elevated Prayer Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Kneel in front of a flat bench or elevated surface. Place both elbows on the edge of the bench roughly shoulder-width apart and press your palms together in a prayer position (or hold a light stick).

Execution:
1. Push your hips back and allow your chest to sink toward the floor, letting your head drop between your upper arms.
2. Bend your elbows to bring your hands back toward the nape of your neck/upper back.
3. Feel a deep stretch through your lats, triceps, and thoracic spine.
4. Hold the position for 20–40 seconds while taking slow, deep breaths, then gently ease out of the stretch.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation Left
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Start on all fours on hands and knees, with knees under hips and your right hand placed firmly on the floor under your right shoulder. Place your left hand lightly behind your head with your elbow flared out.

Execution:
1. On an inhale, rotate your thoracic spine downward, bringing your left elbow toward your right supporting arm/wrist.
2. On an exhale, rotate your chest and upper back upward to the left, pointing your left elbow toward the ceiling.
3. Keep your hips and pelvis level and steady throughout the rotation.
4. Perform the movement in a controlled rhythm for the prescribed repetitions.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation Right
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Start on all fours on hands and knees, with knees under hips and your left hand placed firmly on the floor under your left shoulder. Place your right hand lightly behind your head with your elbow flared out.

Execution:
1. On an inhale, rotate your thoracic spine downward, bringing your right elbow toward your left supporting arm/wrist.
2. On an exhale, rotate your chest and upper back upward to the right, pointing your right elbow toward the ceiling.
3. Keep your hips and pelvis stable and level without shifting to the side.
4. Repeat smoothly for the desired number of repetitions.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Hindu Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin in a downward dog position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your hips pushed high, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and swoop downward in a sweeping arc, skimming your chest and face close to the floor.
2. Push up dynamically into an upward dog position, driving your chest forward and shoulders back.
3. Reverse the motion or push your hips straight back and up to return to the inverted 'V' starting position.
4. Repeat in a smooth, continuous fluid cycle.
exercises.author: Imobard

exercises.name: Shoulder Dislocates (with Band or Stick)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a resistance band, PVC pipe, or broomstick in front of your body with a wide overhand grip and arms fully extended.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbows straight, rotate your shoulders to sweep your arms up and overhead in a smooth, wide arc.
2. Continue the rotation backward until the band or stick reaches down behind your hips/glutes.
3. Avoid arching your lower back or bending your elbows; widen your grip if necessary.
4. Reverse the movement smoothly back over your head to the front of your body.
5. Repeat for the target number of fluid, mobility-enhancing repetitions.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Bent-Over Row to External Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Hinge forward at your hips with a flat back and knees slightly bent (torso angled at roughly 45–60 degrees). Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor.

Execution:
1. Row your elbows up to shoulder level so your upper arms are perpendicular to your torso and forearms point down at 90 degrees.
2. Keeping your elbows pinned at shoulder height, externally rotate your shoulders by raising your forearms and hands upward until level with your head.
3. Pause briefly at the top to contract your rotator cuff and rear deltoids.
4. Lower the forearms back down with control, then extend your arms to the starting position.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Prone Y-W-T Raises
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended and neck neutral, gazing toward the floor.

Execution:
1. Y-Position: Extend your arms overhead at roughly 45 degrees forming a 'Y', with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. Lift your arms and chest slightly off the floor, pinching your shoulder blades together. Hold for 10–20 seconds.
2. W-Position: Pull your elbows down and in toward your ribs, forming a 'W' shape while keeping your hands and arms elevated. Squeeze your mid-back firmly.
3. T-Position: Extend your arms directly out to the sides perpendicular to your torso forming a 'T', thumbs pointing up. Pinch your scapulae together and hold.
4. Transition smoothly through each letter to optimize scapular stability and upper-back endurance.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet planted flat. Hold a dumbbell in each hand positioned over your chest, with your upper arms resting on the floor and elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees to your torso.

Execution:
1. Press the dumbbells upward in a controlled, powerful motion until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
2. Squeeze your pectoral muscles hard at the top lockout position.
3. Lower the dumbbells slowly until the backs of your upper arms gently touch the floor.
4. Pause briefly on the floor to eliminate momentum, then press back up for the next rep.
exercises.author: admin

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set up in a standard high plank position, but place your hands close together directly beneath your chest (narrower than shoulder-width, thumbs almost touching). Your body should form a straight, rigid line from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Lower your body under control by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked tightly against your ribs.
2. Descend until your chest nearly touches the back of your hands.
3. Push forcefully through your palms and extend your arms, driving through the triceps back to the top plank position.
4. Keep your core braced and prevent your hips from sagging throughout the movement.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hang Power Cleans
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Hinge slightly at your hips and bend your knees to lower the dumbbells to just above knee level (hang position), keeping your back flat.

Execution:
1. Explosively extend your hips and knees while executing a powerful shoulder shrug.
2. Guide the momentum of the dumbbells vertically close to your body, quickly whipping your elbows forward underneath the weights.
3. Catch the dumbbells at shoulder level in a partial quarter-squat with soft knees.
4. Stand up fully to complete the repetition, then lower the weights back to the hang position with control.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a wide stance (roughly 1.5 to 2 times shoulder width) with your toes turned out at approximately 45 degrees. Stand over a vertically oriented dumbbell placed on the floor between your feet.

Execution:
