1. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees, keeping your chest tall and back straight, to grip the upper end of the dumbbell with both hands.
2. Drive your feet through the floor and extend your hips and knees to pull the weight upward to a full standing lockout.
3. Squeeze your glutes and inner thighs firmly at the top.
4. Lower the dumbbell back down under control until it touches the ground before initiating the next repetition.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the floor with knees bent. Keep your feet lightly touching the ground or elevated for increased difficulty. Hold a medicine ball with both hands in front of your chest and lean your torso back slightly to roughly 45 degrees, keeping your spine straight.

Execution:
1. Engage your core and rotate your torso smoothly to the right, bringing the medicine ball toward the floor near your right hip.
2. Reverse the twist through the center and rotate over to the left side, bringing the ball beside your left hip.
3. Keep your hips and legs as quiet as possible so the rotation originates strictly from your thoracic spine and obliques.
4. Continue alternating smoothly from side to side for the desired repetitions.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up (V-Push-Up)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set your hands and feet on the floor shoulder-width apart. Walk your feet in and drive your hips high into the air so your body forms an inverted 'V' (pike position). Keep your legs and back as straight as comfortable.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head diagonally forward toward the floor between and slightly ahead of your hands.
2. Descend with control until your head lightly approaches the ground.
3. Push through your palms and shoulders to press back up and back into the full inverted 'V' position.
4. Keep your core braced and focus the push on your front deltoids and triceps.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a strong high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet set slightly wider than hip-width apart for greater stability.

Execution:
1. Brace your core, glutes, and thighs to keep your pelvis completely level and prevent your hips from rotating.
2. Lift your right hand off the floor and tap your left shoulder in a smooth, controlled motion.
3. Return your right hand to the ground, then lift your left hand to tap your right shoulder.
4. Continue alternating sides while keeping your body as rigid and stable as possible.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Heavy Bag Training (Boxing)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand about an arm's length from the heavy bag in a balanced boxing stance. Keep your lead hand slightly forward, rear hand protecting your chin, knees soft, and weight on the balls of your feet.

Execution:
1. Throw crisp, powerful punches—such as jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts—into the center of the bag.
2. Rotate your hips, core, and pivot on your feet with each strike to generate power through kinetic linking.
3. Quickly snap your hands back to guard position after every punch and practice active footwork around the bag.
4. Work in timed rounds (e.g., 2–3 minutes) combining punch output, conditioning, and shoulder endurance.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Indoor Rowing Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit tall on the sliding seat and secure your feet firmly in the footstraps. Slide forward into the Catch: knees bent, shins vertical, torso tilted slightly forward at the hips (1 o'clock position), and arms extended straight grasping the handle.

Execution:
1. The Drive: Push explosively through your legs. As your legs reach near-full extension, swing your torso slightly backward (11 o'clock position), then pull the handle smoothly into your lower ribs.
2. The Finish: Legs extended, core engaged, shoulders down and back, handle lightly touching the lower sternum.
3. The Recovery: Extend your arms forward, hinge forward at the hips, and then bend your knees to slide smoothly back to the Catch.
4. Maintain a fluid rhythm with a powerful drive and a relaxed, controlled recovery.
exercises.author: Boertie

exercises.name: Seated Chest Press Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Adjust the seat height so the machine handles align with your mid-to-lower chest when seated. Sit tall with your back and head pressed against the backrest and your feet planted firmly on the floor.

Execution:
1. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, retract your shoulder blades, and brace your core.
2. Press the handles forward in a powerful, controlled motion until your arms are nearly fully extended without locking your elbows.
3. Squeeze your pectoral muscles hard at peak contraction.
4. Slowly return the handles under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, then repeat.
exercises.author: colundrum

exercises.name: Standing Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your weight balanced on your support leg. Place a hand on a wall or sturdy bar for balance. Keep your torso upright, pelvis level, and core engaged.

Execution:
1. Lift your working leg out to the side in a smooth, controlled motion without tilting your torso to the opposite side.
2. Raise the leg as high as comfortable while keeping your toes pointing forward and your hips squared.
3. Pause at the top and squeeze your gluteus medius and outer hip.
4. Slowly lower your leg back down under control without resting your weight between reps.
5. Complete all repetitions before switching legs.
exercises.author: tregga

exercises.name: Seated Rear Delt Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the edge of a flat bench with your feet planted together. Hold a pair of light dumbbells, hinge forward at your hips, and rest your chest near your thighs, letting the weights hang beneath your legs with elbows softly bent.

Execution:
1. Raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc, leading with your elbows, until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
2. Squeeze your rear deltoids and pinch your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
3. Pause for a second at peak contraction without using body momentum.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Dynamic Single-Leg Side Hold with Kettlebell
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Loop an elastic resistance band through the handle of a kettlebell and hold the band in one hand so the kettlebell hangs freely by your side. Stand tall with your spine neutral.

Execution:
1. Lift one foot off the floor to balance on a single leg.
2. Brace your core, obliques, and standing hip to maintain a strictly upright posture, actively stabilizing against the oscillations of the hanging kettlebell.
3. Hold for the prescribed duration, optionally switching your standing leg mid-set.
4. Repeat with the weight held in the opposite hand.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Wall Balls
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand roughly an arm's length away from a sturdy wall or target with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold a medicine ball at chest height with elbows tucked in.

Execution:
1. Descend into a full, deep squat, keeping your chest tall and knees tracking over your toes until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower.
2. Drive up explosively through your heels and hips, using the upward momentum to push-press and throw the ball high against the wall target (typically 9–10 feet high).
3. Catch the rebounding ball smoothly at chest height and immediately absorb the impact as you descend into the next squat.
4. Maintain a continuous, fluid rhythm throughout the set.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Isometric Pull-Up / Row Hold
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Grasp a pull-up bar (overhand or underhand grip) or suspension trainer/barbell set for inverted rows.

Execution:
1. Pull yourself up to the top flexed-arm position (chin over the bar or chest to the handles/bar).
2. Lock in this position statically: depress and retract your shoulder blades, squeezing your lats, rhomboids, and biceps intensely.
3. Maintain steady breathing and do not allow your shoulders to shrug up or your chest to collapse.
4. Hold for the prescribed duration (e.g., 10–30 seconds) before lowering under control.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Alternating Reverse Lunges
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your core engaged. Keep your hands on your hips or clasped in front of your chest.

Execution:
1. Step one foot backward in a long, controlled stride, landing on the ball of your rear foot.
2. Lower your hips vertically until both knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees. Your back knee should hover just above the ground while your front knee stays stacked over your ankle.
3. Push firmly through the heel and midfoot of your front leg to return to the standing starting position.
4. Immediately repeat with the opposite leg stepping backward, alternating legs fluidly with each repetition.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Walking Bridge
exercises.description: from a standing position with knees slightly bent and hands resting on the floor. From here, proceed forward with your hands keeping your buttocks contracted and without losing control of your lower back.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Walking
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with a relaxed, upright posture, shoulders drawn down and back, and eyes looking forward.

Execution:
1. Walk forward with a smooth, rhythmic stride, landing gently on your heel and rolling through to push off from the ball of your foot.
2. Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your leg movements with elbows softly bent.
3. Maintain an active, brisk pace of at least 100 steps per minute for optimal cardiovascular benefits.
4. Keep your core gently engaged and breathe steadily throughout your walk.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Tuck
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the floor or mat with your hands placed on the ground slightly behind your hips for support. Lean your torso back slightly and elevate your feet off the floor with knees softly bent.

Execution:
1. Extend your legs straight out in front of you while reclining your torso slightly further back, keeping your feet hovering above the ground.
2. Flex at your hips and knees, driving your knees toward your chest while pulling your torso slightly forward to maximize abdominal contraction.
3. Pause briefly at peak crunch, focusing on your rectus abdominis and hip flexors.
4. Slowly extend your legs back out without letting your feet touch the floor, repeating in a steady rhythm.
exercises.author: utkb

exercises.name: Cable Concentration Curl
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Position a bench in front of a low cable pulley. Sit on the bench, grasp the single-handle attachment with an underhand (supinated) grip, and brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.

Execution:
1. Curl the handle upward toward your shoulder by flexing at your elbow, keeping your upper arm securely pinned against your inner thigh to isolate the bicep.
2. Squeeze your bicep hard at the peak of the movement against the constant cable resistance.
3. Slowly lower the handle back down under control until your arm is nearly fully extended.
4. Complete all prescribed reps on one arm before switching to the other side.
exercises.author: cshep442

exercises.name: Incline Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on a sturdy bench, box, or elevated surface. Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels with your core engaged.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the edge of the elevated surface in a slow, controlled descent.
2. Lower until your chest nearly touches the surface, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body.
3. Press firmly through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
4. This variation decreases loading compared to flat push-ups and emphasizes the lower and mid-chest muscles.
exercises.author: anon1337

exercises.name: Decline Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place your feet elevated on a sturdy bench or box and set your hands flat on the floor directly under or slightly wider than your shoulders. Your body should form a rigid, diagonal straight line from heels to head.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and lower your chest under control toward the floor, keeping your core braced and hips elevated.
2. Lower until your nose or upper chest nearly grazes the ground.
3. Push firmly into the floor, extending your arms to press back up to the top lockout.
4. This variation increases loading on the upper pectorals (clavicular head) and anterior deltoids.
exercises.author: anon1337

exercises.name: Parallette Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set up two parallette bars parallel to each other on the floor roughly shoulder-width apart. Grip the bars firmly with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and extend your legs behind you into a solid plank position.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows and lower your chest deeply between the parallettes under complete control.
2. Take advantage of the increased range of motion to achieve a full stretch across your pectoral muscles.
3. Drive firmly through your palms to press back up to full arm extension.
4. The neutral wrist alignment reduces wrist joint strain while maximizing chest and triceps recruitment.
exercises.author: anon1337

exercises.name: 3D Lunge Warmup
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Hold light dumbbells at your sides or perform with bodyweight during warmups.

Execution:
1. Sagittal plane: Take a controlled lunge step directly forward, lower your hips until both knees bend at roughly 90 degrees, and push back to center.
2. Frontal plane: Step out laterally into a side lunge, bending the stepping knee while keeping the trailing leg straight, then drive back to standing.
3. Transverse plane: Step diagonally backward and open your hips at a 45-degree angle, sink into the lunge, and return to center.
4. Repeat the sequence across all planes with both legs to prepare your hips, knees, glutes, and adductors for multi-directional movement.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Dumbbell Farmer's Carry
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Deadlift a pair of heavy dumbbells off the floor using proper hinge mechanics and hold them firmly at your sides with arms fully extended. Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders pulled back and down, and core fully braced.

Execution:
1. Walk forward taking short, controlled, and deliberate steps.
2. Maintain an uncompromisingly upright posture: do not lean forward or allow your torso to sway laterally.
3. Keep your grip squeezed tightly and prevent the dumbbells from swinging as you walk.
4. Continue walking for the prescribed distance (e.g., 20–50 meters) or duration, then set the weights down safely with a flat back.
exercises.author: philip

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit at the seated cable row station and place your feet firmly on the footplates with knees softly bent. Hinge forward with a flat back to grip the handle (such as a close-grip V-bar), then push back until your torso is upright at 90 degrees with shoulders depressed and retracted.

Execution:
1. Pull the handle smoothly toward your abdomen/lower ribs, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together firmly at the end of the pull, contracting your lats and rhomboids.
3. Keep your torso stationary without excessive swinging or leaning back.
4. Slowly extend your arms and let your shoulder blades glide forward under control to feel a full stretch before the next rep.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Seated Machine Row (Close Grip)
exercises.description: Seated machine row performed with a close grip.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Seated Machine Row (Underhand Grip)
exercises.description: Seated machine or cable row performed with a close underhand (supinated) grip.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Supinated Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit at the lat pulldown machine and adjust the thigh pad so your thighs are securely anchored. Grasp the bar with a wide underhand (supinated, palms facing you) grip roughly shoulder-width to wider than shoulder-width apart. Keep your chest up and torso slightly reclined.

Execution:
1. Pull the bar down smoothly, guiding it close past your chin until it touches or nearly touches your upper chest.
2. Drive your elbows downward and slightly backward, actively depressing and squeezing your shoulder blades.
3. Keep your torso steady without excessively swinging your upper body backward.
4. Slowly allow the bar to return to the top position under control, fully extending your arms and feeling a deep stretch through your lats.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Close-Grip Supinated Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs firmly under the pads.
• Grasp the bar with a close underhand (supinated) grip, shoulder-width or slightly narrower, palms facing toward you.
• Keep your torso upright with a slight natural arch in your lower back and your chest lifted.

Execution:
• Pull the bar down smoothly toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and slightly backward close to your sides.
• Squeeze your lats and shoulder blades together at the bottom for a brief pause.
• Slowly let the bar return upward with control until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Cable Glute Extension
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley of a cable machine and secure it around your working ankle.
• Stand facing the machine, hinge forward slightly at the hips, and hold onto the frame for stability.
• Keep your supporting leg slightly bent and your pelvis squared forward.

Execution:
• Extend your working leg straight back and up behind you by contracting your glute, keeping a very slight bend in the knee.
• Squeeze your glute firmly at the peak of the movement for a brief pause without hyperextending your lower back.
• Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position under control, maintaining tension throughout.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: GHD Glute Extension
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie face down on a GHD (Glute-Ham Developer) or 45-degree hyperextension bench, securing your ankles firmly under the foot rollers.
• Position your hips just past the front edge of the pad so your hips can hinge freely.
• Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands lightly behind your head.

Execution:
• Lower your upper body by hinging forward at the hips while maintaining a neutral, flat spine.
• Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings to extend your hips and lift your torso back up until your body forms a straight line.
• Pause briefly at the top, focusing on maximum glute contraction, then lower with control.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit at a lat pulldown station (or kneel facing a high cable pulley) and secure your thighs firmly under the support pads.
• Grasp a parallel-grip attachment with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
• Sit tall with your chest lifted and a slight natural arch in your lower back.

Execution:
• Pull the handle down smoothly toward your upper chest, leading with your elbows driving down and back.
• Squeeze your shoulder blades together and pause briefly at the bottom to maximize lat contraction.
• Slowly let the handle return upward with full control until your arms are fully extended.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: High-Pulley Cable Pullover
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand facing a high pulley cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
• Grasp the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands shoulder-width apart and arms nearly straight with elbows softly unlocked.
• Hinge forward slightly at the hips while keeping your spine straight and core braced.

Execution:
• Pull the bar down in a wide sweeping arc toward your upper thighs using your lats, keeping your arms extended.
• Squeeze your lats firmly at the bottom of the movement for a brief pause.
• Slowly return the bar back up along the same arc to eye level, controlling the resistance throughout.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Incline Bench Cable Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Set up an incline bench at approximately 30 to 45 degrees facing a high cable pulley.
• Lie chest-down on the bench, keeping your head neutral and feet planted for stability.
• Reach overhead and grasp the cable handle or bar with extended arms.

Execution:
• Pull the handle smoothly down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
• The bench support prevents torso momentum, allowing strict isolation of the latissimus dorsi.
• Squeeze your back muscles at the peak contraction, then slowly extend your arms back up under control.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Arabesque
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright and shift your entire body weight onto one supporting leg.
• Keep a soft bend in the knee of your standing leg, with your hips and pelvis completely level and square to the front.
• Keep your spine in a neutral position and brace your core.

Execution:
• Hinge forward at the hips while extending your non-supporting leg straight back and up behind you.
• Lower your torso and elevate your rear leg until they form a horizontal line parallel to the ground.
• Squeeze the glute and hamstring of your standing leg to slowly bring yourself back up to the starting position.
exercises.author: cleen

exercises.name: Machine Back Extension
exercises.description: Back extension performed on a weighted extension machine to target the lower back.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright facing a high cable pulley equipped with a straight bar, EZ-bar, or rope attachment.
• Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip, elbows bent and tucked firmly against your ribs.
• Lean forward slightly from the hips with a flat back and braced core.

Execution:
• Push the bar down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended toward your thighs.
• Keep your upper arms completely stationary by your sides throughout the movement.
• Squeeze your triceps forcefully at the bottom of the movement for a brief pause.
• Slowly allow the bar to return to approximately chest height under full control.
exercises.author: anto.kreegyr

exercises.name: One-Arm Cable Bent-Over Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Attach a single D-handle to the low pulley of a cable station.
• Stand facing the machine in a staggered or athletic stance, hinging forward at your hips with a flat spine.
• Grasp the handle with one hand, arm fully extended toward the pulley.

Execution:
• Pull the handle smoothly back toward your hip/waist, driving your elbow backward close to your torso.
• Retract your shoulder blade at the peak of contraction and squeeze your lat firmly.
• Slowly extend your arm back forward under control to feel a deep stretch in your back before the next repetition.
exercises.author: anto.kreegyr

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
• Place your other hand lightly behind your head or resting on your opposite hip.
• Keep your chest open and your core braced.

Execution:
• Slowly bend your torso laterally strictly in the frontal plane toward the side holding the dumbbell. Do not rotate or twist your torso forward or backward!
• Use the oblique muscles on the opposite side to pull your torso back up to the vertical position.
• Complete the prescribed repetitions with control, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, arms fully extended, palms facing inward (neutral grip).
• Keep your chest lifted, shoulders back, and elbows tucked close to your ribs.

Execution:
• Curl one dumbbell upward while rotating (supinating) your forearm so that your palm faces your shoulder at the top of the movement.
• Squeeze your biceps firmly at the peak contraction for a brief pause.
• Slowly lower the dumbbell back down with control while initiating the curl with the opposite arm.
• Keep your torso completely stationary without swinging or using momentum.
exercises.author: Franpol

exercises.name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit on a mat with your knees bent and heels touching the floor (or lifted off the ground for increased difficulty).
• Hold a dumbbell horizontally with both hands in front of your chest.
• Lean your torso back at roughly a 45-degree angle, keeping your spine straight and core firmly engaged.

Execution:
• Rotate your torso smoothly to the right, bringing the dumbbell toward the floor next to your hip.
• Pause briefly, then rotate through the center to the left side in a controlled motion.
• Focus on turning your ribcage and engaging your obliques, keeping your hips and lower body as stable as possible.
exercises.author: lion

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley set at chest height.
• Grasp the handle with both hands and hold it tight against the center of your chest.
• Set your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly unlocked, and brace your core and glutes firmly.

Execution:
• Press the handle straight out in front of you until your arms are fully extended.
• Actively resist the rotational pull of the cable, keeping your shoulders and hips squared forward.
• Hold the extended position for 1 to 2 seconds, then slowly return your hands back to your chest under full control.
exercises.author: prevail90

exercises.name: Side Slides to Squats
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart in a low, athletic defensive stance.
• Keep your chest up and your knees bent.

Execution:
• Perform three quick, controlled lateral slide steps to one side, pushing off the trailing foot.
• Plant your feet firmly and perform a deep squat, keeping your chest tall and driving your knees outward.
• Pivot 180 degrees or reverse direction, continuing with lateral slides to the other side followed by another squat.
exercises.author: Insight

exercises.name: Wall Drills (Sprint Mechanics)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand facing a sturdy wall about one large step away.
• Place your hands firmly against the wall at shoulder height and lean your entire body forward at a 45-degree angle.
• Maintain a rigid straight line from your head down to your heels with your core firmly braced.

Execution:
• Drive one knee explosively up toward your chest until your thigh is parallel to the ground, keeping your ankle dorsiflexed (toes pulled up).
• Hold the posture to train single-leg hip stability, or alternate legs rhythmically in a marching or sprinting tempo (wall marches / switches).
• Drive through the ball of the stance foot while keeping your hips extended and spine neutral.
exercises.author: Insight

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Set a barbell in a rack at waist height (or use a Smith machine or suspension trainer).
• Lie supine underneath the bar and grasp it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
• Extend your legs with your heels on the ground, forming a straight rigid line from head to heels.

Execution:
• Pull your chest up to the bar by driving your elbows back and retracting your shoulder blades.
• Keep your glutes and core fully braced so your hips do not sag.
• Lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended before beginning the next rep.
exercises.author: Gavru

exercises.name: Tibialis Raises
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with your back leaning flat against a wall.
• Place your feet about one to two feet out in front of you with your legs straight and heels planted firmly on the floor.

Execution:
• Flex your ankles to lift your toes and the balls of your feet as high as possible toward your shins (dorsiflexion).
• Squeeze and hold the peak contraction in your tibialis anterior muscles for 1 to 2 seconds.
• Lower your feet back down slowly under control until they gently touch the floor before the next rep.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: Dragon Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and hands clasped in front of your chest for balance.
• Engage your core and keep your chest lifted.

Execution:
• Step one foot diagonally back behind your opposite leg, bending both knees into a deep cross-over squat (curtsy motion).
• Lower your hips until your front thigh is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your shoulders and hips facing forward.
• Drive through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie on your side on a fitness mat.
• Bend your bottom leg slightly at the knee for stability and keep your top leg completely straight and in line with your torso.
• Rest your head on your lower arm and place your top hand on the floor in front of you for balance.

Execution:
• Raise your top leg smoothly toward the ceiling while keeping your toes pointing forward or slightly downward.
• Keep your hips stacked vertically and prevent your pelvis from rolling backward.
• Squeeze your gluteus medius at the top for a brief pause, then slowly lower your leg back down with control.
exercises.author: wakanda90

exercises.name: Left-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Stand on the floor or on the edge of a step to increase the range of movement.
Raise one foot.
Lift your heel until you're standing on your toes.
(variable) Stay in this position for three seconds
Slowly lower your foot until you almost touch the ground with your heel - don't slam your foot!
exercises.author: wakanda90

exercises.name: Stationary Bike Cardio Session
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Adjust the stationary bike saddle height to hip level so that your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
• Position the handlebars so you can maintain a comfortable upright or slightly inclined posture without straining your neck.

Execution:
• Pedal smoothly with a steady cadence typically between 70 and 90 RPM.
• Adjust the resistance to achieve your target aerobic heart rate zone for the planned duration.
• Keep your upper body relaxed and stable on the saddle, avoiding rocking your hips from side to side.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Sitting on a bench, grab the dumbbell with your palms facing up
and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs
and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.
Perform the movement by
curling your palms and wrists towards your face.
(optional/variable) Pause at the top.
Slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.author: wakanda90

exercises.name: Scorpion Kick
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Begin in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
• Ensure your body forms a straight line from head to heels with core firmly braced.

Execution:
• Drive your right knee slightly toward your chest, then raise your bent right leg up and back behind you.
• Rotate your hips to swing your right foot across your left leg toward the floor on the opposite side.
• Keep your shoulders squared to the ground as much as possible to create a dynamic spinal rotation and hip stretch.
• Return smoothly to the starting plank position and repeat on the left leg.
exercises.author: lxmx

exercises.name: Prisoner Squat
exercises.description:
Stand upright with your chest slightly raised, your feet hip-width apart and your toes pointing straight ahead.
Bring your hands to the back of your head with your fingers slightly interlaced and your elbows pointing to the side. Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your upper body as upright as possible.
Push your knees outwards, they must never point towards each other. If your upper body moves slightly forward, make sure that it does not bend. Always keep your elbows level with your ears by tensing the muscles between your shoulder blades. If you are flexible enough, you can sink down until your buttocks touch your calves.
However, make sure that you do not bend your spine.
Before this happens, reverse the movement and use your heels and glutes to push yourself upwards with so much momentum that your feet lift off briefly and you do a little hop.
If necessary, correct the position of your feet, arms and upper body before you move on to the next repetition.
exercises.author: lxmx

exercises.name: Three-Point Push-Up
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Set up in a standard push-up position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart.
• Lift one foot approximately 5 to 10 cm off the floor so that your body is supported on three points.
• Keep your hips level and square to the ground with your core rigidly braced.

Execution:
• Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor in a smooth, controlled motion.
• Resist the rotational torque through your hips and maintain a straight line from your head to your supporting heel.
• Press firmly through your hands to return to the top position.
• Complete your repetitions and switch legs.
exercises.author: lxmx

exercises.name: Skydiver with Arms in T-Position
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie prone on your stomach on a mat with your legs wider than shoulder-width apart.
• Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height to form a T with your upper body.

Execution:
• Lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor simultaneously by contracting your entire posterior chain.
• Turn your thumbs toward the ceiling and squeeze your shoulder blades firmly together.
• While keeping your torso, arms, and thighs elevated in the air, adduct your legs together and then spread them open repeatedly.
• Lower back down with control upon completing the repetitions.
exercises.author: lxmx

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Hang from a pull-up bar using an overhand (pronated) grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
• Pull your knees tight into your chest in a tucked position and brace your entire core.

Execution:
• Pull down through straight arms using your lats, rear deltoids, and core to elevate your torso.
• Bring your torso parallel to the ground into a completely horizontal position while keeping your knees tucked.
• Hold this isometric position steady for the desired duration (e.g., 5 to 15 seconds).
• Lower yourself slowly and under full control back to a dead hang.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie prone face down on a mat with your legs straight and arms extended overhead in front of you.
• Keep your neck neutral and gaze pointed toward the floor.

Execution:
• Lift your arms and upper chest slightly off the floor by engaging your upper back muscles.
• Sweep your arms outward and downward in a wide arc along your sides until your hands approach your thighs, mimicking a snow angel motion.
• Retract and squeeze your shoulder blades firmly together at the bottom of the sweep.
• Slowly reverse the arc to return your arms overhead, keeping them elevated off the ground throughout.
exercises.author: mike6426

exercises.name: Hangboard Recruitment Pulls
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Position yourself underneath a climbing hangboard and choose a specific edge size.
• Grip the edge with one hand while keeping your feet supported on the ground or a small box.
• Set an open elbow angle of roughly 120 to 150 degrees (never hanging in complete elbow lockout).

Execution:
• Pull with maximum isometric effort upward for 3 to 5 seconds, recruiting maximum motor units in the fingers, forearm flexors, and back.
• Keep your shoulder engaged and locked into place throughout the pull.
• Rest adequately between attempts before repeating on the opposite arm.

exercises.name: Finger Push-Up
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Start in a plank position with your hands directly beneath your shoulders.
• Spread your fingers wide apart and place only your fingertips and thumbs firmly on the ground, lifting your palms off the floor.
• Maintain a rigid straight line from your head to your heels with your core firmly braced.

Execution:
• Slowly bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled motion.
• Maintain stability and solid arching tension in your fingertips without letting your finger joints collapse.
• Press through your fingertips and thumbs to straighten your arms, returning to the starting position.

exercises.name: Knee Push-Up
exercises.description:
Start by kneeling on the floor, keeping your knees together. Place your hands on the floor in front of you, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Make sure your body forms a straight line from head to knees. Hands should be positioned below shoulders.
Lower your torso towards the ground, bending your elbows while keeping your trunk stable. Keep your knees in contact with the floor.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position. Be sure to maintain contraction of chest, shoulder and arm muscles at the top of the movement.
Perform the desired number of repetitions, controlling the movement and maintaining good form.
exercises.author: PaukOne

exercises.name: Australian Pull-up
exercises.description:
Lie down under a high bar or suspension bar, positioned at an appropriate height.
Position yourself on your back under the bar, gripping the bar with a supinated grip (palms facing you).
Adjust your position so that your body is aligned straight from head to toe. Arms should be fully extended, shoulders stabilized, and legs aligned with the rest of the body.
Bend your elbows and pull your chest towards the bar, contracting your back muscles. Imagine you're trying to bring your shoulder blades together.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize muscle activation.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your elbows.
exercises.author: PaukOne

exercises.name: Claps Over the Head
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms resting naturally at your sides.
• Keep your chest lifted and shoulders relaxed.

Execution:
• Raise your extended arms out to the sides in a wide sweeping arc until your hands clap together directly overhead.
• Lower your arms back down smoothly along the same lateral path to the starting position.
• Repeat in a fluid, rhythmic cadence as a dynamic warm-up to activate the deltoids and mobilize the shoulder girdle.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Drag Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing forward.
• Let your arms hang in front of your thighs with shoulders back and chest up.

Execution:
• Drag the dumbbells vertically straight up along your torso by pulling your elbows backward.
• Lift the weights to chest level while keeping them as close to your body as possible to isolate the biceps.
• Squeeze your biceps firmly at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly along the same path back down.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wide Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
• Angle your forearms outward slightly wider than shoulder-width, keeping your elbows pinned lightly against your sides.

Execution:
• Curl the dumbbells upward along the angled path toward your outer shoulders, emphasizing the inner (short) head of the biceps.
• Squeeze your biceps firmly at the peak contraction for a brief pause.
• Slowly lower the dumbbells back down along the same path under full control.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl to Overhead Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms extended.
• Keep your core braced and shoulders pulled back.

Execution:
• Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by flexing your elbows.
• Smoothly transition by rotating your wrists outward and pressing the dumbbells directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
• Reverse the overhead press slowly back to shoulder level, then lower the dumbbells down through the eccentric curl to the starting position.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
• Let your arms hang straight down beneath your shoulders with an overhand (pronated) grip, palms facing back.

Execution:
• Row the dumbbells upward by flaring your elbows out wide to the sides at roughly a 90-degree angle to your torso.
• Pull until your upper arms are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your posterior deltoids and upper back.
• Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under control without rounding your spine.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand directly above your chest with arms extended.
• Use a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and press the dumbbells together so they touch firmly.

Execution:
• Lower the dumbbells toward the center of your chest while keeping them pressed together and tucking your elbows close to your torso.
• Press the dumbbells back upward by forcefully contracting your triceps and pectorals.
• Lock out your arms briefly at the top while maintaining continuous inward pressure between the dumbbells.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand or sit tall with your spine in a neutral alignment.
• Raise your left arm overhead, bend your elbow, and let your left hand drop behind your neck or between your shoulder blades.

Execution:
• Grasp your left elbow with your right hand and gently pull it backward and slightly down.
• Hold a gentle, comfortable stretch in your left triceps for 20 to 30 seconds.
• Breathe deeply and avoid overarching your lower back.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand or sit tall with your spine in a neutral alignment.
• Raise your right arm overhead, bend your elbow, and let your right hand drop behind your neck or between your shoulder blades.

Execution:
• Grasp your right elbow with your left hand and gently pull it backward and slightly down.
• Hold a gentle, comfortable stretch in your right triceps for 20 to 30 seconds.
• Breathe deeply and keep your core slightly braced to avoid overarching your lower back.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Standing Biceps Stretch (Left)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with your left side adjacent to a flat wall.
• Extend your left arm straight back and place your left palm flat against the wall at shoulder height, fingers pointing behind you.

Execution:
• Slowly rotate your torso and hips away from the wall to your right.
• Stop when you feel a comfortable stretch through your left biceps, anterior deltoid, and chest.
• Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing steadily.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Standing Biceps Stretch (Right)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with your right side adjacent to a flat wall.
• Extend your right arm straight back and place your right palm flat against the wall at shoulder height, fingers pointing behind you.

Execution:
• Slowly rotate your torso and hips away from the wall to your left.
• Stop when you feel a comfortable stretch through your right biceps, anterior deltoid, and chest.
• Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing steadily.
exercises.author: Lynn_McIntyre

exercises.name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Hip Thrust
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit on the floor with your upper back resting across the edge of a sturdy bench.
• Place a dumbbell securely across your hips and hold it in place with your hands.
• Plant one foot firmly on the floor (working leg) with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees, and lift the opposite leg off the ground with the knee bent.

Execution:
• Drive through the heel of your working leg to extend your hips upward until your torso and working thigh form a straight horizontal line.
• Squeeze your glute forcefully at the top of the movement for a 1 to 2-second pause.
• Lower your hips back down slowly under control without resting completely on the floor before the next rep.
• Complete all repetitions and switch sides.
exercises.author: carlos3c

exercises.name: Frog Stand
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Squat down with your feet close together and place your hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart with fingers spread wide.
• Place your knees against the outside of your elbows or rest them on the backs of your upper arms (triceps).

Execution:
• Slowly shift your body weight forward onto your hands.
• Lift your feet off the floor one at a time until you are balancing solely on your hands with bent elbows.
• Brace your core, press firmly into the floor through your fingertips, and gaze slightly forward to maintain balance.
• Hold this isometric position for the prescribed duration (e.g., 10 to 30 seconds), then lower your feet gently back to the ground.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand facing a wall roughly arm's length away and place your hands on the wall at shoulder height.
• Step one leg straight back into a staggered stance.

Execution:
• Keep your rear leg completely straight with your rear heel pressed firmly flat into the floor.
• Bend your front knee and gently lean your hips forward toward the wall until you feel a deep stretch in your rear calf (gastrocnemius).
• Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then switch legs.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Standing Soleus Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand facing a wall with your hands resting on the wall at chest height.
• Step one foot slightly back into a shorter staggered stance than a standard calf stretch.

Execution:
• Keep both heels flat on the floor and bend both knees simultaneously, focusing on bending the rear knee.
• Sink your hips downward to target the deeper soleus muscle located beneath the gastrocnemius, just above the Achilles tendon.
• Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds with steady breathing, then switch legs.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight out in front of you.
• Secure one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor in front of you and loop the other end around the ball and top of your foot.
• Move back until there is moderate tension on the band even when your foot is relaxed.

Execution:
• Pull your toes and the ball of your foot backward toward your shin against the band's resistance (dorsiflexion).
• Squeeze your tibialis anterior muscle at peak contraction for 1 to 2 seconds.
• Slowly allow your foot to extend forward under control, resisting the band's pull.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Exercise Band Plantarflexion
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you. Loop the center of a resistance band around the ball of your foot and hold both ends firmly with your hands to create tension.

Execution:
1. Press your foot forward and down against the band's resistance (plantarflexion), strongly contracting your calf muscles.
2. Hold the peak contraction briefly at the end of the movement.
3. Slowly return the foot back to the starting position under control.

Tips:
Keep your leg stationary and isolate movement entirely to the ankle joint. Excellent for calf strengthening and Achilles tendon rehabilitation.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Double Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. Rest your hands lightly against a wall or sturdy object if needed for balance.

Execution:
1. Press through the balls of both feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
2. Hold the peak contraction at the top for 1–2 seconds, squeezing your calves firmly.
3. Slowly lower your heels back to the floor with full control.

Tips:
Perform the repetitions smoothly without bouncing or relying on momentum. Builds ankle stability and calf strength.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Yoga exercise: Cow-cat
exercises.description: First get into the four-footed stance. The hands are underneath the shoulders. The fingers are fanned out wide and ensure a stable stance. It is best to rest your front body weight on your thumbs and index fingers. Now place your legs hip-width apart on the yoga mat. Your thighs should be vertically below your hips. Make sure that your weight is evenly distributed between your hands and knees. Your head is an extension of your spine and you are looking down at your mat. Your back is in a neutral position. Breathe in deeply and start with the cat. With the next exhalation, round your back vertebra by vertebra. Try to pull yourself as far as possible towards the ceiling. Pull your head towards your chest and tilt your pelvis. Now inhale deeply and move into the opposite position, cow pose. Bend your back down, pull your shoulders back slightly and lift your head as far as is comfortable for you. Your gaze is directed upwards. Breathe out consciously and switch back to the cat. With the next exhalation, switch back to cow. Repeat the exercise a few times and make sure that you are in the flow.
exercises.author: damnlost

exercises.name: Front Lever
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Hang from a sturdy pull-up bar using a shoulder-width overhand grip.

Execution:
1. Depress and retract your scapulae, engaging your lats, core, and glutes.
2. Pull your body upward with straight arms until your entire body is completely horizontal and parallel to the floor.
3. Hold this static hold for the target duration, maintaining a rigid straight line from head to heels.

Tips:
Keep arms and legs fully straight and do not allow your hips to sag. An advanced calisthenics isometric hold.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: TRX Rollout
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Kneel or stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the TRX handles with arms extended forward at chest height.

Execution:
1. Keeping your core braced and your body in a straight rigid line, lean forward and allow your arms to extend straight overhead.
2. Lower yourself forward under control to a point where you can still maintain tension without collapsing through your lower back.
3. Engage your abs and lats to pull your arms down, returning your body to the starting position.

Tips:
Keep your glutes and abs tight throughout to protect your lower back and prevent hyperextension.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: Ice Cream Maker
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin at the top of a chin-up or pull-up, holding the bar with arms bent and chest close to the bar.

Execution:
1. Push your torso backward using your shoulders and arms while keeping your core rigid, extending your arms until you reach a horizontal front lever position.
2. From the front lever position, pull your body back up in a smooth arc to the top of the pull-up position.
3. Repeat for repetitions in a controlled cadence.

Tips:
Demands high levels of lat strength and dynamic core control.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Front Lever Pull-up
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a horizontal front lever position (full or tuck variation) hanging below the pull-up bar with straight arms.

Execution:
1. Pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back.
2. Maintain strong core and lat engagement to keep your body strictly horizontal throughout the pull.
3. Lower yourself back down under control to the starting front lever position.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: TRX Knee Tuck to Elbow
exercises.description:
Place your feet in the stirrups and assume a high plank with your hands directly beneath your shoulders.
Pull your knees to your right elbow, then push them back out and to the centre.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: TRX Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Place the grips as if they were a continuation of the straps. We will position our arms stretched forward and our body leaning back, completely straight. The biceps muscles will activate as you bend your elbows to bring your body towards the straps. The contraction movement will end with a slight outward movement of the hands, due to the grip we are using.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: TRX Gorilla Biceps Curl
exercises.description: We'll stand facing the TRX straps and grab them with our fists facing each other, facing forward, with our arms fully extended at about shoulder-width apart. We'll keep our body straight, backward, as in the previous exercises, since we'll be lifting our body toward the TRX straps by activating our biceps. Our body will be straight, with our feet flat on the floor. This time, we'll place our arms open to the sides and at chest height. The movement we'll perform is a contraction toward our chest. To achieve this, we'll bend our elbows so that, by activating our biceps, we can pull our body toward the straps.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: TRX Single-Arm Biceps Curl
exercises.description: Step 1: Stand comfortably and grasp the handles of the suspension system. Step 2: Lean back resting your weight on one arm, keepng the spine neutral. Step 3: Slowly curl to pull your body weight to the up position. Supinate the arm and squeeze as you approach the end position. Step 4: Lower yourself back down and repeat.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: Back Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on the floor with your back resting on the floor and your legs bent, feet flat on the floor, leaving about 20 cm between your feet and your buttocks. Your hands remain flat on the floor, pressed against your ears, with your fingers pointing toward your toes. Your elbows are bent and pointing toward the ceiling. This is the starting position. Now push your hips as high as you can, raising your body off the floor, and continue pushing through your hands, extending your elbows and knees, until your back is fully arched (lumbar bridge). Your head also comes off the floor and should be level with your elbows, looking back. This is the final position. The descent should be slow and controlled. Your spine should be in a convex curve. It's not good to lift your back off the floor; it should remain straight. It should be well rounded. You'll also notice a feeling of increased oxygenation in your back. After lifting off the floor, your hips should be very high, even above the level of your head. Your arms and legs should remain straight. It seems easy, but it requires a good level of flexibility. Breathing should be deep. This posture stretches the rib cage and puts pressure on the diaphragm. If the posture is performed correctly, breathing will be perfect. Never hold your breath during the exercise.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: TRX Tricep Extension
exercises.description:
Attach the TRX or other suspension system overhead, having the handles hanging at chest level or slightly lower. Experiment to see what height allows you to set up in the best way.
Stand in front of the handles and grab them with your palms facing down.
Engage your abs, squeeze your glutes, take a breath and lean forward, lifting your heels off the floor. Keep your elbows straight.
Take another breath and lower yourself slowly by bending your elbows.
Go down until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle (to the point where your wrists are above your elbows). Hold the position for a moment.
Extend your arms by engaging your triceps and bring yourself to the starting position as you exhale.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: TRX Dips
exercises.description:
Start with the hands on the suspension trainer and feet on the ground.
Your hands should be under your shoulders with the feet slightly in front.
Lower yourself by bringing the hips between the handles and flexing the elbows.
Extend the elbows to come back to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.author: cynomops

exercises.name: Low Pulley Cable Fly
exercises.description:
Adjust the cable machine: Set the pulley to the lowest setting possible.
Choose your handles: You can use neutral grip handles (palms facing each other) or straight handles depending on your preference. Neutral grip might be easier on your wrists.
Stand with proper form: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and core engaged. Maintain a slight arch in your lower back throughout the exercise.
Grip the handles: Grab the handles with your chosen grip and step back a small step or two until there's slight tension on the cables.
Initiate the movement: Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the exercise. Imagine you're giving someone a big hug. Squeeze your chest muscles as you bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Control the movement: Focus on squeezing your chest muscles rather than using your arms to pull the handles.
Peak contraction: Briefly hold the squeeze at the top of the movement with your hands together at chest level.
Return slowly: Slowly release the tension and return the handles back down to the starting position with your arms slightly extended but not locked out.
exercises.author: FEFFO

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on a bench (either lengthwise or across the bench with only your upper back supported) with feet flat on the floor. Grasp a dumbbell with both hands forming a diamond grip under the inner weight plate, holding it directly over your chest with elbows slightly bent.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbows slightly bent and fixed throughout, slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in your lats and chest.
2. Pull the dumbbell back over your chest along the same arc, contracting your chest and lat muscles.
3. Pause briefly at the top and repeat.

Tips:
Do not turn the movement into a triceps extension by bending your elbows more. Keep your hips stable and avoid excessive arching in your lower back.
exercises.author: 3leh

exercises.name: Sitting Calf Stretch (Dorsiflexion)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit upright on the floor or an exercise mat with one leg extended straight in front of you.

Execution:
1. Flex your ankle to pull your toes back toward your shin (dorsiflexion).
2. Reach forward with your hand or loop a towel around the ball of your foot to gently deepen the calf and Achilles stretch.
3. Hold the stretch comfortably for 20–30 seconds while breathing smoothly.
4. Slowly release and repeat on the other side.

Tips:
Keep your knee straight without forcing it. A gentle, effective stretch for ankle mobility and calf rehab.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Plantarflexion Stretch with Band
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you. Loop a light resistance band over the top of your foot (instep), holding the ends to guide the stretch.

Execution:
1. Gently point your toes forward and downward (plantarflexion), creating a mild stretch along the front of your ankle and the tibialis anterior muscle.
2. Hold the stretch comfortably for 20–30 seconds.
3. Release slowly and switch to the other foot.
exercises.author: erikocobra

exercises.name: Biceps Close Grip Pull Down
exercises.description: On a lat pull down machine, hold the bar keeping your hands relatively close. Use an underhand grip (I.E.: the back of your hand must be facing the machine). Then pull down the bar in a straight line towards the ground. Make sure your biceps are the main drivers of the motion. You will probably feel your shoulders and lats working, but make sure your biceps are working more.
exercises.author: daniel.escada

exercises.name: Isometric Reverse-Grip Chin-Up Hold
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Grasp the pull-up bar with a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip and pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.

Execution:
1. Hold this top position statically with elbows fully flexed and tight to your sides.
2. Keep your lats, biceps, and core tightly engaged throughout the hold.
3. Lower yourself down slowly and under control once the target time is reached.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Incline Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description:
Set up an adjustable bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay on your stomach with your head hanging just above the edge of the bench.
Grab a dumbbell in each hand and set up with a good posture – core and lats engaged and shoulders neutral.
Row the dumbbells toward the top of the stomach and squeeze the back at the top of the rep.
Finally, lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat until all reps are completed.
exercises.author: carlos3c

exercises.name: Pseudo Planche Push-up
exercises.description: You should have the shoulder line in front of your wrists and perform a push-up, maintaining the shoulder in the same position. Keep your core braced and protract your shoulder blades at the top of each rep.
exercises.author: vdrb

exercises.name: Butt Kicks
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your core lightly engaged.

Execution:
1. Begin jogging in place or moving forward in a steady rhythm.
2. Flex your knees to kick your heels up toward your glutes with each stride.
3. Keep your thighs pointing mostly downward while pumping your arms naturally.

Tips:
Great dynamic warm-up exercise for activating the hamstrings and calves before intense lower-body work.
exercises.author: painDpice

exercises.name: Plank Tuck Jump
exercises.description:
Start in a plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core to keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
From this position, bend your knees slightly and jump with both feet inward, bringing them as close to your core as possible
As soon as your feet touch the ground, push off forcefully to jump again and return to the starting plank position.
Continue repeating this jumping motion, maintaining control and core stability throughout the exercise.
Make sure to keep your breathing steady while jumping, breathing deeply and controlling your breathing.
Keep your gaze fixed on the ground to maintain proper spinal alignment.
Repeat the jumps for the desired length of time or the number of repetitions recommended for your workout program.
To finish the exercise, rest by releasing the plank position, then stretch if necessary to loosen your muscles.
exercises.author: painDpice

exercises.name: Reach-up
exercises.description: To perform this exercise, lie on your back with your arms extended overhead. Then, contract your abdominals and lift your torso off the floor while reaching your arms toward the ceiling to "reach" as high as possible. Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the movement. Reach ups strengthen the abdominal muscles and improve the flexibility of the spine. They can be incorporated into a variety of training routines to work on core strength and stability.
exercises.author: painDpice

exercises.name: Dynamic Side Plank
exercises.description: The dynamic side plank involves positioning yourself on your side, supported on one elbow and the side of your foot, then dipping your hips up and down while keeping your body in a straight line.
exercises.author: painDpice

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curls
exercises.description: Seated Dumbbell Curls are an effective bicep workout that isolates the muscles by stabilizing the upper body, reducing momentum that can detract from the exercise’s effectiveness. This exercise is performed sitting down with a dumbbell in each hand, focusing on controlled movement to maximize engagement of the bicep muscles.
exercises.author: sTiKyt

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Barbell Curls
exercises.description:
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) approximately shoulder-width apart. Ensure your back is straight, shoulders slightly pulled back, and arms fully extended.
Curl the barbell upwards towards your chest in a controlled motion, keeping your elbows close to your body. The motion should be smooth without any swinging or momentum use.
Once the barbell is at chest level, pause briefly to maximize contraction in the biceps and forearms.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with a controlled movement, fully extending your arms.
exercises.author: sTiKyt

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Hang from a pull-up bar using a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip, with your palms facing towards you and arms fully extended.

Execution:
1. Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
2. Squeeze your lats and biceps firmly at the top of the movement.
3. Lower yourself down slowly and under complete control back to the starting dead hang.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a push-up position with your feet spread wide for balance. Place your supporting hand on the floor directly beneath your chest, and rest your free arm on your lower back.

Execution:
1. Bend your supporting elbow to lower your chest toward the floor with steady control.
2. Keep your core and glutes firmly braced to minimize torso rotation.
3. Press firmly through your palm to return to the starting plank position. Complete all reps on one side before switching arms.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hamstring Curl
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie on your back on a mat. Place the heel of one leg on the floor (or on a slider/towel) with the knee slightly bent, while holding the other leg elevated off the ground.

Execution:
1. Lift your hips off the mat into a single-leg bridge position.
2. Curl your heel toward your glutes by flexing at the knee, strongly contracting the hamstrings.
3. Slowly extend your leg back out under control while keeping your hips elevated.

Tips:
Effectively isolates and strengthens the hamstring group (biceps femoris, semimembranosus, semitendinosus) unilaterally using only bodyweight.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Low-Cable Crossover
exercises.description: The low-cable cross-over is an isolation movement that uses a cable stack to target the upper portion of the pectoral muscles. It is common in upper-body and chest-focused muscle-building workouts, often in combination with presses or flyes from other angles to target all portions of the chest.
exercises.author: JackSparrow

exercises.name: High-Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
The high-cable cross tricep extension is an isolation exercise for targeting the triceps,
particularly the long head. It utilizes cables and handles grasped with opposite hands, allowing for a unique pressing motion that can be effective for building tricep strength. Unlike exercises that use a straight bar or rope, this variation can be more comfortable on your wrists and elbows
exercises.author: JackSparrow

exercises.name: JM Press
exercises.description: The JM press keeps your shoulders stationary, relying on the elbow flexion and extension to move the weight using your triceps strength. That means you get all the benefits of the best triceps-strengthening exercises without overtaxing that delicate shoulder joint. Classic win-win!
exercises.author: Epiphany8424

exercises.name: Helms Row
exercises.description:
Setup: Place your chest on the end of a bench, using a towel or anything soft to keep your chest protected. You want your chest to be in contact with the bench around the nipple line. Your back should be almost parallel to the floor
Execution: When you’re starting the exercise, focus on pulling your elbows back until you feel maximum tightness in the lats.
If you want to get some trap activation with the exercise, relax your shoulder blades when the weights are hanging down and then retract them as you start the rep.
exercises.author: carlos3c

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.description: The Meadows row is a unilateral row performed with a landmine setup, overhand grip, and staggered stance. Lean your torso forward and grip the barbell. Rest the other forearm on the forward leg. Start this movement by driving the elbow behind you while retracting the shoulder-blade. Keep the working shoulder down. Pull toward your back hip until the elbow is level with your torso.
exercises.author: carlos3c

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description:
The plank is a bodyweight exercise. As a multi-functional movement, the plank not only targets your abdominal muscles but also the spine and hip. Plank strengthens and tightens your entire body, improves your posture and balance, reduces body fat, and can help boost your metabolism.
Exercises such as the “plank pose” help strengthen the stamina of stabilizing abdominal muscles. It can also help relieve back pain associated with a weakening of the function of the stabilizing muscles of the body.
Planks are a versatile exercise that targets many of the most important muscle groups in the body, so they can be applied by anyone to improve endurance and overall body strength.
exercises.author: hektkaso

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description:
Squat is a type of bodyweight exercise. It is one of the most popular exercises for strength and muscle growth. Squat is particularly effective for focusing on the muscles of the leg and hips.
Squat are an easy exercise for beginners to do. It can help strengthen leg muscles, tighten hip muscles and burn calories to lose weight.
It tightens the butt and legs. Squats are very effective for firming and strengthening your legs by acting on the gluteus,hip flexors, quadriceps, hamstrings and inner thigh muscles. Also, bodyweight squats can help shape your glutes and butt.
exercises.author: admin

exercises.name: Jumping Jack
exercises.description:
Jumping jack are a plyometric exercise. Plyometrics are explosive aerobic moves that increase speed, quickness, and power and they work your whole body.
Jumping jack target the arm, shoulder, abdominal muscles, hip muscles and hip flexors and also work on the thighs, knee tendons and quadriceps.
Jumps are beneficial to your health because they combine cardiovascular conditioning with strength work. Since jumps elevate your heart rate, they can also improve your cardiovascular fitness.
exercises.author: hektkaso

exercises.name: High Knee Skips
exercises.description:
You can use this exercise both as a dynamic warm-up before training and add it to your cardio training routine to burn fat.
High knee skips are a plyometric exercise. Plyometrics are explosive aerobic moves that increase speed, quickness, and power and they work your whole body.
High knee skips target the oblique, leg muscles, hip muscles and hip flexors and also work on the thighs, knee tendons, quadriceps and shoulders.
Jumps are beneficial to your health because they combine cardiovascular conditioning with strength work. Since jumps elevate your heart rate, they can also improve your cardiovascular fitness.
exercises.author: hektkaso

exercises.name: Bench Dips On Floor
exercises.description:
Triceps dips on floor are a compound exercise as they worked multiple muscle groups simultaneously. Although this bodyweight exercise mainly targets the triceps, it also hits your chest and front of your shoulder.
Triceps dips on floor are one of the most effective exercises to increase arm strength and also build lean muscle in your upper arms.
Triceps dips on floor are a closed kinetic chain exercise and express that you do the movements around a fixed point. It increases compression force on your joints thereby improving stability.
exercises.author: hektkaso

exercises.name: Bodyweight Lunge
exercises.description:
Bodyweight lunges are an effective calisthenic exercise for
strengthening the lower body, improving balance and stability, and
developing functional strength. They are a popular choice for bodyweight workouts, home workouts, and can also be included as part of a larger strength training routine.
exercises.author: hektkaso

exercises.name: Lateral Push Off
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin in an athletic, balanced stance with your knees slightly bent and core engaged.

Execution:
1. Push off explosively from your planted leg in a lateral direction.
2. Land softly on the opposite leg, absorbing the impact through your knee and hip.
3. Regain your balance briefly and push off back to the other side.
exercises.author: cleen

exercises.name: Underhand Dumbbell Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs or the bench edge, with your wrists extending just past your knees. Hold dumbbells with an underhand (palms up) grip.

Execution:
1. Slowly lower the dumbbells as far as comfortably possible by extending your wrists downward.
2. Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your wrists, contracting your wrist flexors firmly at the top.
3. Lower the weights back down slowly with full control.

Tips:
Isolate movement entirely to the wrists. Avoid using arm or body momentum.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit upright on a bench or stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell with both hands overhead, with arms extended.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows pointed forward close to your head, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
2. Lower until your triceps are fully stretched.
3. Press the dumbbell back up overhead by extending your elbows, squeezing the triceps at the top.

Tips:
Keep your elbows fixed in place throughout and avoid overarching your lower back.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with an overhand grip (palms facing your body).

Execution:
1. Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells forward and upward until they reach shoulder or eye level.
2. Pause briefly at the top to emphasize contraction in the front deltoids.
3. Lower the weights slowly and with control back to your thighs.

Tips:
Avoid swinging your torso or using leg momentum. Keep your core braced throughout the lift.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Position yourself face down on the Roman chair / hyperextension bench with your thighs resting on the pads and hips free to hinge. Lock your heels securely under the foot pads. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands lightly by your ears.

Movement:
Slowly hinge at the hips to lower your torso toward the floor, keeping your spine neutral. Lift your upper body by contracting your erector spinae, glutes, and hamstrings until your body forms a straight line from heels to head.

Notes:
Avoid hyperextending your lower back at the top of the movement. Maintain a controlled tempo without using momentum.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hex Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor. Hold a pair of dumbbells (hexagonal dumbbells work best) with a neutral grip, pressing them firmly together directly over your chest.

Movement:
Maintain continuous inward pressure pressing the two dumbbells against each other as you lower them with control toward the center of your chest. Press them back up to arm's length, keeping constant tension on your pecs.

Notes:
Do not let the dumbbells separate at any point during the movement. The constant inward squeeze maximizes chest activation throughout the entire range of motion.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, two kettlebells positioned between or slightly in front of your feet. Hinge at your hips with a flat back and grip the handles.

Movement:
1. Clean: Explosively drive your hips forward to propel the kettlebells upward, keeping them close to your body and catching them smoothly in the rack position at chest level.
2. Press: Brace your core and glutes, then press both kettlebells overhead until your elbows are fully locked out.
3. Lower the kettlebells with control back into the rack position, then swing them back down between your legs.

Notes:
Do not lean back or arch your lower back during the overhead press. Ensure a solid core brace throughout the entire lift.
exercises.author: m4k3r

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Clean two kettlebells into the rack position at chest level: elbows tucked close to your ribcage, wrists neutral, and kettlebell bells resting in the triangle formed by your forearms and biceps. Set your feet shoulder-width apart.

Movement:
Inhale and brace your core firmly. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to squat down deeply, keeping your torso as upright as possible. Drive through your midfoot and heels to return to a full standing position.

Notes:
Keep your chest tall and elbows elevated throughout the movement to prevent the weight from rounding your upper back forward.
