exercises.author: m4k3r

exercises.name: Foam Rolling (Blackroll)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place the foam roller on an exercise mat and position the target muscle group (such as the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, upper back, or calves) across the roller. Support your body weight with your hands and feet to regulate pressure.

Movement:
Roll slowly and deliberately back and forth across the muscle tissue. When you encounter a tender trigger point, pause on that spot for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply until the tension releases.

Notes:
Avoid rolling directly over bones, joints, or your lower back (lumbar spine). Keep the movement controlled without using momentum.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms extended. Step one foot forward into a split stance with feet hip-width apart for balance. Keep your front foot flat and the rear heel elevated.

Movement:
Lower your hips straight down toward the floor by bending both knees until your back knee almost touches the ground and your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor. Drive through the heel of the front foot to return to the starting upright position without moving your feet.

Notes:
Keep your torso upright and core engaged throughout. Complete all repetitions on one leg before switching sides.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs or at your sides. Keep your shoulders back, chest proud, and knees slightly soft.

Movement:
Hinge at your hips by pushing your glutes backward, allowing your torso to lean forward while keeping your spine straight and neutral. Lower the dumbbells close to your shins until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings. Drive through your heels and extend your hips to return to the standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top.

Notes:
Do not round your lower back. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs throughout the entire movement.
exercises.author: Anastasious

exercises.name: Assisted Triceps Dips (Machine)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Select the appropriate counterweight on the assisted dip machine (higher weight provides more assistance). Grasp the parallel handles, place your knees or feet onto the support platform, and press yourself up until your arms are nearly fully extended.

Movement:
Lower your body with control by bending your elbows back until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor (approximately 90-degree elbow bend). Press through your palms and contract your triceps to push yourself back up to the starting position.

Notes:
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso to emphasize the triceps rather than the chest. Do not lock out your elbows harshly at the top.
exercises.author: matpn

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand facing a sturdy plyometric box at a comfortable distance of about one to two feet. Set your feet shoulder-width apart with arms relaxed at your sides.

Movement:
1. Swing your arms back and quickly hinge into a quarter squat to load your hips and legs.
2. Explosively jump upward and forward by driving through your hips, knees, and ankles while swinging your arms forward and up.
3. Land softly on top of the box with both feet absorbing the impact in a partial squat.
4. Stand tall to complete hip and knee extension, then carefully step down one foot at a time.

Notes:
Do not jump down backwards from the box, as this places unnecessary stress on the Achilles tendons and knees.
exercises.author: tekknokrat

exercises.name: Rotary Torso Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the rotary torso machine and adjust the chest and knee pads so your lower body is comfortably locked in place. Grasp the handles and sit upright with a straight spine.

Movement:
Rotate your torso to one side using the strength of your obliques. Pause momentarily at the end of the range of motion while maintaining peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position against the weight stack resistance.

Notes:
Choose a moderate weight to ensure smooth rotational control. Avoid wrenching or using momentum from your shoulders or arms.
exercises.author: 6LXBO

exercises.name: Barbell Calf Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Position a barbell across your upper traps as you would for a back squat. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, optionally placing the balls of your feet on a calf block or weight plate for a greater stretch.

Movement:
Drive through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, achieving a peak contraction in your calves. Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your heels with control until you feel a gentle stretch in the calf muscles.

Notes:
Keep your knees slightly soft but stationary throughout the movement. Avoid bouncing at the bottom or using momentum from your hips.
exercises.author: pera_perkan

exercises.name: Standing Torso Twist
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly soft. Keep your hips facing forward and place your hands across your chest or behind your head.

Movement:
Rotate your torso smoothly to one side by engaging your obliques, keeping your hips and lower body stable. Pause briefly at the end range of motion, return to the center, and rotate to the opposite side in a controlled, rhythmic tempo.

Notes:
Do not forcefully twist through the lumbar spine; initiate the rotation through the thoracic spine and ribcage. Keep your hips stationary throughout.
exercises.author: brucem

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand beside a low cable pulley with the attachment set to the lowest position. Grasp the single D-handle with the hand furthest from the machine (cable running behind or in front of your body). Grip the upright pillar with your inside hand for stability and lean slightly outward.

Movement:
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your working elbow, raise your arm outward in a wide lateral arc until your hand is roughly level with your shoulder. Pause briefly at peak contraction in the lateral deltoid, then lower the handle slowly under continuous tension back to the starting position.

Notes:
Do not shrug your traps or swing your torso to initiate the pull. Maintain constant control throughout both the lifting and lowering phases.
exercises.author: carlos3c

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Hold a resistance band with both hands about shoulder-width apart straight out in front of your chest, arms extended with elbows slightly unlocked and palms facing downward or facing each other.

Movement:
Pull the band apart by moving your hands outward and backward horizontally, squeezing your shoulder blades firmly together until the band touches your chest. Pause briefly in peak contraction, then slowly return your arms forward to the starting position under control.

Notes:
Do not shrug your shoulders toward your ears or arch your lower back. Keep the movement smooth and continuous.
exercises.author: schwolfar

exercises.name: Machine Upper Back Row
exercises.description: Upper Back is suitable for building up the core muscles with a special focus on the deltoid and rhomboid muscles and the upper back muscles
exercises.author: phpi

exercises.name: Pullover Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the pullover machine and adjust the seat height so your shoulder joints align with the machine's axis of rotation. Place your elbows securely on the padded levers and lightly grasp the handles. Fasten the lap belt if available.

Movement:
Drive your elbows downward in a smooth, sweeping arc toward your thighs, focusing on pulling with your latissimus dorsi. Squeeze your lats firmly at the bottom of the movement, then slowly allow the pads to rise back up to achieve a deep stretch in your back.

Notes:
Initiate and power the movement through your elbows rather than pulling with your hands. Keep your lower back supported against the backrest.
exercises.author: Paul@Chemistry

exercises.name: Hamstring Kicks
exercises.description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and extend one arm in front of you. Swing that leg up in front of you and back down while keeping your leg as straight as possible and your toes pointed up.Repeat with the other leg.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.description:
Stand upright and hold weights in both hands if using loads.
Brace your core and lift one leg off the ground.
Keep your back straight, hinge at the hips while lowering your torso forward, ensuring you don’t rotate your hips.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your standing leg's hamstring, then return to standing position. Repeat on both sides.
exercises.author: admin

exercises.name: Toe Touch
exercises.description: Stand with your feet closer together. Hinge at your hips and lower your upper body towards your toes. Reach your hands towards your feet, try to touch your toes, the ground, or as far down your legs as you can comfortably go.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Elephant Walks
exercises.description: Hinge at your hips until you feel a stretch behind your knees. Bend one leg while the other is straight then fluidly bend the other knee while straightening the first knee.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Bodyweight Good Morning
exercises.description: Stand with your feet more than shoulder-width apart (wider stance) and place your hands on your hips. Hinge at your hips and lower your upper body towards the ground while keeping your back straight then come back up.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Single Leg Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Sit on the ground with one leg straight out in front of you and the other leg bent in toward you. Reach forward with both hands, trying to touch the toes of your straight leg.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Sit & Reach
exercises.description: Sit on the ground with your legs extended straight in front of you. Reach both hands forward, trying to reach past your toes or as far as you can go. Return to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Crossbody Leg Swings
exercises.description: Hold onto a wall or something near you for support. Swing one leg across the front of your body, then back and out to the side. Repeat while slowly increasing your range of motion.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Standing Pancake
exercises.description: Stand and open your legs as wide as possible into a straddle position. Then bend at the hips, pushing them back while keeping your back straight.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Standing Pancake Good Morning
exercises.description: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward. Place your hands on the back of your head. Hinge at your hips and lower your upper body towards the ground, keeping your back straight and chest open.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Choke Stretch
exercises.description: Sit on the ground and bend one leg, bringing your knee toward you. Place your hand behind your hamstring and gently pull your leg toward your chest, feeling a stretch in the back of your thigh. Straighten your leg, extending up toward the ceiling.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Roll Down
exercises.description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and slowly roll your upper body forward, one vertebra at a time, until your hands touch the ground or as far as you can comfortably go. Roll back up to the starting position in the same controlled manner.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Crossbody Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: While standing, cross one leg behind the other (keep this leg straight). Reach downward and try to touch the toes of that leg. Slightly bend the other leg so that you can bend down.
exercises.author: captive0592

exercises.name: Plank-to-Elbow Extension (Plank to Push-Up)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly beneath your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, and your body forming a straight, rigid line from head to heels.

Movement:
Place one hand flat on the floor beneath your shoulder and press up, followed immediately by the other hand, bringing yourself into a full high plank (push-up position). Lower yourself back down onto your forearms one arm at a time. Alternate your leading arm with each repetition.

Notes:
Keep your core braced tightly to prevent your hips from swaying from side to side. Avoid arching your lower back.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Cossack squat
exercises.description: The Cossack Squat is a multi-joint exercise that works mainly on the legs and buttocks, but also involves stabilizing muscles. It is an excellent exercise for improving strength, mobility and stability in a functional way.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Wall-sit
exercises.description: The Wall Sit (or wall chair) is an isometric exercise that mainly involves the leg muscles, improving muscular endurance and stability. Here are the main and secondary muscles activated during the exercise.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Dragon-flag
exercises.description:
Keep your body completely rigid throughout the movement, avoiding sagging in your lower back.
Use a firm grip to stabilize your upper body.
Start with simpler versions (such as with bent knees) to build strength and control.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Plank with Alternating Leg Lift
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin in a standard forearm plank with elbows directly beneath your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, and your body forming a rigid, straight line from head to heels.

Movement:
Keeping your leg straight, contract your glutes and lift one foot a few inches off the floor with control. Hold briefly at the top without shifting your weight excessively, then lower your foot back to the floor. Repeat on the opposite leg, alternating sides.

Notes:
Do not allow your hips to rotate, pike upward, or sag toward the floor. Maintain a strong core brace throughout.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Heel Touches
exercises.description:
Starting Position:

Lie on your back on an exercise mat.
Bend your knees, keeping your feet flat on the floor and hip-width apart.
Place your arms along your sides, palms facing inward, just off the floor.



Engage Core:

Lift your head, shoulders, and upper back slightly off the ground.
Keep your neck neutral and chin slightly tucked.



Perform the Movement:

Side-bend to the right, reaching your right hand toward your right heel.
Return to the center, then side-bend to the left, reaching your left hand toward your left heel.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled manner.



Breathing:

Exhale as you reach toward your heel and inhale as you return to the center.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: Bicycle crunches are a core exercise performed on the floor. Lie on your back with your hands behind your head and legs extended. Lift your shoulders off the ground, bring one knee toward your chest, and twist your torso so your opposite elbow meets the knee. Alternate sides in a pedaling motion, ensuring controlled movements and engaging your core throughout the exercise.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Machine Hack Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Position yourself in the hack squat machine with your back and head flat against the backrest and your shoulders tucked under the shoulder pads. Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the center or upper half of the footplate. Disengage the safety handles.

Movement:
Lower the sled under control by bending your knees until your thighs are at least parallel to the footplate (or deeper according to your mobility). Press forcefully through your midfoot and heels to drive the sled back up to the starting position without violently locking out your knees.

Notes:
Keep your lower back firmly supported against the backrest throughout the entire movement. Do not allow your heels to rise off the footplate.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Dumbbell Crunch
exercises.description: Dumbbell crunches are a weighted variation of traditional crunches designed to target the abdominal muscles more intensely. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest or above your head. Lift your shoulders and upper back off the ground in a crunching motion, engaging your core. Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position. Ensure controlled movements throughout the exercise to prevent strain.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Biceps Curl Machine
exercises.description: The biceps curl machine is designed to isolate the biceps muscles and provide a controlled range of motion. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so your arms are aligned with the machine's handles or pads. Grip the handles firmly, keeping your elbows fixed in place, and curl the handles upward by contracting your biceps. Slowly lower the handles to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Toe Taps
exercises.description: Toe taps are a core-focused exercise performed lying on your back. Lie flat with your arms by your sides and your legs raised to a tabletop position (knees bent at 90 degrees). Slowly lower one foot to gently tap the floor, keeping your core engaged and your lower back pressed into the ground. Return to the starting position and alternate legs. This exercise strengthens the core while minimizing strain on the lower back.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Standing Side Crunches
exercises.description: Standing side crunches are a dynamic exercise that targets the obliques while improving balance and stability. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands behind your head or holding a dumbbell in one hand. Lean your torso to one side, contracting your obliques, while bringing your elbow toward your hip (or crunching toward the weight if using a dumbbell). Return to the starting position and alternate sides or perform all repetitions on one side before switching.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Rotations
exercises.description:
Dumbbell shoulder rotations are designed to strengthen the rotator cuff muscles and improve shoulder stability and mobility.

External Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping your elbow stationary. Slowly return to the starting position.
Internal Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm inward, toward your body, and slowly return to the starting position. Perform the exercise with controlled movements to avoid strain.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Hold
exercises.description: The plate pinch hold is a grip strength exercise designed to target the forearms and improve grip endurance. Select one or two weight plates (smooth-edged plates work best) and pinch them together between your thumb and fingers. Hold the plates with your arm straight down by your side or extended slightly in front of you. Maintain the hold for as long as you can, keeping your shoulders relaxed and your grip firm. This exercise can be done for time or repetitions.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Band Reverse Wood Chops
exercises.description:
Attach a looping resistance band to a rack below knee height
Grip the other end of the band like holding a baseball bat with both hands
Stretch the band facing it
Start with your hands at the side of your hips, knees bent
Rotate your hips while moving your hands towards over the top of your opposite shoulder
Imagine the motion as striking a baseball with a bat
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Lat Pull
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hinge forward at your hips to about a 45-degree angle while maintaining a flat, neutral spine. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended downward and elbows slightly unlocked.

Movement:
Pull the dumbbells back in a sweeping arc toward your hips, keeping your arms relatively straight with only a slight bend at the elbows. Squeeze your lats firmly at the top of the contraction, then lower the dumbbells back down under control.

Notes:
Avoid turning this into a standard row; keep the elbow bend fixed to emphasize the lats, teres major, and rear deltoids.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Hang from a pull-up bar using an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width (dead hang). Arms are fully extended, core engaged, and shoulders relaxed upward near your ears.

Movement:
Depress and retract your shoulder blades by pulling them down and together, lifting your body upward a few inches without bending your elbows. Hold the top contracted position for 1 to 2 seconds, then slowly lower yourself back into the full dead hang.

Notes:
Keep your arms completely straight throughout the entire movement. The motion is generated purely by scapular movement and back engagement.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Barbell Pin Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place a flat bench inside a power rack and set the safety pins at the desired height (typically your sticking point, a few inches above your chest). Lie on the bench, grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, and position yourself with feet planted firmly on the floor.

Movement:
Lower the barbell under control until it comes to a complete rest on the safety pins. Pause on the pins for 1 to 2 seconds while maintaining full upper-body tightness, then explosively press the bar upward back to arm's length without bouncing off the pins.

Notes:
Do not lose muscular tension while the barbell rests on the pins. Developing dead-stop pressing power strengthens sticking points and starting strength.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Barbell Pin Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set the safety pins in a power rack at your desired depth (such as parallel or just above your sticking point). Unrack the barbell onto your upper back and take your standard squat stance with core braced.

Movement:
Descend under control into a squat until the barbell comes to rest gently on the safety pins. Pause completely on the pins for 1 to 2 seconds while maintaining full torso and leg tightness, then drive forcefully through your midfoot and heels back to a standing position.

Notes:
Do not collapse or lose core tightness while the bar is resting on the pins. Dead-stop squats build immense starting power and stability out of the hole.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Barbell Clean
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with feet hip-width apart over the barbell with your shins close to the bar. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your knees using a hook grip. Keep your back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.

Movement:
1. First pull: Drive through the floor with your legs to lift the bar smoothly past your knees, maintaining a constant torso angle.
2. Second pull: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) while shrugging your shoulders to propel the barbell upward close to your torso.
3. Turnover and catch: Rapidly pull yourself under the bar, rotating your elbows forward and up to catch the barbell on your front deltoids in a front squat position, then stand up to complete the lift.

Notes:
Keep the barbell close to your body throughout the entire pull. Fast elbow turnover ensures a safe and stable rack position.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Barbell Pin Overhead Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set the safety pins in a power rack at chin height and place the barbell on top. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip, and brace your entire body.

Movement:
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Press the bar explosively off the pins overhead to full elbow lockout, tilting your head back slightly as the bar passes your face. Lower the barbell under control back onto the pins, let it come to a complete stop for a brief moment while holding core tension, then repeat.

Notes:
Starting from a dead stop eliminates elastic momentum, developing pure concentric pressing strength in the anterior deltoids and triceps.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and rack the barbell securely across your front deltoids and clavicles (front rack position).
• Keep your elbows pointing slightly forward and your core braced tightly.

Execution:
• Dip by bending your knees a few inches vertically while keeping your torso strictly upright.
• Explosively extend your knees and hips, using leg drive to propel the barbell upward off your shoulders.
• Finish the movement with your arms, locking out the barbell overhead with straight arms directly above the crown of your head.
• Lower the barbell with control back to the front rack position.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit back on an incline bench adjusted to a high angle (around 60° to 75°), pressing your back firmly against the pad.
• Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward or slightly angled inward.

Execution:
• Press the dumbbells upward overhead in a smooth, controlled arc until your arms are fully extended without locking out forcefully.
• Lower the dumbbells with control back to shoulder level until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, feeling a good stretch in the front deltoids.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Kreis Press with Dumbbells
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit on an incline bench set to approximately a 45-degree angle.
• Hold two dumbbells overhead with arms extended.

Execution:
• Lower the dumbbells outward and down along a circular path until they reach shoulder height.
• Reverse the arc and press the dumbbells back overhead in a smooth circular trajectory.
• Keep tension constant on the front and lateral deltoids throughout the movement without using momentum.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral and Front Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a pair of dumbbells at your sides with elbows slightly bent.

Execution:
• Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until they reach shoulder height (lateral raise).
• Keeping arms at shoulder level, sweep them forward horizontally until the dumbbells meet in front of your chest.
• Slowly lower the dumbbells straight down in front of your thighs.
• Reverse the sequence on alternating reps by raising to the front first, sweeping outward to the sides, and lowering down.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Olympic Jerk
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Rest the barbell securely in the front rack position on your collarbones and front deltoids.
• Stand with feet hip-width apart, spine completely neutral and core braced firmly.

Execution:
• Dip straight down by bending your knees a few inches, keeping your torso strictly vertical.
• Drive explosively upward through your legs, transferring momentum directly to the barbell.
• Drop rapidly under the bar, catching it with arms fully locked out overhead, typically in a split stance (Split Jerk).
• Recover by stepping the front foot halfway back, then the rear foot forward until feet are parallel, maintaining the bar overhead before lowering.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Olympic Clean and Jerk
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand over the barbell with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width (hook grip recommended).
• Keep your spine neutral, hips back, and chest tall.

Execution:
1. Clean: Pull the bar from the floor, extend hips and knees explosively upon passing the thighs, and rapidly pull yourself underneath the bar to catch it in a deep front squat. Stand up fully to finish the clean.
2. Jerk: With the bar in front rack, dip vertically at the knees and drive upward explosively. Drop under the bar into a split stance, locking your arms out overhead.
3. Recovery: Step the front foot halfway back and rear foot forward until feet are aligned parallel, keeping the bar securely locked overhead.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Olympic Snatch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Approach the barbell with a hip-width stance and take a wide grip (snatch hook grip).
• Keep your back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly ahead of the bar.

Execution:
• Lift the bar smoothly off the floor, keeping it tight to your shins and thighs.
• At the hip crease, explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) to accelerate the bar upward.
• Rapidly drop underneath the bar into a full overhead squat, catching the bar with fully locked arms overhead.
• Stabilize and stand up completely while maintaining the barbell locked out directly over your center of gravity.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Seated W-Curl with Dumbbells
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Sit back on an incline bench set to approximately a 60-degree angle.
• Allow your arms to hang naturally at your sides with palms turned outward away from your torso.

Execution:
• Curl the dumbbells upward and slightly outward, forming a 'W' shape with your arms at peak contraction.
• Squeeze your biceps (especially the short head) hard at the top without swinging your elbows forward.
• Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under control to a full stretch.
exercises.author: M9

exercises.name: Stair Climber (ClimbMill)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Step onto the rotating stairs of the ClimbMill machine and maintain an upright posture.
• Lightly place your hands on the handrails for balance without leaning your upper body weight onto them.

Execution:
• Step smoothly and deliberately from one rotating step to the next, placing your entire foot on each step.
• Keep your chest lifted, shoulders back, and core engaged throughout.
• Adjust the stair speed to match your cardio conditioning level.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Cobra Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie prone (face down) on a mat with your legs extended straight behind you, tops of your feet flat on the floor.
• Place your hands flat on the mat directly beneath or slightly in front of your shoulders, keeping elbows tucked close to your ribcage.

Execution:
• Press gently into your palms to lift your chest and torso off the floor while keeping your pelvis and hips pressed firmly against the mat.
• Roll your shoulders down and back away from your ears to lengthen through your cervical spine and open your chest.
• Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply and steadily.
• Slowly lower your chest back down to the floor under control.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Torso Rotation Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft, or sit tall on a bench or mat.
• Place your hands on your hips or cross your arms comfortably across your chest.

Execution:
• Slowly rotate your upper body to one side, keeping your hips and pelvis facing squarely forward.
• Hold the stretch across your torso and thoracic spine for 15 to 30 seconds while breathing normally.
• Return smoothly to center and rotate to the opposite side.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with legs extended and head relaxed.

Execution:
• Bend one knee and grasp your shin or behind your thigh with both hands.
• Gently pull your knee toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your glutes and lower back.
• Keep your opposite leg relaxed and extended flat along the floor.
• Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathe steadily, and repeat on the opposite leg. Can also be performed pulling both knees simultaneously.
exercises.author: hpmbala

exercises.name: Towel Superman
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight behind you.
• Hold a small towel taut between both hands, with arms extended out in front of you shoulder-width apart.

Execution:
• Simultaneously raise your chest, arms, and legs slightly off the floor by engaging your lower back, glutes, and upper back.
• While keeping the towel pulled tight, bend your elbows and pull the towel into your upper chest like a lat pulldown.
• Extend your arms back forward under control without letting your torso drop completely to the floor.
• Repeat for the desired number of controlled reps.
exercises.author: Yderkone

exercises.name: Cable Press Around
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Set the cable pulley to chest height and attach a single D-handle.
• Grab the handle with a neutral grip and hold it at your chest with your elbow tight to your side.
• Turn roughly 45 degrees away from the pulley into a stable staggered stance.

Execution:
• Press the handle forward and slightly across your body's midline in an arc, following the natural angle of your pectoral fibers.
• Squeeze your chest firmly at peak contraction without rotating your hips or lower back.
• Slowly reverse the motion under control, allowing a deep stretch in the chest before the next rep.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Y-Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Attach two single handles to the low pulleys of a dual cable machine.
• Grab the cables across your body (left hand takes right cable, right hand takes left cable).
• Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms crossed in front of your hips.

Execution:
• Raise both arms diagonally upward and outward until they form a wide 'Y' overhead.
• Focus on squeezing your rear deltoids and lower trapezius at the top of the movement.
• Lower your arms slowly and with control back to the starting crossed position.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: No Leg Drive Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Lie on a flat bench holding a pair of dumbbells at your chest.
• Lift your feet off the floor (placing your legs extended on the bench or elevated in the air) to completely eliminate leg drive.
• Position your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso.

Execution:
• Press the dumbbells vertically upward over your chest using pure pectoral and triceps strength.
• Squeeze your chest at the top without forcefully locking your elbows.
• Lower the weights slowly and under control until your upper arms are level with the bench pad.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Punches
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand in a balanced athletic boxing stance with one foot forward and knees slightly bent.
• Bring both hands up to chin level with elbows tucked close to your ribs for guard.

Execution:
• Throw alternating straight punches (jabs and crosses) directly forward in a sharp, rhythmic tempo.
• Rotate your hips and torso into each punch while turning your fist over horizontally upon extension.
• Rapidly snap each punch back to your defensive guard at your chin immediately after extending.
• Keep your core braced and exhale sharply with each punch.
exercises.author: lh1701

exercises.name: Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a pair of dumbbells with an underhand (supinated) grip.
• Hinge at your hips to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.

Execution:
• Row the dumbbells upward toward your ribcage and hips, leading with your elbows close to your sides.
• Squeeze your lats and upper back firmly at the peak contraction.
• Lower the dumbbells all the way down until they lightly touch the floor (dead stop), eliminating momentum before initiating the next repetition.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Pause Hack Squats
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
• Step into the hack squat machine, placing your shoulders snugly beneath the pads and resting your back against the backrest.
• Position your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.

Execution:
• Lower the sled slowly by bending your knees until your thighs are at or below parallel to the platform.
• Hold a complete dead stop pause for 1 to 2 seconds at the bottom without bouncing.
• Drive forcefully through your feet, engaging your quadriceps and glutes to press back up to the start without locking out your knees harshly.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Dumbbell Spider Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 45 degrees. Lie prone with your chest fully supported against the pad, your head clearing the top of the bench, and your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging vertically and palms facing forward (supinated grip).

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to the floor, flex your elbows to curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak contraction for 1 to 2 seconds.
3. Lower the weights slowly and under control over 3 to 4 seconds back to the fully extended starting position.

Cues:
The chest support eliminates momentum and body sway, placing maximal isolated tension on the biceps.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Calf Raise on Hack Squat Machine
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Step into the hack squat machine, resting your shoulders under the pads and placing your back flat against the backrest. Position the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the footplate with your heels hanging off into space. Disengage the safety stops and keep your knees almost fully extended with a slight soft bend.

Execution:
1. Lower your heels slowly and under control as far below the platform as comfortable to achieve a deep stretch in the calf muscles.
2. Drive through the balls of your feet to press upward onto your tiptoes as high as possible.
3. Squeeze your calves firmly at the peak contraction for one second before lowering back down with control.

Cues:
Do not bounce at the bottom or bend your knees to generate momentum; ensure the movement originates entirely from the ankle joints.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Incline Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie back on an incline bench set to roughly 30 to 45 degrees. Grip the barbell with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above your upper chest with your arms fully extended.

Execution:
1. Lower the barbell in a controlled manner toward your upper chest or lower neck, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso (at roughly a 30- to 45-degree angle).
2. Press the bar upward explosively by extending your elbows, concentrating the effort on your triceps and upper pectorals.
3. Lock out your arms briefly at the top without hyperextending your elbows, then repeat.

Cues:
Avoid an excessively narrow grip to protect your wrists; keeping your elbows close to your sides maximizes triceps engagement.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Floor Skull Crusher
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on the floor or an exercise mat with an EZ-curl bar resting on the floor behind your head. Grasp the bar with a narrow overhand grip on the inner curves and press it up so your arms are extended, tilted slightly back from vertical.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms fixed in position, flex your elbows to lower the barbell down behind your head until the weight plates rest gently on the floor.
2. Pause briefly on the floor to eliminate the stretch reflex and prevent any momentum.
3. Press the bar back up explosively by extending your elbows, squeezing the triceps hard at the top.

Cues:
Resting the bar on the floor between reps protects the elbows from sudden joint strain and allows you to handle heavier loads safely.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Bent-Over Cable Flye
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set the pulleys on a cable crossover station to a middle-to-high position and attach D-handles. Grasp the handles, step into the center with a staggered stance, and hinge forward at the hips to roughly a 45- to 60-degree angle (around 105 degrees relative to vertical) with a flat back. Keep your arms extended out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows.

Execution:
1. Bring the handles forward and downward in a wide hugging arc until your hands meet in front of your lower chest.
2. Squeeze your chest muscles forcefully at the peak contraction for a full second.
3. Slowly reverse the movement under control back to the starting stretch, maintaining the same slight bend in your elbows.

Cues:
Keep your torso stationary throughout; do not rock back and forth to generate momentum. Movement should occur exclusively at the shoulder joints.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: One-Arm Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a single D-handle to a high cable pulley. Kneel on one knee directly facing or slightly angled to the machine, placing the knee on the working side down on the floor or mat. Grasp the handle with your arm fully extended upward to achieve a deep stretch in the lat, keeping your torso upright and core engaged.

Execution:
1. Pull the handle downward by driving your elbow down and slightly back toward your hip until your hand reaches chest level.
2. Squeeze your lat hard at the bottom of the movement for one second.
3. Slowly return the cable to the starting position under full control, allowing the lat to fully stretch before beginning the next rep.

Cues:
The half-kneeling position locks your pelvis and core, preventing momentum and rotational cheating, and isolating the latissimus dorsi.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Kroc Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Support your torso by placing one hand and knee on a flat bench, or bracing one hand against a sturdy dumbbell rack. Keep your back flat and core tight. Hold a heavy dumbbell in your free hand with your arm hanging straight down in a neutral grip.

Execution:
1. Explosively pull the heavy dumbbell upward toward your hip, allowing a slight, controlled degree of body momentum to initiate the pull with the heavy load.
2. Drive your elbow high and back, squeezing your lats and upper back muscles forcefully at the top.
3. Lower the weight under control through the full range of motion, allowing the shoulder to stretch at the bottom before initiating the next rep.

Cues:
Pioneered by Matt Kroc, this powerbuilding staple combines heavy loads with high reps (often 15–25+ reps) to build massive back thickness and grip strength.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Cable Shrug-In
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach two D-handles to the lowest pulley settings on a dual cable station. Stand upright in the center between the towers with feet shoulder-width apart, holding each handle with your arms straight at your sides, aligning with the angle of the cables.

Execution:
1. With arms kept straight, shrug your shoulders upward and slightly inward toward your ears, matching the line of pull from the cables.
2. Squeeze your upper trapezius muscles hard at the top of the movement for a full one-second pause.
3. Lower your shoulders slowly and under control back down into a full stretch.

Cues:
The diagonal inward pull of the cables matches the anatomical fiber orientation of the upper traps better than vertical barbell shrugs. Keep your elbows locked throughout.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Flye
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set both pulleys of a dual cable machine at upper-chest to eye level. Grab the cables crosswise (left cable with right hand, right cable with left hand) by the carabiners or D-handles. Stand centered with feet shoulder-width apart, holding your arms extended forward in front of your chest with a soft bend in your elbows.

Execution:
1. Pull both arms simultaneously out and backward in a wide horizontal arc until your hands are in line with your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your rear deltoids and rhomboids firmly at the peak contraction for one second.
3. Slowly bring your arms back forward under full control to the starting crossed position.

Cues:
Maintain the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement; do not turn it into a triceps extension or row. Keep your torso stationary.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: W-Raise
exercises.description:
This challenging exercise is a variation of reverse crunches that is made up of three parts in which we’re basically drawing an upside down ‘W’ with our legs.
Start position is lying face up flat on the floor with legs extended at the low point of the outer leg of the ‘W’. Keeping a strong core and legs straight, go up, raise your hips and then slowly lower your legs down halfway. Then, lifting your legs back up to the top, raise your hips again, maintaining that straight line, use your core strength to finally come back all the way down to the other outer leg of the W. Then you reverse the ‘W’ to return to the start.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Black Widow Knee Slides
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Begin in a high plank position with your hands planted directly beneath your shoulders, fingers spread, and body forming a rigid straight line from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Drive one knee across and under your torso toward the opposite elbow.
2. Slide the knee upward along the forearm, curling the pelvis into a posterior pelvic tilt to strongly contract your obliques and rectus abdominis.
3. Return the leg under control to the starting plank position.
4. Repeat the motion on the opposite side, alternating fluidly between reps.

Cues:
Do not allow your lower back to sag or hips to rotate excessively; keep your core braced tightly throughout.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Butterfly Sit-up
exercises.description:
In this midrange exercise your arm muscles provide you with a little bit of momentum to help to get you off the ground. You also open them up in overhead position which engages the upper back.
Start lying with feet flat on the ground, knees at an angle, arms crossed in towards your chest. Using your ab muscles, bring your upper body off the ground as you open your arms into goal post position, then slowly lower yourself back down to return to starting position.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Seated Corkscrew
exercises.description:
To
do this abs and obliques exercise, start with your hands back behind your body
and bring your knees in and across, really trying to contract the obliques.
Then extend your legs back out to starting position and repeat toward the
opposite side of the abs.
Beginners
might find that they can’t even get through the first 45 seconds of this
challenging reverse crunches variation. That’s ok because it gives you a
place to start and something to improve upon.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Levitation Crunch
exercises.description: For this top down movement, we’re trying to move the upper torso without moving the lower torso. Start lying on the ground with feet flat on the floor and crossed arms above your head with hands behind head. Lift upper body up and clear your shoulder blades off the ground and then hold and pause at the top for a one or two count. Try to make the upper abs work and hold that contraction for 10 good quality reps.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Sit Up Elbow Thrust
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands in a defensive guard position near your face.

Execution:
1. Perform an explosive sit-up by driving your upper body upward using your abdominal muscles.
2. At the top of the sit-up, rotate your torso sharply and drive one elbow diagonally across your body in a powerful thrusting motion.
3. Return your torso to center and lower yourself back down to the floor under control.
4. Repeat, alternating the elbow thrust to the opposite side on each rep.

Cues:
Combine the forward flexion with explosive rotational drive at the top to maximally engage both the rectus abdominis and obliques.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Lying Barbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position for this practical triceps exercise is lying on a standard bench holding a barbell in both hands with an overhand grip, hands at shoulder width apart.
Begin with arms over your upper chest and elbows bent back at about a 45-degree angle.
First bend at the elbows and then allow the upper arm to drop back, bringing the barbell behind your head and down toward the floor. In terms of upper arm position, the barbell should never be fully above your head, but instead behind it, to ensure that you’re targeting the triceps.
Keep the shoulder blades tucked under, the elbows tight in toward your head and your core active during this entire movement.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Cable Drag Pushdown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand facing a high cable pulley with a rope attachment secured. Grasp the ends of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing inward) and set your feet shoulder-width apart, hinging slightly forward at the hips with an upright chest.

Execution:
1. Instead of pinning your elbows strictly by your ribs, let your elbows drift slightly back as you drag the rope straight downward, keeping it as close to your torso as possible.
2. Fully extend your elbows at the bottom and spread the rope ends apart, achieving a powerful peak contraction in the long head of the triceps.
3. Slowly return the rope back upward under control while maintaining proximity to the body.

Cues:
Dragging the attachment tight against your torso allows maximal extension and contraction of the triceps long head.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Dumbbell Cheat Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a heavy dumbbell in each hand at arm's length with a supinated (palms forward) grip.

Execution:
1. Use a slight, controlled hinge at the hips to generate just enough momentum to overcome the sticking point and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak contraction for a brief moment.
3. Lower the weights in a strictly controlled manner over 3 to 4 seconds, resisting the heavy load during the eccentric phase.

Cues:
The purpose of cheating through the concentric phase is to overload the eccentric (lowering) portion of the lift with heavier weight than could otherwise be curled with strict form.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Biceps Curl Trifecta
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended down at your sides.

Execution:
This exercise combines three distinct curl variations into a single continuous sequence:
1. Supinated Cross Body Curl: Supinate your forearm with your palm facing the ceiling and curl the dumbbell across your torso toward the opposite shoulder.
2. Pronated Cross Body Curl: Pronate your forearm with your palm facing the floor (overhand grip) and curl across your body toward the opposite shoulder to target the brachialis and forearm flexors.
3. No Money Curl: Curl the dumbbells while simultaneously externally rotating your shoulders, driving the hands outward to maximize peak tension on the biceps.

Cues:
Cycle through all three variations smoothly to accumulate high-volume time under tension across all elbow flexors.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Omni Cable Crossover
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set one pulley on a dual cable machine to the highest setting and the opposite pulley to the lowest setting. Stand in the center with a staggered stance for stability, gripping both handles.

Execution:
1. For the low cable, pull upward and diagonally across your torso to target the upper clavicular pectorals.
2. Simultaneously or in sequence with the high cable, draw it downward and across your body to recruit the lower sternal pectorals.
3. After completing the set, reverse the heights of the pulleys to work both sides of the chest evenly.

Cues:
Adjust your weights to the angle of pull: downward presses can typically handle 20% to 40% more weight than upward flyes due to muscle leverage.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Rocking Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand in a staggered stance in front of a high cable pulley with a rope attachment. Grasp the ends of the rope with a neutral grip and lean your upper body slightly forward toward the cable with your weight over your front foot.

Execution:
1. Push the rope downward while rocking your weight slightly back onto your rear foot, allowing your hands to extend behind the line of your torso.
2. Flare the rope ends outward at the bottom for an intense peak contraction in the triceps.
3. Slowly let the rope rise back up under control while shifting your weight forward again onto the front foot.

Cues:
The subtle rocking motion extends the active range of motion, providing a deeper lockout and enhanced engagement of the triceps long head.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Alternating High Cable Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a single handle to a high cable pulley. Stand about three feet back facing the pulley in a staggered stance, gripping the handle with one hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent.

Execution:
1. Pull your elbow downward and inward toward your torso with a slight, controlled torso rotation, engaging your lat and upper back.
2. Squeeze your back muscles at the peak contraction for one second.
3. Slowly return the cable to the starting stretch, switch hands to the other side, step back with the opposite foot, and repeat the movement.

Cues:
Perform reps alternately between arms to challenge anti-rotational core stability while building balanced back strength.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Hyper Y-W Combo with Weight Plates
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Position yourself on a hyperextension bench (or roman chair/GHD) with your hips against the pad and feet secured. Hold a light weight plate in each hand with your arms hanging down.

Execution:
1. Raise your torso until it forms a straight line with your legs, engaging your glutes and spinal erectors.
2. Raise your arms diagonally overhead into a Y position, squeezing your lower traps and holding briefly.
3. Draw your elbows down and back into a W position, retracting your scapulae firmly to hit the mid traps and rotator cuff.
4. Lower your arms and torso back down under control before initiating the next rep.

Cues:
Use light weight plates (2.5 to 5 lbs); focus entirely on scapular retraction, lower trap activation, and spinal control.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Plank Jacks
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a solid plank position on your forearms (or hands) with elbows directly beneath your shoulders and feet positioned close together, forming a rigid straight line from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Keeping your core braced and torso level, jump both feet outward simultaneously into a wide stance, similar to the leg motion of a jumping jack.
2. Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately spring back to the center starting position.
3. Continue hopping out and in with a smooth, controlled rhythm.

Cues:
Do not allow your hips to bounce up and down or your lower back to sag; the core must remain tightly locked against anti-extension throughout.
exercises.author: jayninja

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set an incline bench to approximately a 60-degree angle. Lie prone with your chest resting firmly against the inclined pad, feet planted on the floor for stability. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, retract your shoulder blades, and bring your upper arms up so they are roughly parallel to the floor alongside your ribs.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms completely still and elbows pinned, extend your elbows backward until your arms form a straight line.
2. Squeeze your triceps forcefully at the top lockout for a full second.
3. Slowly lower your forearms back down to a 90-degree angle under strict control.

Cues:
Resting your chest against the bench eliminates momentum and cheating, delivering intense isolation to the triceps long head.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cable High Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a single D-handle to a high cable pulley. Kneel on one knee facing the cable tower (working-side knee on the mat) with your torso tall and core braced. Grasp the handle with your arm extended upward in line with the cable.

Execution:
1. Pull the cable downward and backward by driving your elbow down toward your hip and ribs.
2. Squeeze your lat, rhomboids, and upper back firmly at the contraction point for a full second.
3. Slowly allow the cable to return upward under control, achieving a deep stretch in the lat before beginning the next repetition.

Cues:
The high-to-low pulling trajectory emphasizes the lats and lower traps while the half-kneeling setup prevents lower-back arching and momentum.
exercises.author: aahuja

exercises.name: Cable Bayesian Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a D-handle to a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the cable tower with a staggered stance about one step forward. Grasp the handle behind your torso with your arm extended backward, putting the long head of the biceps into a position of deep stretch.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arm stationary behind your body, flex your elbow to curl the handle forward and upward toward your shoulder.
2. Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak contraction for one second.
3. Slowly lower the handle back down and behind you over 2 to 3 seconds until you feel a full stretch in the biceps.

Cues:
The shoulder extension position places the long head of the biceps under loaded stretch, while the cable provides constant tension throughout the entire curve.
exercises.author: aahuja

exercises.name: Supinated Dumbbell Upper Chest Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright or sit on a low-incline bench holding a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand (supinated) grip at hip height, elbow softly bent. Lean your torso slightly toward the working arm to align with the clavicular pec fibers.

Execution:
1. Raise the dumbbell upward and diagonally across the upper chest toward head height, keeping the palm facing upward throughout.
2. Follow the natural angle of the upper pectoral muscle fibers.
3. Squeeze the upper chest and anterior deltoid firmly at the peak contraction for one second.
4. Lower the dumbbell slowly under control back to the starting position.

Cues:
Maintaining supination while driving up and across maximizes clavicular head recruitment of the pectoralis major.
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: DB Underhand bench press
exercises.description: Underhand grip DB, perform a normal bench press movement, keeping the elbows close to the chest
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press
exercises.description: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press, chest press movement focusing on the triceps. DB stays parallel with body
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Gorilla Row
exercises.description: Slightly bent down and knees to mimic a gorilla position and pull/row up the DBs to the chest. DB stay straight (thumbs pointing up)
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: DB Cross Body Hammer Curls
exercises.description: Dumbbell cross body biceps curls, works on the braccialis
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: Dumbbell Frog Press
exercises.description: Similar to hip thrust, but with feet put up together, lifting the butt off the ground in a frog like position.
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bradford Press
exercises.description: From a front hold of the dumbbells in an overhead press, press above the head, bring back towards the rear of the shoulders, down, and press back forward.
exercises.author: JohnPreston

exercises.name: High-Incline Smith Machine Press
exercises.description: Set the bench to a 45-60° incline. Touch the upper chest with the bar.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Kickback
exercises.description:
Grab onto the handle, and pull your elbow up and back slightly above
your torso. Keep your upper arm to be parallel to the ground for the
duration of the set
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Neutral Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Lat pull downs with a neutral grip on the bar.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Kong Curl
exercises.description:
This exercise is somewhat similar to a cable curl and a cable crossover. But instead of a chest/biceps exercise, this exercise targets the brachialis muscle, responsible for that broad arm when viewed from a front view.
During the exercise, maintain a pronated forearm position with starting position of approx. 45 degree pronated. Start with slightly bend elbows and alternately curl until your hands (your thumb first) meet your upper middle chest (similar to how Kong hits his chest, thus the name of this exercise).
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Drop Curl
exercises.description:
Drop curls in a modified position at a slow pace effectively engage the brachialis for arm width.
Starting position is with both arms in a slight angle towards each other at chest height with a dumbbell in each hand. Lower one dumbbell close to full extended arm position slowly and in a controlled manner during the first half of the curl, then curl it back up to starting position, while the other dumbbell stays at its starting position. Now lower the other dumbbell down. This keeps tension on the brachialis. As we pass the 90deg mark on our way down, the biceps will take over the work.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
exercises.description: Use rope handle with your back against the cable machine. Straighten your arms until they are fully extended and reverse the motion resisting on the negative.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Lateral Walk
exercises.description: Lateral walks, also known as side steps or squat walks, are a type of exercise where you move sideways in a squatting position. They can be performed with or without resistance bands. These exercises strengthen the hip abductors, glutes, and other stabilizing muscles.
exercises.author: cozyGalvinism

exercises.name: Leg Press Toe Press
exercises.description: Move the leg press using your calves by placing your feet at the bottom of the platform.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Handstand
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Place both hands shoulder-width apart on the floor with fingers splayed for stability. Keep your shoulders active, pressing firmly into the ground.

Execution:
1. Kick up one leg smoothly while pushing off with the trailing leg until your body is inverted vertically.
2. Lock your elbows, push tall through your shoulders, and squeeze your core, glutes, and legs together in a straight line.
3. Balance by making micro-adjustments with your fingertips and the palms of your hands.

Cues:
Avoid excessive arching in the lower back; keep your ribs pulled down and maintain a rigid hollow body position.
exercises.author: Fittness69

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit on a bench with back support or stand upright with a tight core. Grasp an EZ bar using a close overhand grip and press it overhead to arm's length.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms close to your head and elbows pointing forward, slowly lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows to roughly 90 degrees.
2. Pause briefly in the fully stretched position.
3. Extend your elbows to press the bar back up to the starting position, contracting your triceps firmly at the top.

Cues:
Keep your elbows from flaring out wide. The overhead position heavily recruits the long head of the triceps.
exercises.author: benjamin.yildiz

exercises.name: Pendulum Hack Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Position yourself in the pendulum hack squat machine with your back and shoulders firmly against the pads. Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate and disengage the safety handles.

Execution:
1. Descend smoothly along the curved pendulum trajectory by bending your knees and hips into a deep squat.
2. At the bottom of the movement where your quadriceps are fully stretched, drive through your whole foot to press back up.
3. Stop just short of locking your knees to keep tension squarely on the quads.

Cues:
The pendulum arc significantly reduces knee joint shear forces while providing intense quad loading throughout the full range of motion.
exercises.author: polloperro

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Load the sled with the appropriate weight. Stand behind the sled and grip the vertical uprights with arms extended or slightly bent, leaning your torso forward at roughly a 45-degree angle.

Execution:
1. Drive powerfully through the balls of your feet, pushing the sled forward with strong, continuous strides.
2. Keep your core braced and maintain a straight line from your head through your spine to your driving leg.
3. Push through the target distance or time with steady cadence and high intensity.

Cues:
The sled push builds powerful leg drive and conditioning with minimal eccentric muscle damage, making it ideal for speed, power, and metabolic conditioning.
exercises.author: flanny

exercises.name: Battle Ropes
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart in an athletic quarter-squat stance. Hold the rope handles firmly in each hand with a neutral grip in front of your hips.

Execution:
1. Drive your arms up and down alternately (or simultaneously) in an explosive, rhythmic motion, creating continuous waves that travel all the way to the anchor.
2. Keep your core solidly braced and your spine neutral to absorb the momentum.
3. Maintain a rapid pace and high intensity for the prescribed work interval.

Cues:
Battle ropes deliver high-intensity cardiovascular conditioning while taxing the deltoids, lats, and core stabilizers.
exercises.author: flanny

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slams
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees and hips slightly bent, holding a medicine ball with both hands at chest height. Engage your core.

Execution:
1. Extend your knees and hips explosively while raising the ball overhead, rising onto your toes.
2. Use your core, lats, and arms to slam the ball straight down into the floor between your feet with maximum force.
3. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to absorb the movement as you follow through.
4. Squat down to retrieve the ball and immediately transition into the next repetition.

Cues:
A full-body explosive power exercise developing triple extension, core strength, and metabolic conditioning.
exercises.author: flanny

exercises.name: SkiErg (Ski Machine)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand on the platform of the ski ergometer with feet hip-width apart. Reach overhead and grasp the handles with palms facing inward.

Execution:
1. Soften your knees, hinge your hips back, and drive both arms straight down past your thighs in an explosive, fluid pulling motion.
2. Finish the pull with your hands passing just beside your knees.
3. Extend your hips forward to return to an upright standing position as your arms return smoothly overhead.

Cues:
Simulates cross-country skiing double-poling technique, providing intense, low-impact cardiovascular training while engaging the lats, triceps, and anterior core.
exercises.author: flanny

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Step onto the pendulum squat platform, placing your shoulders snugly against the pads and feet shoulder-width apart in the center of the footplate. Disengage the safety latch and brace your core.

Execution:
1. Bend your knees and hips to descend along the machine's curved circular arc into a deep squat.
2. When your thighs reach full depth and your quadriceps are fully stretched, drive through your midfoot and heels to push back up.
3. Return to the starting position without forcefully locking your knees out at the top.

Cues:
The pendulum mechanism counterbalances spinal loading and allows an exceptionally deep knee flexion angle, placing tremendous tension on the quadriceps.
exercises.author: schweezer

exercises.name: Glute Drive
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit in the glute drive machine, resting your upper back against the pivot pad. Fasten the padded belt securely across your hips. Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate with toes slightly flared.

Execution:
1. Disengage the safety release and drive through your heels to bridge your hips upward against the belt.
2. Ascend until your torso and thighs form a straight horizontal line, squeezing your glutes intensely at peak contraction for 1–2 seconds.
3. Lower your hips back down slowly under control before repeating.

Cues:
The machine provides a stable, biomechanically guided setup for heavy hip thrusting, isolating the gluteus maximus safely.
exercises.author: schweezer

exercises.name: Toes-to-Bar
exercises.description: The name "Toes to Bar" says it all: This exercise, in which you hang from a pull-up bar, involves bringing your toes toward the bar, pointing toward your face. This really works your abdominal muscles. "Toes to Bar" is popular in functional fitness programs like Freeletics and CrossFit, and is an effective exercise for six-pack training.
exercises.author: florian.bussmann

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie flat on your back on a bench. Let your arms hang down straight towards the floor on either side of the bench.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms stable and elbows in place, curl the dumbbells upward until your forearms are perpendicular to the ceiling.
2. Squeeze your biceps firmly at the top of the movement.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under control until your arms are fully extended.

Cues:
Lying on a bench eliminates torso momentum and places the long head of the biceps under a significant passive stretch at the bottom.
exercises.author: Moffi

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a straight or EZ bar to the low pulley of a cable station. Stand upright (or sit) facing the machine and grasp the bar with a shoulder-width supinated grip (palms facing up). Pin your elbows to your sides.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms completely still, curl the bar up towards your upper chest by flexing at the elbows.
2. Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the range of motion.
3. Lower the weight under control until your arms are almost fully extended, resisting the cable tension.

Cues:
Cables deliver continuous mechanical tension on the biceps throughout both the concentric and eccentric phases.
exercises.author: Brigade7938

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand or sit upright with your shoulders relaxed and spine in neutral alignment.

Execution:
1. Bring one arm horizontally across your chest at shoulder height.
2. Use your opposite hand to gently press your upper arm or elbow closer to your torso until you feel a comfortable stretch in the rear shoulder.
3. Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
4. Release slowly and repeat on the opposite side.

Cues:
Effectively stretches the posterior deltoid and external rotators. Avoid elevating the shoulder toward your ear during the stretch.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: Pull-Up Isometric Hold
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Pull yourself up into your target hold position (such as chin over the bar or with elbows bent at 90 degrees).

Execution:
1. Lock your body completely in place at that specific joint angle.
2. Retract and depress your scapulae, maintaining maximal static contraction in your lats, upper back, and biceps.
3. Hold for the prescribed duration (e.g., 10 to 30 seconds) before lowering under control.

Cues:
Builds isometric pulling strength, reinforces scapular stability, and helps overcome sticking points in the pull-up.
exercises.author: DiscoCop

exercises.name: Archer Pull-Up
exercises.description:
An archer pull-up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that strengthens your back and biceps, serving as a progression towards a one-arm pull-up. It gets its name from the "bow-drawing" position your body takes at the top.Here's how to do it:

Grip: Grasp a pull-up bar with a wider-than-shoulder-width overhand grip.
Starting Position: Hang with arms fully extended, engaging your core and keeping your shoulder blades pulled down.
The Pull: Pull your body up towards one hand, similar to a regular pull-up. At the same time, extend the other arm out to the side, keeping it as straight as possible. Your chin should come towards the hand that is pulling.
Hold and Lower: Briefly hold the top position where one arm is bent and pulling, and the other is extended. Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Alternate: Repeat the movement, pulling up towards the opposite hand.The key to this exercise is to keep the assisting arm as straight as possible to maximise the load on the working arm. This makes it a challenging but effective exercise for unilateral pulling strength.
exercises.author: Antsy6277

exercises.name: Larsen Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie back on a flat bench beneath the barbell. Extend your legs straight out in front of you suspended in mid-air (or rest them flat on an adjacent bench), completely removing your feet from the floor. Grasp the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and retract your shoulder blades.

Execution:
1. Unrack the bar and lower it with steady control to your mid-chest, keeping your core rigidly braced for balance.
2. Press the barbell straight back up to full arm extension using pure upper-body pressing power, completely devoid of leg drive.
3. Pause briefly at lockout before beginning the next repetition.

Cues:
Eliminating leg drive places tremendous isolated overload on the pectorals and triceps while forcing significant core and scapular stability.
exercises.author: Expenses7000

exercises.name: StairMaster (Stair Climber)
exercises.description: Cardio and lower-body strength machine designed to simulate climbing stairs. It provides a low-impact, high-intensity workout that targets the legs, glutes, and core while improving cardiovascular endurance.
exercises.author: MisterPinnacle

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description:
The push-up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, arms, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability. It requires no equipment and is excellent for building upper body strength.
Instructions:

Start in a plank position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width, feet together, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body or flared slightly outward.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the ground while maintaining a neutral spine.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
exercises.author: Settebello

exercises.name: Clap Push-Up
exercises.description:
The clap push-up is an explosive upper body movement that builds power and fast-twitch muscle strength. It adds a plyometric challenge to the traditional push-up by requiring the hands to leave the ground mid-rep.

Start in a strong push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and core engaged
Lower your body explosively and push off the ground with enough force to lift your hands.
Quickly clap your hands together at chest level before returning them to the floor.
Land with soft elbows to absorb the impact and immediately move into the next rep
exercises.author: Settebello

exercises.name: Devil's Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Place a pair of dumbbells on the floor shoulder-width apart and stand behind them.

Execution:
1. Drop down placing your hands on the dumbbell handles, kick your feet back into a plank, and lower your chest to the floor between the weights (dumbbell burpee).
2. Explosively jump your feet forward just outside the dumbbells into a wide hinge stance.
3. In one continuous, fluid hip-hinge motion, swing the dumbbells slightly back between your legs and snatch them directly overhead to full lockout.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control back to the floor and immediately begin the next rep.

Cues:
A demanding metabolic conditioning movement combining a burpee and a double dumbbell snatch. Keep your back flat during the hip drive.
exercises.author: Settebello

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with knees slightly bent and feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arm stationary and elbow tucked, curl one dumbbell up toward your shoulder with the weight vertical.
2. Squeeze your brachioradialis and brachialis firmly at the top of the curl.
3. Lower the dumbbell slowly with control back to the starting position before repeating with the other arm.

Cues:
Avoid swinging the torso or using momentum. The neutral grip maximizes tension on the forearm and brachialis.
exercises.author: Mariano_O

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Begin on all fours (quadruped position) on a mat with hands directly under shoulders and knees under hips. Maintain a neutral spine and engage your core.

Execution:
