1. Simultaneously reach your right arm straight forward and extend your left leg straight back until both are parallel to the floor.
2. Pause and hold the fully extended position for 1–2 seconds, actively squeezing your glute and spinal erectors without arching your lower back.
3. Return to the starting position under control and switch to the opposite arm and leg.

Cues:
Keep your hips and shoulders squared to the floor. Avoid rotating your pelvis or overarching the lumbar spine.
exercises.author: Settebello

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Kneel on a padded mat with your knees hip-width apart. Grasp the handles of the ab wheel firmly, resting it on the floor in front of your knees.

Execution:
1. Brace your abdominal muscles, tuck your pelvis slightly, and slowly roll the wheel forward in a controlled line, extending your body towards the floor.
2. Roll out as far as you can maintain a neutral, slightly rounded lumbar spine without sagging in the lower back.
3. Pull through your abdominals and lats to roll the wheel back to the starting position.

Cues:
A premier anti-extension exercise for the rectus abdominis and transversus abdominis. Never allow your lower back to collapse into excessive extension.
exercises.author: lhegedus

exercises.name: Swimming
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Enter the pool and prepare in the water for laps using your preferred stroke (such as freestyle or breaststroke).

Execution:
1. Swim continuous laps at a steady, rhythmic cadence focusing on smooth breathing and efficient propulsion.
2. Engage your latissimus dorsi, deltoids, and core to pull through the water with full arm extension.
3. Maintain a streamlined horizontal body position throughout the session.

Cues:
Swimming provides low-impact, high-efficiency cardiovascular conditioning and muscular endurance, heavily engaging the back, shoulders, and core.
exercises.author: delta@romeo

exercises.name: Standing Dowel Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and core engaged. Grasp a lightweight wooden dowel (or PVC pipe/broomstick) with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width at chest height.

Execution:
1. Press the dowel smoothly overhead until your arms are fully extended and shoulders shrugged slightly up to clear the subacromial space.
2. Lower the dowel with control either in front to your clavicles or behind your neck, alternating between front and back positions.
3. Focus on shoulder and thoracic mobility rather than resistance.

Cues:
An excellent warm-up and mobility drill for the shoulder girdle and thoracic spine. Move only within a pain-free range of motion.
exercises.author: mountain.potato

exercises.name: Snap Down
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Reach your arms straight up overhead and rise onto your toes, making your body as tall and elongated as possible.

Execution:
1. Explosively snap your arms downward while rapidly dropping your hips and bending your knees into a solid athletic stance.
2. Land softly on full feet, absorbing the force with chest up, hips hinged, and core firmly braced.
3. Hold the solid athletic landing position for a brief pause before resetting.

Cues:
Develops rapid deceleration, landing mechanics, and eccentric control to prepare for explosive jumps and changes of direction.
exercises.author: mountain.potato

exercises.name: Bretzel Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side on a mat. Bring your top knee up to hip level at a 90-degree angle resting on the floor, and hold it pinned down with your bottom hand.

Execution:
1. Bend your bottom knee behind you and grab the bottom foot or ankle with your top hand.
2. Inhale deeply, then exhale as you slowly rotate your top shoulder and upper back towards the floor.
3. Keep the top knee pinned to the floor to preserve rotation in the thoracic spine and stretch through the hips.
4. Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, taking slow deep breaths, then switch sides.

Cues:
A premier mobility drill that combines thoracic spine rotation with a stretch of the bottom leg's hip flexors/quads and top leg's gluteals.
exercises.author: mountain.potato

exercises.name: Hip Hinge
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. Place your hands on the creases of your hips or across your chest. Keep a soft, slight bend in your knees.

Execution:
1. Push your hips straight back as if trying to touch a wall behind you with your glutes.
2. Hinge forward at the hips while maintaining a flat, neutral spine and keeping your chest proud.
3. Lower your torso until you feel a distinct hamstring stretch without rounding your lower back.
4. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes powerfully to return to standing.

Cues:
The foundational movement pattern for deadlifts, swings, and good mornings. Ensure movement originates from the hips, not by squatting or bending the spine.
exercises.author: mountain.potato

exercises.name: Bronco Test
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set up cones at 0m (start line), 20m, 40m, and 60m markers on a running track or field.

Execution:
1. Sprint 20m from the start line, touch the line/cone, and sprint back to the start.
2. Immediately turn and sprint 40m, touch the mark, and sprint back to the start.
3. Immediately turn and sprint 60m, touch the mark, and sprint back to the start (this completes 1 repetition of 240m).
4. Repeat for a total of 5 continuous repetitions without rest (1,200 meters total) as fast as possible.

Cues:
A gold-standard aerobic and anaerobic running fitness test widely used in rugby and field sports.
exercises.author: MU5H

exercises.name: Perpendicular Unilateral Landmine Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set up a barbell in a landmine attachment so that the bar extends perpendicular (at 90 degrees) to your body. Stand beside the sleeve end of the bar in a staggered or athletic stance, hinge at the hips with a flat back, and grip the sleeve or collar with one hand.

Execution:
Brace your core and pull the barbell up toward the side of your chest or lower ribcage. Drive your elbow back and upward while keeping your torso square and stationary. Squeeze your lats and mid-back at the peak of the movement, then lower the barbell under control until your arm is fully extended.

Cues:
- Keep your spine neutral and resist twisting through your torso during the pull.
- Pull with your elbow rather than your hand to maximize lat and upper back recruitment.
exercises.author: CptnFatbeard

exercises.name: Dumbbell Scapular Press (Trap Press)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a bench holding a dumbbell in one hand. Extend your arm vertically toward the ceiling directly above your shoulder, with your elbow locked out or nearly locked.

Execution:
Keeping your arm completely straight and without bending your elbow, protract your shoulder blade to push the dumbbell directly upward toward the ceiling as high as comfortable. Squeeze your serratus anterior at the top, then slowly retract your shoulder blade to lower the weight back to the resting position on the bench.

Cues:
- Movement must occur entirely at the shoulder blade (scapular protraction and retraction), not at the elbow joint.
- Keep your core engaged and your back flat against the bench throughout the movement.
exercises.author: CptnFatbeard

exercises.name: Side-Lying Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Laying on your side and using the arm closest to the bench, maintain a 90 degree bend at the elbow and allow the weight to fall towards the ground past the bench as low as comfortable. Bring the weight up using only rotation of the shoulder to the opposing shoulder.
exercises.author: CptnFatbeard

exercises.name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press (Supine Press)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor. Grip the barbell with a close overhand grip (roughly shoulder-width apart) and unrack the bar directly above your upper chest with your arms extended.

Execution:
Inhale and lower the barbell in a controlled manner toward your lower chest or sternum, keeping your elbows tucked relatively close to your torso (around 30–45 degrees). Lightly touch your chest without bouncing, then press the barbell powerfully back up to full elbow extension by contracting your triceps and pecs.

Cues:
- Keep your wrists stacked directly over your forearms and elbows.
- Do not grip too narrowly (hands should not touch), which avoids excessive wrist and elbow strain.
exercises.author: CptnFatbeard

exercises.name: March or Jog in Place
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, chest lifted, and core gently engaged. Keep your arms relaxed and bent at a 90-degree angle by your sides.

Execution:
Begin lifting one knee up toward hip height, then lower it with a soft landing as you lift the opposite knee. Synchronize your arms by swinging them naturally in rhythm with the opposite legs (like a running motion). Keep a steady, low-impact marching pace or increase the tempo into a gentle jog in place.

Cues:
- Land softly on the balls of your feet and roll through to your heels.
- Maintain an upright posture without leaning forward or backward.
exercises.author: MrAlfaRobot

exercises.name: Leg and hip stretch
exercises.description: Gentle movements to improve the flexibility of the lower body and release tension in the hips.
exercises.author: MrAlfaRobot

exercises.name: Arm and neck stretch
exercises.description: Relieves tension in the upper body, especially useful for people with office jobs or prolonged postures.
exercises.author: MrAlfaRobot

exercises.name: Deep breathing (standing or seated)
exercises.description: A conscious breathing technique to improve oxygenation, reduce stress and connect with the present moment.
exercises.author: MrAlfaRobot

exercises.name: Guided or free meditation
exercises.description: A mental mindfulness exercise that helps reduce anxiety, improve focus and enhance overall well-being.
exercises.author: MrAlfaRobot

exercises.name: Smith Machine Split Squat
exercises.description:
The "Smith Machine Split Squat" is a strength exercise
performed on the Smith machine, ideal for targeting the legs and glutes.
It involves placing one foot forward and the other back, lowering the
body until the front thigh is parallel to the ground while the bar
slides vertically along the machine. This exercise helps improve
stability, correct muscle imbalances, and reduces stress on the back,
providing a safe environment for strength training.
exercises.author: workout

exercises.name: Dumbbell Scaption
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep a slight bend in your elbows, shoulders relaxed and shoulder blades pulled back.
Execution:
Slowly raise the dumbbells forward and slightly to the side, at about a 30–45° angle from your body (between a front raise and a lateral raise).
Lift until your arms are about shoulder height (do not go overhead).
Pause for a second at the top and feel the activation in your shoulders and scapular stabilizers.
Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
Breathing:
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells.
Exhale as you lift them.
Common mistakes:
Using dumbbells that are too heavy (causing jerky movements).
Lifting above shoulder height (puts unnecessary stress on the shoulder joint).
Arching the lower back instead of keeping the movement controlled at the shoulders.
Purpose of the exercise:
Activates the lower trapezius, serratus anterior, and scapular stabilizers.
Helps correct posture and improve shoulder balance.
exercises.author: zdelko

exercises.name: Leg curl with elastic
exercises.description: Lying on your stomach with a resistance band anchored to a low point and looped around your ankle, bend your knee to curl your heel toward your glutes against the band.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Sliding Lateral Lunge
exercises.description: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell close to your chest in goblet position. Place one foot on a slider, gliding disc, or towel. Keep your chest tall and core engaged. Slowly slide the foot outward to the side while bending the opposite knee, lowering your hips into a lateral lunge. Keep the working leg’s knee aligned with the toes and avoid letting it collapse inward. The non-working leg remains straight and slides smoothly along the floor. Push through the heel of the bent leg to return to the starting position while maintaining control of the kettlebell.
exercises.author: RiccaBaro

exercises.name: Copenhagen Adduction Exercise
exercises.description: Lie on your side with the elbow placed directly under the shoulder, similar to a side plank position. Place the upper leg on a bench with the inside of the foot or ankle resting on it. Lift your hips and hold your body in a straight line while keeping the lower leg off the floor. The exercise strongly activates the adductors of the upper leg while also challenging the core and hip stabilizers.
exercises.author: RiccaBaro

exercises.name: Arm Raises (T/Y/I)
exercises.description:
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, core engaged, and arms relaxed at your sides. From this position, perform three different arm raises to target the shoulders and upper back:

T Raise: Lift your arms straight out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a “T” shape.
Y Raise: Lift your arms upward at about a 45° angle from your body to form a “Y” shape.
I Raise: Raise your arms straight overhead, close together, forming an “I” shape.

Maintain a neutral spine, avoid arching your lower back, and move slowly with control. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.
exercises.author: WiNNiE

exercises.name: Typewriter Pull-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width. Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar. At the top position, instead of going straight down, shift your body to one side by extending one arm while keeping the other arm bent. Move smoothly from one side to the other, like a typewriter motion, before lowering yourself back down. This exercise increases time under tension and strengthens the lats, biceps, and shoulders while building unilateral pulling strength.
exercises.author: tenebrizz

exercises.name: Bodyweight Biceps Curl
exercises.description: Set up under a straight bar (around waist or chest height). Grip the bar with your palms facing you (supinated grip), hands about shoulder-width apart. Lean back with straight arms so that your body is at an angle to the ground. Keeping your elbows high and close to the bar, pull your upper body toward the bar by flexing your elbows, similar to a biceps curl. Lower yourself back down in a controlled manner. Keep your core tight and movement slow to maximize tension on the biceps.
exercises.author: tenebrizz

exercises.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description:
Place your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, pointing your toes outward.
Keep your back straight, shoulders back, and chest up.
The knees must follow the same direction as the toes and not move forward.
When going up, it is advisable to contract your glutes to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise..
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Rubber Band Glute Kickback
exercises.description: A rubber band glute kickback is an exercise performed on hands and knees, where you anchor a resistance band to your foot and kick your heel back and up, squeezing your glute at the top of the movement, while maintaining a stable core and flat back to target and strengthen the gluteal muscles.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Treadmill Cardio
exercises.description:
It's a cardiovascular workout performed on a treadmill to improve endurance, burn calories, and promote heart health. It offers multiple benefits, such as the ability to easily adjust speed and incline, allowing for a variety of workouts, from hill walking to high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and tempo runs. To optimize results, it's important to vary your workouts.
Benefits of Treadmill Cardio:

Improved Cardiovascular Health:
Regular aerobic exercise on a treadmill strengthens the heart and lungs, which can help prevent heart disease.
Weight Loss:
By burning calories, treadmill training can be an effective tool for weight loss and maintaining a healthy weight.
Muscle Strengthening:
It strengthens the muscles in the legs and glutes, helping to prevent muscle loss, which is especially important with age.
Training Flexibility:
Allows you to vary speed, incline, and intervals, making your workout more dynamic and adaptable to different fitness levels.
Types of Treadmill Training:
Hill Walking:
Increasing the incline of the treadmill and walking at a brisk pace can improve endurance and work your leg muscles.
Endurance Jog:
A run at a comfortable, steady pace that keeps your heart rate in a target zone (such as Zone 2) to build endurance.
Interval Training:
Alternating periods of high intensity (fast running) with periods of low intensity (easy walking or jogging) to maximize calorie burn and cardiovascular improvement.
Tempo Run:
A run at a steady, sustained pace that is slightly faster than a normal jog, which challenges your ability to sustain a more intense effort for an extended period.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Dumbbell donkey kick
exercises.description:
The dumbbell donkey kick is an effective exercise for working the glute and hamstring muscles. This exercise is usually performed on all fours, using a dumbbell to add resistance. The steps for performing it correctly are described below.
Starting position: Get on all fours on a mat, with your hands aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips.
Placing the dumbbell: Take a dumbbell and place it behind the knee of the leg you are going to lift. Make sure it is held securely to prevent it from falling during the exercise.
Exercise:
Inhale and, as you exhale, lift the leg with the dumbbell upward, keeping the knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
Raise the leg until it is parallel to the floor, feeling the contraction in the glutes.
Hold the position for one second at the top and then slowly lower the leg back to the starting position.
Repetitions: Perform 10 to 15 repetitions per leg, making sure to maintain good form throughout the exercise.
Sets: Complete 2 to 3 sets, depending on your fitness level.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Stationary bike cardio
exercises.description:
Benefits of Stationary Bike Cardio
Stationary bike cardio is an excellent form of exercise that offers multiple benefits for health and well-being. Here are some of the most notable ones:
Improved Cardiovascular Health
Strengthens the heart: Regular exercise helps improve the heart's efficiency and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.
Increases circulation: It improves blood flow, which can help lower blood pressure.
Calorie Burning and Weight Loss
Efficient for burning calories: Depending on the intensity, you can burn between 400 and 600 calories per hour.
Helps with weight loss: Combined with a balanced diet, stationary bike cardio can be effective for losing weight.
Muscle Strengthening
Tones the legs: It mainly works the leg muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings and calves.
Improves muscular endurance: Over time, you can increase the endurance and strength in your legs.
Mental Health Benefits
Reduces stress: Exercise releases endorphins, which can improve your mood and reduce stress.
Boosts energy: Regular physical activity can raise your energy levels and improve sleep quality.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.description: The seated dumbbell calf raise is a targeted exercise for strengthening the lower leg muscles. It follows the same movement pattern as the machine version: you place the weight on your knees, and by extending and flexing your ankles, you move the weight.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Unilateral Cable Row
exercises.description: Put a vertical seated bench in front of the cable row machine.position it so that you can focus on one side, and then do slow pulls focusing on the lateral muscles and ensuring tention in those muscles when in a stretched position.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Blaze
exercises.description: BLAZE is a full-body HIIT workout. Designed to supercharge your cardio fitness and strength. Delivered in its own purpose-built studio, BLAZE is a unique mix of martial arts, intense cardio and strength training.
exercises.author: ricwheatley

exercises.name: Cable Rope Pullover Row
exercises.description: Set up an incline bench in front of a low cable pulley with a rope attachment. Lean forward over the back of the bench, initiate the movement by pulling the rope toward your hips in a sweeping pullover arc, and finish with a row by driving your elbows backward to fully contract the lats.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Modified pulldown
exercises.description: With an inclined bench in front of the pulldown machine, use a close-grip to do latfocused pulldowns.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Single arm row
exercises.description: Sitting on the ground, use a high cable in a single grip, to do lat pulldowns with a focus on a long stretch in the lats.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Barbell Clean and press
exercises.description: This exercise involves lifting a barbell from the ground to the shoulders, then pressing it overhead. It is a compound movement that targets multiple muscle groups, including the legs, back, shoulders, and arms. It is often used in strength and conditioning programs to improve overall power and athleticism.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent Over Face Pull
exercises.description: This exercise involves using dumbbells to perform a bent over face pull, which targets the upper back and shoulders. The movement involves pulling the weights towards the face while keeping the elbows high and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Squat
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height and performing a squat. It targets the lower body muscles, including the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core and upper body.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Kettlebell One Legged Deadlift
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a kettlebell in one hand and standing on one leg while bending forward to touch the kettlebell to the ground. It targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while also improving balance and stability.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: This exercise involves sitting on the ground with a dumbbell resting on the hips, then thrusting the hips upward while squeezing the glutes. It is a great exercise for strengthening the glutes and improving hip mobility.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Weight Plate Crunch
exercises.description:
The Weight Plate Crunch is a variation of the classic crunch exercise that involves holding a weight plate to increase the intensity of the abdominal work.

Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a weight plate securely across your chest or extended above you.
Lift your shoulders and upper back off the floor by flexing your spine, contracting your abs.
Lower slowly back to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and bending sideways to work the oblique muscles on the side of the body. It can be done standing or seated and is often used as a core strengthening exercise.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and stepping back into a lunge position, then returning to standing. It primarily targets the glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and bending forward at the hips while keeping the back straight, then returning to a standing position. It primarily targets the hamstrings and glutes.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Squat
exercises.description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and performing a squat while stepping to the side. It targets the legs, glutes, and core muscles.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The machine lateral raise is an isolation exercise that targets the medial (side) deltoid muscle to build wider, more defined shoulders. The machine's fixed path of motion provides greater stability than dumbbells, making it ideal for beginners or those who want to focus solely on muscle activation.
exercises.author: roneydya

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press - Decline
exercises.description: Single arm chest press done with the cable machine. Use the other arm to brace bodyweight to focus on strength of the press, rather than balancing of the body. Start with the hand as close to the chest as possible, and then press against the cable at a slight decline and aiming towards the center of your chest.
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Preacher Curl - Internally Rotated
exercises.description: Single arm curl that can be done using a dumbbell and a preacher bench, or a preacher curl machine. Turn body towards the weight
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Preacher Curl - Externally Rotated
exercises.description: Single arm curl that can be done using a dumbbell and a preacher bench, or a preacher curl machine. Turn body away from the weight
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cross-Body Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Sit at lat pulldown machine with body at a diagonal angle so that only one leg is under the pad. Pull the cable down with the opposite arm. this will force the cable to across your body while pulling down. Emphasises the stretch of the lat.
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press - Incline
exercises.description: Single arm chest press done with the cable machine. Use the other arm to brace bodyweight to focus on strength of the press, rather than balancing of the body. Start with the hand as close to the chest as possible, and then press against the cable at a slight incline and aiming towards the center of your chest.
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Press
exercises.description: A single arm exercise that starts with the hand close to the chest with with the elbows bent, and the elbow flared out. Press forward and down against the cable straightening the elbow.
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Cable Tri Extension - Internal Rotation
exercises.description: single arm exercise with cable held at opposite shoulder with elbow bent. Turn towards the cable, and the straighten the elbow across the body.
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: Curl with Shoulder Elevated
exercises.description: Place elbow so that it is about level with the shoulder. Curl the wieght to your shoulder. Focus on the stretch in the eccentric part of the curl
exercises.author: Shiladree

exercises.name: One Arm Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
exercises.description:
Set the pulley at the bottom of the cable machine and grab onto it without using any attachments. Extend the cable directly overhead.
While keeping your back straight and upper arm stationary, lower the cable behind your head until you feel a good stretch in your triceps, and then extend it back upward until your elbow is locked out.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Leg Swings (Front–Back)
exercises.description: Stand tall next to a wall or stable support. Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion, keeping the torso upright and the core engaged. Alternate legs after completing the repetitions.
exercises.author: Jhonatan

exercises.name: Seated Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Starting Position:

Adjust the seat height so that your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit with your back flat against the backrest, maintaining good posture.
Place the outside of your thighs against the machine's padded levers.
Position your feet flat on the footrests or platform of the machine.
Grasp the handles or sides of the seat for stability.
Ensure your spine is neutral and your core is slightly engaged.

Movement:

Exhale as you slowly push your legs outward against the resistance pads.
Focus on initiating the movement from your hips, not your knees.
Continue opening your legs until you feel a strong contraction in your outer hips and thighs.
Hold the fully abducted position briefly (1-2 seconds) to maximize muscle engagement.
Inhale as you slowly control the return of your legs to the starting position, resisting the weight throughout the movement.
Avoid allowing the weight stack to touch down between repetitions to maintain constant tension on the muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the set.
exercises.author: Iko

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: The Wall Angels exercise primarily targets the upper back and shoulder muscles, helping improve posture, shoulder mobility, and scapular control.
exercises.author: bbayuwega

exercises.name: Seated Figure Four
exercises.description: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground. Place your left ankle over your right knee. Your right knee stays flat. Keep your back straight. Gently push your left knee down.
exercises.author: ricardodavidrd

exercises.name: Zottman curl
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward (underhand grip).

Movement:
1. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders in a smooth, controlled motion.
2. At the top of the movement, rotate your wrists so that your palms face downward (overhand grip).
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under control in this pronated position.
4. At the bottom, rotate your palms forward again to reset.

Tips:
Keep your elbows stationary at your sides and avoid swinging. The controlled overhand lowering phase heavily recruits the brachioradialis and forearm muscles.
exercises.author: meldun

exercises.name: Dumbbell Thruster
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a pair of dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows slightly forward.

Movement:
1. Lower your hips down and back into a deep squat until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
2. Drive up explosively through your heels, using the upward momentum to press the dumbbells overhead in one fluid motion.
3. Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders with control as you transition smoothly into the next squat repetition.

Tips:
Keep your chest up and core braced throughout the movement to maintain a stable spine.
exercises.author: meldun

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Single-Arm Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Drive through your heels to raise your hips into a stable glute bridge, and press the dumbbell directly above your chest.

Movement:
1. Lower the dumbbell with control until your upper arm or elbow touches the floor at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body.
2. Press the dumbbell back up to the starting position while keeping your hips fully extended.
3. Complete the prescribed repetitions, then repeat on the opposite side.

Tips:
Keep your glutes firmly squeezed and core tight throughout to prevent your hips from rotating or sagging.
exercises.author: meldun

exercises.name: Bear Crawl Pull-Through
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a quadruped position with hands beneath your shoulders and knees beneath your hips. Place a dumbbell on the floor just behind one hand. Hover your knees a few inches off the floor while maintaining a flat back (bear crawl hold).

Movement:
1. Reach underneath your torso with the opposite hand, grasp the dumbbell handle, and pull or slide it across to the other side.
2. Return your hand to the floor to re-stabilize your bear crawl position.
3. Repeat the movement in the opposite direction using the other hand.

Tips:
Keep your hips and shoulders parallel to the floor. Do not allow your pelvis to sway or rotate as you drag the weight.
exercises.author: meldun

exercises.name: Kickstand RDL
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Shift approximately 80–90% of your body weight onto the front working leg. Place the rear foot slightly behind you with only the toes touching the floor for balance (kickstand position).

Movement:
1. Keeping your chest up and spine neutral, push your hips backward and hinge forward at the waist.
2. Lower the barbell close to your front shin until you feel a deep stretch in the hamstring of your front leg.
3. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the upright starting position.

Tips:
The rear foot is strictly for balance and should bear minimal weight. Focus all muscular tension on the hamstring and glute of the front leg.
exercises.author: eriktrinkle

exercises.name: Cable Fly Middle Chest
exercises.description:
Execution

Start position: Arms extended out to your sides (a big “T” shape), feeling a stretch in your chest.

Movement: Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide hugging motion.

Focus on squeezing your chest at the center.
Do not lock your elbows or turn it into a press.

Return: Slowly open your arms back to the start, maintaining tension on the chest.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Cable Fly Upper Chest
exercises.description:
Execution

Start position:

Arms down and slightly behind your body, elbows slightly bent.
Feel a light stretch across your chest.

Movement:

Bring your hands upward and together in front of your upper chest — roughly at chin to collarbone level.
Use a smooth, controlled motion (avoid jerking).
Squeeze your chest at the top for 1–2 seconds.

Return:

Slowly let your arms move back down and out to the sides, keeping control and tension.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Cable Fly Lower Chest
exercises.description:
Execution

Start position:

Arms extended out to your sides in a “Y” shape.
Feel a stretch in your chest (slight bend in elbows — don’t lock them).

Movement:

Bring your hands downward and together in front of your lower chest or upper abs, in a smooth arc motion.
Squeeze your chest hard at the bottom for 1–2 seconds.

Return:

Slowly raise your arms back up along the same path until you feel a good stretch in your chest.
Maintain control — don’t let the weights pull you back too quickly.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Static Hold
exercises.description:
Execution

Hold Position:

Lower the dumbbells a few inches above your chest — about the midpoint of a normal incline press.
This is where your upper chest is under maximum tension.

Static Hold:

Hold the position for 20–45 seconds while keeping the chest tight.
Breathe slowly but stay tense — do not relax your chest or shoulders.

End the set:

After the hold, carefully bring the dumbbells down and rest.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Flat Machine Press
exercises.description:
Execution

Start position:

Elbows bent at roughly 90°, hands just outside your chest.
Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.

Pressing phase (concentric):

Push the handles forward until your arms are almost fully extended — don’t lock out.
Focus on squeezing your chest at the end of the movement.

Returning phase (eccentric):

Slowly bring the handles back toward your chest, feeling the stretch in your pecs.
Maintain tension — don’t let the weight stack touch down between reps.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.description:
Execution

Pulling phase (concentric):

Drive your elbows down and slightly back, pulling your chest toward the bar.
Focus on leading with your chest, not your chin.
Keep your shoulders depressed (avoid shrugging).

Top position:

Chin should clear the bar (or at least reach bar level).
Pause for a brief squeeze in your lats.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.description:
Execution

Pulling phase (concentric):

Drive your elbows down and back, pulling your chest toward your hands.
Keep your shoulders depressed and retracted (avoid shrugging).
Focus on squeezing your lats and upper back at the top.

Top position:

Chin should clear or reach the level of your hands.
Pause briefly and contract your lats hard.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand)
exercises.description:
Execution

Starting position:

Hold the barbell with arms fully extended toward the floor.
Maintain tension in your lats and back muscles.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Underhand)
exercises.description:
Execution

Starting position:

Hold the barbell with arms fully extended toward the floor.
Maintain tension in your lats and back muscles.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.description:
Execution

Hinge at the hips:

Push your hips backward, keeping a slight bend in the knees (soft knees).
Lower the barbell along the front of your thighs/shins while maintaining a neutral spine.
Keep the bar close to your body.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: One-Arm Heavy Row
exercises.description:
Execution

Rowing phase (concentric):

Pull the dumbbell toward your lower chest or waist, leading with your elbow.
Keep your torso stable — avoid twisting or rotating your shoulders.
Pause at the top and squeeze your lats.
exercises.author: daiben

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: The lat pulldown is a pulling exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi muscles (commonly known as “lats”) in your back. It involves pulling a cable bar or handle down towards your chest while seated on a machine specifically designed for this exercise. The lat pulldown is typically performed with a wide grip, but can also be done with a narrow grip or underhand grip to target different muscle groups in the back and arms. It is a popular exercise for building upper body strength and improving posture.
exercises.author: Mariano_O

exercises.name: Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.description:
The dumbbell kickback is a popular strength training exercise that targets the triceps muscles in the back of your upper arms. It helps strengthen and tone the triceps, contributing to overall arm strength and aesthetics.
Among the exercises that work the arm muscles, kickback and its variations are very effective. You can easily apply these exercises with dumbbells, cables or resistance bands.
exercises.author: Mariano_O

exercises.name: Tuck L-sit
exercises.description: The tuck L-sit is a bodyweight hold where you support yourself on parallel bars, parallettes, or the floor with straight arms while pulling your knees toward your chest. Your hips stay lifted, your spine stays tall, and your feet hover off the ground. The goal is to keep your core tight, shoulders depressed, and arms locked out while maintaining the tucked position. It’s a core-intensive, shoulder-stabilizing static hold often used as a progression toward the full L-sit.
exercises.author: clafal

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat with Dumbbells
exercises.description: The Bulgarian split squat consists of performing a squat on one leg with the rear foot resting on a raised platform. Elevating your back leg on a bench creates instability and increases the range of motion of the exercise.
exercises.author: AlucardEvil40

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand sideways next to a low cable pulley. Grasp the single handle with the far-side hand across the front of your body. Keep your chest tall and maintain a slight bend in your elbow.

Movement:
1. Raise the cable handle out to the side leading with your elbow until your arm is parallel to the floor at shoulder height.
2. Pause briefly at the top to emphasize the peak contraction of the lateral deltoid.
3. Lower the weight slowly and under control back to the starting position.

Tips:
Avoid shrugging your traps or using momentum from your torso. The cable provides constant, smooth tension throughout the entire movement.
exercises.author: polloperro

exercises.name: Reverse Fly Standing
exercises.description:
Stand with a good posture holding a cable in each hand opposite the machine
Starting with the hands in front of your chest pull the arms out to
your side into the shape of a T with the elbows nearly straight
Slowly release the arms forward to the start
Repeat with the arms moving into the shape of a Y
Repeat with the arms in the shape of a W
Repeat with the arms in the shape of an L by your side
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Butchers Block Stretch
exercises.description:
Kneel down with the hands together
Rest the elbows on a bench in front of you and lower the chest down
Keep the elbows bent with good posture and hold
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.description:
Lie on your side so that you are resting a little weight on your shoulder blade to keep it still
Extend your arm to 90 degrees in front of you, resting on the floor/mat
Lift your hand with your elbow so that your fingers point to the ceiling and your palm points towards your feet
Keeping your elbow still, gently lower your palm toward the floor
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Horizontal Shoulder Flexion Stretch
exercises.description:
Raise your arm out to the side, placing your hand on a wall or doorway beside you at shoulder height
Turn your body away from your arm to stretch the chest, as far as is comfortable
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Doorway Pectoral Stretch
exercises.description:
Place the forearm vertically on a door frame or stationary object at head height
Step forward past the arm, keeping it still against the object to stretch the chest
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Shoulder Dumbbell Pendular Exercise
exercises.description:
Lean forward to rest your hand on a chair or other object, holding a dumbbell in the other hand
Gently swing the dumbbell in a circular motion
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Shoulder External Rotation with Dumbbell
exercises.description:
Lie on your side holding a dumbbell in your upper hand
Tuck your elbow into your side and rest the hand in front of you
Rotate the shoulder so the hand raises up
Lower the hand down
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Incline Scapular Push-Up
exercises.description:
Place your hands on the bench in a press up position
Push your chest away from the bench to separate your shoulder blades
Keeping your elbows straight, lower your chest towards the bench so your shoulder blades move closer together
Push your chest away from the bench again
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: One-Arm Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with your back to a high cable pulley. Grasp the single handle or rope attachment overhead with one hand, elbow bent and pointing forward next to your head.

Movement:
1. Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend your elbow to press the cable forward and slightly downward until your arm is fully extended.
2. Squeeze the triceps firmly at peak contraction.
3. Slowly bend your elbow to return to the stretched starting position under full control.

Tips:
Keep your core braced and your spine neutral. The overhead cable angle places a strong stretch on the long head of the triceps.
exercises.author: polloperro

exercises.name: Single-Arm High Cable Row
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set a cable pulley to a high position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine in a staggered stance, brace your non-working hand on the machine frame for stability, and grasp the handle with arm extended.

Movement:
1. Pull the cable handle diagonally toward your upper chest or ribcage, driving your elbow backward.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blade and upper back firmly at the end of the pull.
3. Slowly extend your arm to return to the starting position under full control.

Tips:
Keep your torso stationary and avoid twisting your hips or spine during the row.
exercises.author: polloperro

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling One-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set a cable pulley high and attach a single handle. Adopt a half-kneeling position on the floor, placing the knee on the working side on the ground and the opposite foot forward for balance. Grasp the handle with your arm extended overhead.

Movement:
1. Pull the handle down toward your shoulder, driving your elbow straight down toward your hip.
2. Squeeze your lat tightly at the bottom of the movement.
3. Slowly allow your arm to extend back overhead, feeling a deep stretch along the side of your back.

Tips:
Keep your torso upright and core engaged. The half-kneeling position prevents lower body sway and isolates the latissimus dorsi.
exercises.author: polloperro

exercises.name: Glute Kickback (Machine)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Position yourself on the glute kickback machine, resting your upper body against the support pad. Place the sole of your foot, emphasizing the heel, firmly against the footplate.

Movement:
1. Drive through your heel to push the plate backward and upward until your hip is fully extended.
2. Squeeze your glute firmly at the peak contraction point.
3. Slowly return the pedal back to the starting position under full control.

Tips:
Drive through the heel rather than your toes to isolate the gluteus maximus. Avoid hyperextending your lower back at the top of the movement.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Standing Adduction (Cable)
exercises.description:
Keep your hips square and still, pulling the cable across your opposing leg using only your inner thigh.
Don’t let your torso lean or twist — no side bending to help the rep.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Seated Row (Machine)
exercises.description:
Keep your chest up and squeeze your shoulder blades at the end.
Don’t hunch forward or round your back during the pull.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description:
Keep arms straight but not locked, pulling with your lats, not your shoulders.
Don’t let your shoulders shrug up during the movement.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Cable Standing Lateral Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description:
Keep your torso still, pulling the handle down along your side using the outer lat.
Don’t twist your body or rotate your torso to cheat the rep.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Shoulder Internal Rotation (Cable)
exercises.description:
Keep your elbow tucked to your side like it's superglued there.
Don’t rotate your torso — only your forearm should move.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Shoulder External Rotation (Cable)
exercises.description:
Keep elbow fixed at your side and rotate forearm outward smoothly.
Don’t let your wrist or elbow drift upward — stay in one plane.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Side Lateral Raise (Cable)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand sideways next to a low cable pulley. Grasp the single handle with your outside hand across the front of your body. Keep your torso tall and a slight bend in your elbow.

Movement:
1. Raise your arm out to the side leading with your elbow until it reaches shoulder height.
2. Pause briefly at the top to emphasize the lateral deltoid contraction.
3. Lower the handle slowly and under control back to the starting position.

Tips:
Lead the movement with your elbow, not your hand. Avoid shrugging your shoulder; keep your upper traps relaxed.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Front Raise (Cable)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand facing away from or toward a low cable pulley. Grasp the handle with an overhand grip in front of your thighs. Keep a slight bend in your elbow and engage your core.

Movement:
1. Raise the handle forward and upward in a smooth arc until your arm reaches shoulder height.
2. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the anterior deltoid.
3. Lower the handle slowly and under control back to the starting position.

Tips:
Maintain a steady posture without leaning back or swinging your torso to initiate the rep.
exercises.author: barry

exercises.name: Resistance Band Face Pull
exercises.description: Face pulls with band – standing horizontal pull. Grab the band at face height, pull elbows high and wide towards your face while squeezing shoulder blades together. Trains upper back, rear shoulders and improves posture.
exercises.author: 54str

exercises.name: Isometric Squat to Failure
exercises.description:
Isometric Squat to Failure: A Strength Training Technique
Definition
The isometric squat to failure is a variation of the squat exercise where you hold a static squat position at a specific angle, maintaining the position until your muscles can no longer sustain the contraction.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lunge with Kettlebell
exercises.description:
How to do a single-leg kettlebell lunge
Preparation: Stand with your feet together. Hold the kettlebell with both hands by the handle, keeping it close to your chest, or hold it with one hand (on the same side as the working leg).
Step and Lower: Take a large step forward (or backward, which is safer for your knees) with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees form a 90-degree angle.
Focus: Shift your weight onto your front (or bent) leg, keeping your back straight and your torso upright.
Return: Push off with your front leg to return to the starting position.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Single-leg side glute press
exercises.description:
The Single-Leg Side Glute Press is a leg press machine variation where you angle your body sideways on the pad, placing one foot high and slightly angled to press the weight, powerfully targeting the outer glute (gluteus medius/minimus) and hamstrings for balanced leg development and stability, requiring focus on pushing through the heel and maintaining control without locking out.
How to Perform:
Setup: Sit in the leg press machine, rotate your body to one hip, placing one foot high on the platform at about a 45-degree angle with toes pointed slightly out/forward.
Positioning: Keep your hip, knee, and ankle aligned, and ensure your lower back stays on the pad.
Descent: Slowly lower the weight, allowing your knee to bend deeply (near 90 degrees), feeling a stretch in your glute and hamstring.
Press: Drive through your heel (not your toes) to press the weight back up, squeezing your glutes and hamstrings, stopping just before your leg fully extends.
Control: Avoid bouncing and don't let your lower back lift off the pad; maintain tension throughout the movement.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift with Dumbbell
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with a slight bend in your knees, holding a dumbbell in one or both hands. Shift your weight onto your supporting leg (e.g., your right leg) and lift your non-supporting foot slightly off the floor.
The Hinge: Keeping your back flat and core engaged, hinge at your hips, pushing your glutes backward. As your torso lowers, extend your non-supporting leg straight back behind you for balance, keeping your hips square to the floor. The dumbbell(s) should lower toward the ground along the line of your supporting leg.
Range of Motion: Continue lowering your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, or you feel an intense stretch in your supporting hamstring, ensuring your back remains neutral throughout the movement.
Return to Start: Pause at the bottom, then contract your glutes and hamstrings to slowly raise your torso back to the starting position. Your non-supporting leg should return in line with the supporting one.
Switch Sides: After completing your desired number of repetitions on one side, switch your weight and repeat the movement on the other leg.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Assisted chin-ups
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Select the appropriate counterweight on the assisted pull-up machine. Place your knees on the padded platform and grasp the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip (palms facing you). Lower yourself into a controlled dead hang with arms extended.

Movement:
1. Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
2. Squeeze your lats and biceps firmly at peak contraction.
3. Lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are nearly fully extended.

Tips:
Use the machine assistance to focus on a full range of motion and strict control without swinging or kicking.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip pull-ups or TRX rows
exercises.description:
Pull-Up: Vertical Pull — Focuses more on the Lats (back width).
TRX Row: Horizontal Pull — Focuses more on the Rhomboids/Traps (mid-back thickness and posture).
exercises.author: 54str

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright on one leg. Bend your non-working leg behind you at the knee, grasping your ankle or foot with the hand on the same or opposite side.

Movement:
1. Hinge at your hips and bend your supporting knee to lower down in a controlled, single-leg squat.
2. Descend until the knee of your held leg lightly taps the floor behind you.
3. Drive firmly through your standing foot to extend your leg and return to the upright starting position.

Tips:
Lean your torso slightly forward to maintain balance. Control the descent carefully to protect the working knee.
exercises.author: Happy

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Lift one leg off the floor, either extended straight out in line with your opposite thigh or with the knee tucked toward your chest. Keep your arms resting by your sides for stability.

Execution:
1. Drive through the heel of your working foot to lift your hips toward the ceiling until your thighs, hips, and torso form a straight line.
2. Squeeze your glute firmly at the top of the movement and hold for 1 to 2 seconds.
3. Lower your hips slowly and under control back toward the floor without fully resting your weight, then begin the next repetition.

Cues:
Keep your pelvis level throughout the movement, preventing the non-working side from sagging or rotating.
exercises.author: Happy

exercises.name: L-Sit Pull-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Hang with your arms fully extended, then lift your straight legs directly in front of you to a 90-degree angle with your torso, forming an "L" shape. Brace your core and hip flexors tightly.

Execution:
1. Maintaining the strict L-sit position, pull yourself upward by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
2. Pause briefly at the top while keeping your legs locked horizontally.
3. Lower your body under strict control back to the full hang without letting your legs drop.

Cues:
Keep your knees fully extended and toes pointed; do not use momentum or kip.
exercises.author: Happy

exercises.name: Back Lever
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hang from a pull-up bar or gymnastics rings with an overhand or supinated grip. Pass your legs through your arms into an inverted hang (skin the cat position), facing downward toward the floor.

Execution:
1. Slowly lower your body from the vertical inverted hang until your entire body—from shoulders through hips and heels—forms a straight, horizontal line parallel to the ground.
2. Keep your arms completely straight, actively depress and retract your shoulder blades, and contract your glutes, spinal erectors, and core firmly.
3. Hold this static position for the prescribed duration while maintaining steady breathing.
4. Carefully exit the position under control by either pulling back into an inverted hang or lowering to a safe release.

Cues:
Do not allow the hips to sag or pike; progressively build up through tuck and advanced tuck variations to condition the bicep tendons and shoulder joint.
exercises.author: Happy

exercises.name: Hanging Windshield Wipers
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Engage your lats and shoulders, lean your torso slightly back, and raise your straight legs all the way up until your toes point toward the bar or ceiling.

Execution:
1. Keeping your legs straight and feet glued together, slowly rotate your hips and legs down to one side in a sweeping arc like a windshield wiper.
2. Reverse the direction by contracting your obliques and core, bringing your legs back through the vertical center.
3. Lower your legs to the opposite side under control and continue alternating from side to side in a continuous rhythm.

Cues:
Keep the movement strictly controlled with zero swinging; bend your knees into a tuck wiper if straight legs compromise form.
exercises.author: Happy

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise with Short Bar
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a short straight bar to the low pulley of a cable station. Stand facing away from the machine with the cable running between your legs. Grasp the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip (palms down) resting against your thighs. Maintain an upright posture with chest up, shoulders depressed, and a slight bend in your knees.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbows nearly straight, raise the bar upward and forward in a smooth arc until your hands are level with your shoulders.
2. Pause for a second at the top, focusing on the contraction in your anterior deltoids.
3. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control, keeping tension on the shoulders throughout.

Cues:
Avoid rocking your torso or hyperextending your lower back to swing the weight up.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Step under the Smith machine bar and rest it across your upper trapezius. Set your feet shoulder-width apart, positioned slightly in front of the bar's vertical plane to optimize knee mechanics and direct load to the quadriceps and glutes. Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists.

Execution:
1. Inhale and brace your core, then initiate the squat by bending at your hips and knees along the fixed track.
2. Descend under strict control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
3. Drive firmly through your whole foot and heels to return to the starting position.
4. Stop just short of locking your knees out at the top to maintain continuous tension.

Cues:
Keep your chest proud and spine neutral; adjust foot placement forward if you wish to reduce forward knee travel and maximize glute/quad emphasis.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Seated Machine Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit upright in the hip abduction machine with your back flat against the backrest. Place the outside (lateral aspect) of your knees and thighs firmly against the padded lever arms. Rest your feet on the footplates and grasp the side handles to stabilize your pelvis.

Execution:
1. Drive your legs outward against the pads by contracting your gluteus medius and outer hip muscles.
2. Open your legs to full comfortable abduction and pause for 1 to 2 seconds at peak contraction.
3. Slowly resist the weight as you bring your knees back toward the center without allowing the weight stack to touch down between reps.

Cues:
Keep your hips seated and torso stationary; do not use momentum or rock back and forth.
exercises.author: Tierrasverdes

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach a rope attachment to the lowest setting of a cable pulley. Stand facing away from the machine with the cable running between your legs. Grip the rope handles with both hands, take two steps forward to establish cable tension, and adopt a stance slightly wider than shoulder-width with a slight bend in your knees.

Execution:
1. Hinge at your hips, pushing your glutes backward while keeping your spine flat and shoulders packed.
2. Allow the rope to travel backward between your legs until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
3. Powerfully drive your hips forward to return to an upright standing position, squeezing your glutes firmly at the top.

Cues:
This is a hip hinge, not a squat. Keep your arms relaxed and straight; do not pull the weight with your upper body.
exercises.author: manuher89

exercises.name: Front-Crossing Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand sideways next to a low cable pulley. Grasp the single D-handle with your far (outer) hand so that the cable crosses in front of your body. Brace yourself with the inside hand on the cable tower and stand tall with a slight knee bend.

Execution:
1. With a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm out to the side until your hand reaches shoulder height.
2. Pause briefly at the top to emphasize peak contraction in the lateral deltoid.
3. Slowly lower your arm back across the front of your body under control, maintaining continuous tension.

Cues:
Focus the effort entirely on the side (lateral) deltoid; do not shrug your upper traps or lean away from the pulley.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand sideways next to a low cable pulley. Grasp the single D-handle with your far (outer) hand with the cable running behind your hips and back. Hold onto the cable tower with your inside hand and lean slightly forward for balance.

Execution:
1. Keeping a slight bend in your working elbow, raise your arm out to the side until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
2. Squeeze your lateral deltoid at the top of the range of motion.
3. Slowly lower the handle back behind your body, feeling the continuous resistance in the side shoulder.

Cues:
Running the cable behind your back prevents friction against your hips and maintains pure lateral deltoid recruitment without trap takeover.

exercises.name: 45° Scapular Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a pair of dumbbells in front of your thighs with a neutral to semi-pronated grip. Keep your chest up and shoulders pulled back and down.

Execution:
1. Raise the dumbbells upward along the scapular plane, approximately 30 to 45 degrees forward from purely out to your sides.
2. Lift until your arms reach shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and thumbs slightly tilted upward.
3. Pause for a split second at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly and under control to the starting position.

Cues:
Moving in the scapular plane (scaption) provides an ergonomically optimal, impingement-free path for the shoulder joint while thoroughly loading the lateral deltoid.

exercises.name: Cable Shoulder Y-Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Attach D-handles to the low pulleys of a dual-cable station. Stand in the center and grasp the handles with crossed arms (right hand grabs the left cable, left hand grabs the right cable). Begin with your hands crossed in front of your waist.

Execution:
1. Pull both arms upward and diagonally outward in a smooth sweeping motion until your arms form a "Y" shape above shoulder height.
2. Actively retract and depress your shoulder blades at the top, focusing on your lower trapezius and lateral deltoids.
3. Slowly lower your arms along the same diagonal path back to the crossed starting position.

Cues:
Maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows and avoid arching your lower back to complete the lift.

exercises.name: Plank Reach
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a forearm plank position with your elbows directly beneath your shoulders, forearms parallel, and feet slightly wider than hip-width apart to provide a stable base of support. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Slowly lift one arm from the floor and reach it straight out in front of you at shoulder height.
2. Hold the extended position for 1 to 2 seconds while actively resisting any rotation or tilting of your hips.
3. Return the forearm to the starting position under control, then immediately repeat with the opposite arm.
4. Continue alternating sides with steady, deliberate pacing.

Cues:
Focus on anti-rotation; keep your hips and shoulders completely square to the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Extend your arm down, then slightly lift your forearm
Extend your wrist in a supinated form (palm up)
Adjust cable height so that the cable handle is in your supinated hand
Perform the movement by
curling your palms and wrists upwards
(optional/variable) Pause at the top
Slowly return to the starting position
exercises.author: eufvksruh

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms at your sides, palms pressing into the floor for support. Raise your legs with your hips and knees bent at approximately 90 degrees.

Execution:
1. Contract your abdominal muscles and curl your knees toward your chest.
2. At the peak of the movement, actively curl your pelvis and lower back a few inches off the mat.
3. Hold the contraction at the top for 1 to 2 seconds while breathing out.
4. Slowly and under control, lower your pelvis back down until your thighs return to vertical, keeping abdominal tension engaged.

Cues:
Avoid kicking or using momentum with your legs; the movement must be driven purely by curling your spine with your abdominals.
exercises.author: eufvksruh

exercises.name: Legend Incline Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit in the incline bench of the Legend Fitness LeverEdge machine. Adjust seat height so that the converging handles align comfortably with your upper chest. Press your head, upper back, and glutes firmly against the back pad, and plant your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with a firm overhand grip.

Execution:
1. Drive through your palms to press the independent lever arms upward and inward along their converging arc until your arms are nearly fully extended.
2. Squeeze your upper chest (clavicular head) firmly at lockout.
3. Lower the weight slowly and under control, feeling a deep stretch across the pectorals before initiating the next repetition.

Cues:
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the back pad throughout the press.

exercises.name: Chair Dips
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit on the front edge of a sturdy chair or bench. Place your hands next to your hips gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward. Extend your arms and slide your hips forward so they hover just off the edge. Place your feet flat on the floor with knees bent (easier) or extend your legs out straight with heels on the floor (harder).

Execution:
1. Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows directly behind you, keeping your back close to the chair.
2. Descend until your upper arms are approximately parallel to the floor (90-degree bend in the elbows).
3. Press firmly through your palms to extend your arms, returning to the starting position with triceps locked out.

Cues:
Keep your torso upright and close to the chair; avoid flaring your elbows wide outward to protect your anterior shoulder capsule.
exercises.author: tinman

exercises.name: Pec Deck Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit facing the pad of a pec deck machine. Adjust the seat height so that the handles align with your shoulders. Rest your chest flat against the back pad, plant your feet firmly on the floor, and grasp the handles with a neutral or overhand grip with elbows slightly bent.

Execution:
1. Drive your elbows back and outward in a wide horizontal arc by contracting your posterior deltoids.
2. Pause for a second at peak contraction when your arms are in line with your torso.
3. Slowly resist the weight as you bring the handles back together to the starting position without allowing the weight stack to rest.

Cues:
Focus on pulling with the back of your shoulders; avoid shrugging your traps upward or relying solely on excessive scapular pinching.
exercises.author: eufvksruh

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Deadlift a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell from the floor with one hand like a suitcase. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders packed, and torso completely vertical. Brace your core and obliques tightly.

Execution:
1. Walk forward with slow, deliberate, and controlled steps in a straight line.
2. Actively resist the pull of the weight: keep your shoulders level and prevent your torso from tilting sideways toward the load (anti-lateral flexion).
3. Continue for the designated distance or time, set the weight down safely, and switch hands.

Cues:
Walk with tall posture as if balancing a book on your head; do not lean toward the weight or hike your opposite hip.
exercises.author: aboksz

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Place two weight plates, yoga blocks, or push-up handles slightly wider than shoulder-width on the floor. Place your hands on the elevated surfaces and assume a rigid plank position with feet together and core braced.

Execution:
1. Lower your body under strict control by bending your elbows at approximately 45 degrees to your torso.
2. Descend past hand level into the deficit until you feel a deep, comfortable stretch across your pectorals.
3. Powerfully press through your palms to return to the top plank position with arms fully extended.

Cues:
The deficit provides an extended range of motion; maintain complete core stiffness and only descend as deep as shoulder mobility safely allows.
exercises.author: Rottekongen

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie back on an incline bench set to an angle of 30 to 45 degrees. Position your eyes under the racked barbell, retract and depress your shoulder blades into the pad, and plant your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, unrack it, and stabilize it directly over your upper chest with straight arms.

Execution:
1. Inhale, brace your core, and lower the bar with control to your upper chest (just below the collarbones), keeping your elbows tucked at roughly 45 to 70 degrees from your torso.
2. Touch your chest lightly without bouncing the weight.
3. Press the bar forcefully upward along a slight arc back over your upper chest until your arms are extended.

Cues:
A 30- to 45-degree angle provides optimal recruitment of the clavicular (upper) pectoral head while minimizing excessive anterior deltoid strain.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Anchor one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment or corner. Stand facing the bar with feet shoulder-width apart. Cup the sleeve of the free end with both hands with interlaced fingers, arms extended in front of your chest. Keep a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.

Execution:
1. Lower the barbell in a controlled, wide arc down toward one hip, keeping your arms nearly straight.
2. Allow your torso to rotate and your back foot to pivot slightly while actively decelerating the weight using your obliques and core.
3. Reverse the motion by contracting your core, bringing the bar back to the top center, then lower it smoothly to the opposite hip.
4. Continue alternating in a smooth, continuous tempo.

Cues:
Do not bend your elbows excessively to turn it into an arm exercise; the power and control should originate from your rotational core.
exercises.author: aboksz

exercises.name: Unilateral Cross-Body Cable Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set the pulley of a cable station to its highest position. Stand slightly offset so the cable travels diagonally across your upper torso. Grasp the handle or cable ball with your far hand, maintain a slight forward hinge at the hips, and allow your arm to extend fully upward in line with the cable.

Execution:
1. Pull the cable diagonally downward and inward across your torso toward your hip, keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbow.
2. Drive your elbow tightly toward your ribcage, squeezing your latissimus dorsi and teres major hard at peak contraction.
3. Slowly let the cable guide your arm back up along the diagonal path into a full lat stretch before initiating the next rep.

Cues:
Aligning the cable across your body matches the natural anatomical fiber orientation of your lats for superior isolated recruitment.

exercises.name: Barbell Full Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Unrack a barbell from a squat rack across your upper trapezius (high-bar position). Take two steps back into a shoulder-width or slightly wider stance with toes angled outward 15 to 30 degrees. Inhale deeply into your belly to brace your intra-abdominal pressure, keeping your chest tall.

Execution:
1. Break at your hips and knees simultaneously, driving your knees outward in line with your toes.
2. Descend smoothly past parallel into full squat depth, keeping your torso upright and heels firmly anchored.
3. Pause briefly without bouncing out of the hole, then drive forcefully through your whole foot to return to a standing lockout.
4. Exhale at the top and reset your brace before the next repetition.

Cues:
Full depth maximizes quadriceps, adductor, and gluteus maximus recruitment; descend only as deep as you can maintain a neutral spine without excessive pelvic tuck (butt wink).
exercises.author: fabrice

exercises.name: Trap Bar Squat
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Step inside the center of a trap bar (hex bar) with your feet shoulder-width apart. Squat down with an upright torso posture and grip the neutral handles firmly. Pull your shoulders back, keep your chest high, and brace your core.

Execution:
1. Drive forcefully into the floor through your heels and midfoot, extending your knees and hips in unison.
2. Keep your chest up throughout the ascent to prioritize quadriceps and glute loading.
3. Stand fully upright at the top, squeezing your glutes and quads.
4. Lower the weight under control by breaking at the knees and hips until the plates touch the floor.

Cues:
Maintain a more upright torso than a conventional deadlift to emphasize knee flexion and quadriceps engagement while sparing the lower back.
exercises.author: kmcalderwood

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rocks
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a half-kneeling position on a mat with one knee down and the front foot flat on the floor, about a shin-length in front of you. Place your hands on your front thigh for balance.

Execution:
1. Slowly drive your front knee straight forward tracking over your toes while keeping your front heel glued firmly to the ground.
2. Glide forward into end-range ankle dorsiflexion until you feel a deep stretch in your calf and Achilles tendon.
3. Hold the stretch at end range for 2 to 3 seconds.
4. Gently rock backward to the starting position and repeat the rocking oscillation for reps before switching legs.

Cues:
Do not allow the front heel to lift off the floor; maintaining heel contact is essential for mobilizing the ankle capsule and soleus.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand sideways next to a low pulley cable machine. Reach your outer hand behind your glutes to grasp the D-handle. Hold onto the cable upright with your inside hand for support, and lean slightly forward with your chest proud.

Execution:
1. With a slight, fixed bend in your elbow, raise your arm outward and upward along your side until your hand reaches shoulder height.
2. Squeeze your lateral deltoid hard at the top of the movement for a full one-second pause.
3. Lower the handle back behind your body in a slow, controlled descent, keeping tension on the shoulder throughout.

Cues:
Routing the cable behind your back prevents the handle from bumping your hips and provides uninterrupted tension at the stretched position.
exercises.author: LEBRERO

exercises.name: Parallel Bar Support Hold
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand between a pair of parallel bars or dip station. Grasp the bars with a neutral grip and jump or press yourself up to a top support position with arms fully extended and locked out.

Execution:
1. Actively depress your shoulder blades, pressing your shoulders down away from your ears with a proud chest.
2. Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lock your legs together with pointed toes in a hollow-body position.
3. Maintain this rigid isometric hold for the prescribed duration while practicing controlled, steady breathing.
4. Step down safely under control when finished.

Cues:
Do not allow your shoulders to shrug up toward your ears or your lower back to collapse; maintain active scapular depression throughout.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie face-down on a flat bench or reverse hyper machine so that your hips rest right at the rear edge and your legs hang freely toward the floor. Firmly grip the bench or handles to anchor your upper body.

Execution:
1. Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings to raise your legs backward and upward in a smooth, controlled arc.
2. Lift until your legs are parallel with your torso, feeling a peak contraction in your glutes and spinal erectors.
3. Hold for a brief pause at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
4. Slowly lower your legs back toward the starting position under control before beginning the next rep.

Cues:
Focus on hip extension driven by the glutes and hamstrings rather than swinging your legs or hyperextending your lumbar spine.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Sphinx Pose
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
