Lie flat on your stomach on an exercise mat with your legs extended hip-width apart and the tops of your feet flat on the floor. Place your forearms on the mat parallel to each other, with your elbows aligned directly beneath your shoulders and palms facing down.

Execution:
1. Press your forearms and palms gently into the floor to lift your chest and head off the mat into a gentle backbend.
2. Draw your shoulder blades together and down your back, broadening your collarbones and keeping your gaze soft and forward.
3. Lightly anchor your pubic bone into the mat and engage your glutes slightly, keeping your lumbar spine relaxed and long.
4. Hold this position for several slow, deep breaths before slowly lowering back down.

Cues:
Focus on opening through your thoracic spine and chest rather than collapsing into your lower back.
exercises.author: Joculari

exercises.name: Open Book Thoracic Mobility Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side on an exercise mat with your hips and knees stacked and bent at a 90-degree angle to stabilize your lumbar spine and pelvis. Extend both arms straight out in front of your chest with palms together.

Execution:
1. Inhale and lift your top arm upward and backward in a sweeping arc like opening a book.
2. Rotate through your thoracic spine while keeping your pelvis, hips, and stacked knees firmly glued together.
3. Allow your head and eyes to gently follow your moving hand toward the floor behind you.
4. Exhale as you reach end range, enjoying the stretch across your chest and upper back for 1 to 2 seconds.
5. Inhale and slowly sweep your arm back to the starting position with palms touching.

Cues:
Keep the motion isolated to the mid- and upper back (thoracic spine); do not allow your top knee to slide backward off the bottom knee.
exercises.author: teus_ergaster

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side on an exercise mat with your hips flexed at approximately 45 degrees and knees bent at 90 degrees. Stack your legs directly on top of each other with your heels together. Support your head with your bottom arm and place your top hand on the floor or on your hip for stability.

Execution:
1. Keeping your feet and heels glued together, slowly raise your top knee toward the ceiling like an opening clamshell.
2. Lift as high as you comfortably can without allowing your hips or pelvis to rotate backward.
3. Squeeze your outer hip and gluteus medius at peak contraction for 1 to 2 seconds.
4. Slowly lower your knee back to the starting position under control before repeating.

Cues:
Keep your pelvis stacked perpendicular to the floor; do not roll backward. (A side-plank clamshell can be used as an advanced progression).
exercises.author: teus_ergaster

exercises.name: Dumbbell Tate Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a flat exercise bench holding a pair of dumbbells. Extend your arms directly over your chest as in the lockout of a bench press. Rotate your hands into a pronated grip with palms facing toward your feet and thumbs facing each other, keeping the inner heads of the dumbbells touching or close together.

Execution:
1. Keeping your upper arms fixed and elbows flaring outward to the sides, bend your elbows to lower the inner dumbbell heads toward the center of your chest.
2. Touch the dumbbells lightly against your sternum without resting the weight on your body.
3. Forcefully extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up to the starting position, focusing on "pushing your pinkies toward the ceiling" for peak triceps recruitment.
4. Squeeze your triceps firmly at lockout before beginning the next repetition.

Cues:
Keep the movement isolated to elbow extension; do not let your shoulders or upper arms swing during the press.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Set an incline bench to approximately 30 to 45 degrees. Lie face-down with your chest firmly supported against the pad, feet grounded, and neck neutral. Hold a pair of light dumbbells hanging straight down with a neutral or thumbs-up grip.

Execution:
1. With elbows slightly unlocked, raise the dumbbells upward and diagonally outward in a wide "Y" arc.
2. Focus on pulling through your rear deltoids and retracting your scapulae at peak height.
3. Squeeze firmly at the top when your arms are roughly level with your shoulders for a one-second pause.
4. Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position under full control.

Cues:
Resting your chest against the bench prevents body swaying and ensures strict, isolated posterior deltoid and upper-back recruitment.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart with External Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, chest upright, and shoulders set back and down. Grasp a light resistance band with both hands using an underhand (supinated) grip in front of your navel. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees and tuck your upper arms tight against your ribcage.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbows glued to your sides, rotate your forearms and hands outward away from each other, stretching the band.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down as your shoulders externally rotate.
3. Hold the end-range contraction for 1 to 2 seconds to stimulate the infraspinatus and teres minor.
4. Slowly return your hands to the front starting position under full control.

Cues:
Do not allow your elbows to flare away from your ribs; the movement must come strictly from glenohumeral external rotation.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Double-Leg Abdominal Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on a mat. Raise your legs into a tabletop position with your hips and knees flexed at 90 degrees. Press your lower back firmly into the floor so there is no gap. Place both palms on your thighs just above your knees.

Execution:
1. Push your hands as forcefully as possible against your thighs while simultaneously driving your thighs against your hands with equal force.
2. Lock in a maximal isometric contraction across your entire abdominal wall and deep core (transversus abdominis).
3. Hold this maximal isometric tension for 10 to 15 seconds while continuing to breathe shallowly and rhythmically.
4. Release the tension smoothly, rest for a moment, and repeat.

Cues:
Keep your lumbar spine glued to the floor throughout the effort; do not hold your breath.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Abdominal Draw-In Maneuver (ADIM)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with knees bent and feet flat on the floor (can also be performed in quadruped or seated). Place your fingertips on your lower abdomen just inside your hip bones to monitor muscle recruitment.

Execution:
1. Exhale fully through your mouth, emptying your lungs of air.
2. Gently pull your belly button inward and upward toward your spine as if zipping up a tight pair of jeans.
3. Maintain a neutral spine and stable pelvis without flattening your lower back into the floor.
4. Hold this deep contraction for 10 to 15 seconds while continuing shallow, steady breathing.
5. Slowly release the contraction and take a normal breath before repeating.

Cues:
This exercise specifically isolates the transversus abdominis, the deepest abdominal stabilizer responsible for core stability and waistline control.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Landmine Squat to Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or corner. Stand facing the barbell with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes angled outward 15 to 30 degrees. Cup the sleeve of the free end with both hands interlaced and hold it at mid-chest height just beneath your collarbones.

Execution:
1. Brace your core and descend into a deep squat, keeping your chest proud and heels planted until thighs are parallel to the floor.
2. Powerfully drive through your heels to stand up, utilizing the upward leg drive to thrust the barbell upward.
3. In one fluid motion, press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lean slightly into the bar at the top to support natural upward scapular rotation.
5. Lower the barbell with control back to chest level and seamlessly transition into the next squat repetition.

Cues:
Seamlessly link the squat and the press into a single explosive, coordinated full-body movement.
exercises.author: beagle

exercises.name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Rest a barbell across your upper trapezius. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest proud, and core firmly braced.

Execution:
1. Take a deliberate, controlled step backward with one leg, keeping your hips square.
2. Lower your hips vertically until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee hovers just above the mat (both knees at roughly 90 degrees).
3. Drive firmly through the heel and midfoot of your FRONT leg to stand back up to the starting position.
4. Repeat with the opposite leg, alternating sides, or complete all reps on one leg before switching.

Cues:
Push through the front heel rather than kicking off the rear foot to keep tension loaded on the lead glute and quadriceps.

exercises.name: Hammerstrength Decline Chest Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit in a Hammer Strength decline chest press machine with your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the back pad. Adjust the seat height so that the handles sit level with your lower chest. Plant your feet firmly on the floor and grasp the handles with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.

Execution:
1. Brace your core and drive through your palms to press the handles forward and slightly downward, keeping your elbows tucked at approximately 45 degrees.
2. Extend your arms to near lockout and strongly contract the lower (sternocostal) pectoral fibers.
3. Slowly lower the weight arms back under control until you achieve a comfortable stretch across your chest before the next repetition.

Cues:
Keep your head, upper back, and hips pressed firmly against the seat pad throughout the set.

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand between a pair of hanging gymnastics rings. Grasp the rings with a firm neutral grip and jump or press yourself up into a top support position with arms fully locked out.

Execution:
1. Actively turn the rings outward (Rings Turned Out / RTO) so that your palms face forward and thumbs point away from your body, preventing your forearms from resting against the straps.
2. Depress your shoulders firmly away from your ears and lock your elbows completely straight.
3. Lock into a hollow-body position: brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and hold your legs straight together with toes pointed.
4. Maintain this rigid isometric hold for the required duration while breathing steadily.

Cues:
Turning the rings out eliminates resting on the straps and maximizes chest, bicep, and anterior shoulder stabilization.

exercises.name: Floor Glider Hamstring Curls
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on the floor with your heels planted on sliding discs (or towels on a smooth floor). Keep your arms at your sides for stability. Drive through your heels to raise your hips into a glute bridge position, forming a straight line from knees to shoulders.

Execution:
1. Maintaining hip elevation, slowly slide your heels forward away from your body until your legs are nearly fully extended.
2. Pause briefly at full extension without allowing your glutes to touch the floor.
3. Powerfully curl your heels back toward your glutes by contracting your hamstrings, driving your hips higher as your heels arrive under your knees.
4. Repeat smoothly for the desired number of repetitions.

Cues:
Keep your hips elevated throughout both the extension and curl phases to maximize hamstring recruitment under full tension.

exercises.name: Trap-3 Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hinge forward at your hips to approximately 45 degrees with a flat spine and soft knees. Rest one hand on your knee or an incline bench for support. Let your working arm hang straight down with your thumb pointing upward. Actively depress and retract your working scapula.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbow locked straight, raise your arm diagonally forward and upward until your hand is roughly 15 to 30 degrees above your head.
2. Keep your shoulder blade held down away from your ear to isolate the lower trapezius (Trap 3).
3. Pause for 1 to 2 seconds at peak elevation, feeling the intense contraction in your mid-to-lower back.
4. Lower your arm smoothly back to the hanging starting position under control.

Cues:
Do not shrug your upper trap toward your ear; the goal is pure lower trapezius activation and upward scapular rotation.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell External Rotation
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit on an exercise mat or flat bench with one knee elevated and foot flat. Place the elbow of your working arm on top of your raised knee, bent at a 90-degree angle. Hold a light dumbbell with your forearm positioned horizontally forward.

Execution:
1. Keep your shoulder blade retracted and depressed away from your ear.
2. Rotate your forearm upward along a vertical arc until it is perpendicular to the floor.
3. Pause at the top for one second, feeling the contraction in your external rotators (infraspinatus and teres minor).
4. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to horizontal with control, feeling a gentle stretch at the bottom before repeating.

Cues:
Use a light dumbbell to prevent compensatory movements; keep your elbow anchored stably on your knee throughout.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Banded Shoulder Drills
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Attach a resistance band at shoulder or chest height to a sturdy anchor. Grasp the band with one hand and step away until there is light to moderate tension.
Execution: Perform controlled circular and rotational arm movements across multiple planes of motion to mobilize the shoulder joint and warm up the rotator cuff.
Tips: Maintain an upright posture and keep your core engaged. Move smoothly without jerking or rushing.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Solo Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Kneel on the floor in a half-kneeling lunge position (one knee on the ground, front leg bent at 90 degrees with the foot flat on the floor). Keep your torso upright.
Execution: Tuck your pelvis slightly, engage the glute of the trailing leg, and gently shift your hips forward until you feel a deep stretch in the front of your rear hip (hip flexors/psoas).
Tips: Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily, then switch sides. Avoid arching your lower back.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Bent-Leg Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on your back or sit upright. Grasp the back of your thigh with both hands.
Execution: Draw your thigh toward your chest while keeping the knee slightly bent. Extend your lower leg just enough to feel a comfortable stretch in the muscle belly of the hamstrings.
Tips: Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily, then switch sides. Keeping the knee slightly bent protects the sciatic nerve and focuses the stretch on the muscle tissue.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Extension Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor with your hands placed behind you about shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing backward or slightly outward.
Execution: Keep your arms extended and slide your hips and feet forward, moving your shoulders into extension until you feel a comfortable stretch across the anterior deltoids and chest.
Tips: Move only as far as comfortable without pain. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Banded Clamshell
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on your side (or in a side plank) with your knees bent and legs stacked. Place a mini resistance band around your thighs just above the knees.
Execution: Keeping your feet together, raise your top knee upward against the band's resistance like an opening clamshell. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips: Keep your pelvis stable and square; do not let your hips roll backward as you lift the knee.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Butterfly Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit upright on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees drop open to the sides.
Execution: Grasp your feet or ankles with your hands and gently draw your heels toward your groin. Keeping your spine long, allow your knees to ease downward toward the floor.
Tips: Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily. Avoid aggressive bouncing.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Frog Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin on your hands and knees (quadruped) and widen your knees as far apart as comfortable. Drop down onto your forearms, keeping your shins parallel and inner feet resting on the mat.
Execution: Keeping your spine neutral, slowly rock your hips backward toward your heels until you feel a deep stretch in your hip adductors and groin.
Tips: Rock gently forward and backward with control or hold the deep stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Seated Pancake Good Morning
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit tall on the floor in a wide straddle (pancake) position with your legs straight, knees extended, and toes pointing upward. Place your hands lightly behind your head.
Execution: Keeping your spine flat and chest open, hinge forward from your hips toward the floor until you feel a strong stretch in your inner thighs and hamstrings.
Tips: Engage your glutes and hamstrings to return smoothly to the upright position. Avoid hunching through your upper back.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Horse Stance (Side Splits)
exercises.description:
Stand as for a squat, with your feet wide and your toes pointed slightly outwards.
Gently squat into a deep, wide squat - your hips should be below your knees.
Hold for 3 to 5 seconds.
Come up under control, and repeat as needed.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Straddle L-Sit
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor in a wide straddle seated position. Place your hands on the ground between your thighs.
Execution: Press down firmly through your palms, lock your elbows, and lift your hips and extended legs off the floor, holding your legs horizontally.
Tips: Maintain full-body isometric tension through your core, hip flexors, and triceps for the required duration.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: L-sit
exercises.description:
Sit on the ground with your legs together and your arms by your sides. Push your body off the ground using your hands, maintaining the same sitting position so that your legs are straight and your feet do not touch the floor.
Hold for as long as required.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: L-Sit (Foot Supported)
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor or between parallettes with your legs extended in front of you. Place your hands on the ground next to your hips.
Execution: Press firmly through your palms to lift your hips and torso off the ground, keeping your heels resting on the floor to support a portion of your leg weight.
Tips: Keep your shoulders depressed away from your ears and engage your core and triceps. Hold the position isometrically for the target duration.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Calves foam roller
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor and place the foam roller horizontally beneath your calves (between the Achilles tendon and the back of the knee). Support yourself with your hands behind you and lift your hips slightly off the ground.
Execution: Slowly roll forward and backward from just above your ankles to just below your knees. Rotate your legs slightly inward and outward to target both the inner and outer calf muscles.
Tips: Pause on tender spots (trigger points) for 15–20 seconds while taking deep breaths.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Hamstring Foam roller
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor with the foam roller placed beneath the back of your thighs. Support your body weight on your hands behind you and lift your hips.
Execution: Slowly roll forward and backward from just below your glutes down to just above the back of your knees. Rotate your feet slightly inward and outward to cover the entire hamstring group.
Tips: Move with control and pause on tight areas to encourage myofascial release.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Foam Roller Anterior Tibialis
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin on hands and knees (quadruped) and place the foam roller beneath the outside front of your shin (on the tibialis anterior muscle, not directly on the shin bone).
Execution: Slowly roll forward and backward from just above the ankle to just below the knee, adjusting pressure with your hands and the supporting knee.
Tips: Avoid applying direct pressure onto the bony shin ridge. Focus on the soft muscle belly along the outer side of the lower leg.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Foam Roller Iliotibial band
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on your side with the foam roller positioned under the outer side of your bottom thigh, just below the hip joint. Support yourself on your forearm and place your top foot flat on the floor in front of you for stability and weight management.
Execution: Slowly roll along the outer thigh from just below the hip down to just above the knee joint.
Tips: Never roll directly over the hip bone or the knee joint. Regulate the pressure by pressing into the supporting foot and arm.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Foam Roller Quadriceps
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie face down on the floor with the foam roller positioned beneath the front of your thighs. Support your upper body on your forearms in a forearm plank position.
Execution: Slowly roll forward and backward from the top of the pelvic crease down to just above your kneecaps. Slightly angle your legs inward or outward to address all heads of the quadriceps.
Tips: Keep your abdominal muscles braced to protect your lower back from sagging into excessive extension.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Foam Roller Gluteus
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit directly on top of the foam roller. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee (figure-four position) and shift your weight slightly toward the side of the crossed leg. Support yourself with your hands behind you.
Execution: Roll with slow, controlled motions over the gluteal muscles and outer hip area.
Tips: Pause on tender spots (trigger points like the piriformis) for 15–20 seconds while maintaining steady breathing. Switch sides when finished.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Foam Roller Adductors
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie face down on a mat, supported on your forearms. Place the foam roller parallel to your body. Bend one leg out to the side at roughly a 90-degree angle and rest the inner thigh on top of the roller.
Execution: Slowly roll from just above the inner knee up toward your groin and back.
Tips: Adjust the amount of body weight pressed into the roller using your arms and supporting leg. Breathe steadily throughout.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Side stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand upright with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart. Lightly engage your core.
Execution: Raise one arm overhead and slowly bend your torso laterally toward the opposite side, letting the other hand slide down your outer thigh. Feel a deep stretch along your ribcage, obliques, and latissimus dorsi.
Tips: Keep your hips square and avoid rotating your torso forward or backward. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and place your hands on your hips.
Execution: Make smooth, wide circular motions with your hips, rotating in a clockwise direction before switching to counter-clockwise. Keep your torso relatively upright and allow your hip joints to move through their full available range.
Tips: Move with control and avoid jerking, focusing on lubricating the hip joints and warming up the surrounding musculature.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Hip Crossover
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie flat on your back with your arms outstretched to the sides in a 'T' shape (palms facing down). Bend your knees with feet flat or elevated.
Execution: Slowly lower your knees (or cross one knee over the body) toward the floor on one side, keeping both shoulder blades pinned firmly to the ground. You may gently turn your head toward the opposite side.
Tips: Hold the stretch in your outer hip, glutes, and lower back for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply into your abdomen before switching sides.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Ankle Roll
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit upright on a chair or the floor and elevate one foot so your ankle can move freely in all directions.
Execution: Slowly trace large circles with your toes, rotating your ankle through its full range of motion. Complete several repetitions clockwise, then reverse counter-clockwise.
Tips: Keep your lower leg and knee still so the rotation comes entirely from the ankle joint. Perform 10–15 rotations in each direction per foot.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Banded Ankle Mobility
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Anchor a heavy resistance band low behind you. Assume a half-kneeling position with your front foot inside the loop, positioning the band just below the ankle bones across the talus so it pulls backward and downward.
Execution: Slowly drive your front knee forward past your toes while keeping your heel firmly planted on the floor. Pause for 2–3 seconds at the end-range of dorsiflexion, then release.
Tips: The backward band tension mobilizes the talus bone and improves ankle dorsiflexion without joint pinch. Complete 10–15 controlled repetitions per leg.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Assume a half-kneeling lunge position with your back knee resting on a comfortable mat and your front knee bent at 90 degrees. Keep your torso tall and upright.
Execution: Squeeze the glute on the trailing leg and tuck your tailbone slightly. Gently glide your hips forward until you feel a targeted stretch across the front of your rear hip and upper thigh.
Tips: Maintain an upright spine without overarching your lower back. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily, then switch sides.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Lunge with Twist Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Step into a forward lunge with your front foot planted flat and your rear knee resting on the mat or hovering just above the ground.
Execution: Keeping your torso upright, extend your arms forward or place your hands in front of your chest, then slowly rotate your torso toward the side of the front leg.
Tips: Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes throughout the twist. Hold the stretch for a few seconds or perform 5–8 controlled rotations per side before switching legs.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Lying Figure Four Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Execution: Cross your right ankle over your left knee, creating a figure-four shape. Reach through and grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands, gently drawing the leg toward your chest until you feel a deep stretch in your right glute and piriformis.
Tips: Keep your head, neck, and shoulders relaxed on the floor. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Lying Hamstring Stretch with Band
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Lie flat on your back and loop a resistance band or strap around the ball of one foot. Hold the ends of the band firmly with both hands. The opposite leg rests straight or bent on the floor.
Execution: Extend the banded leg toward the ceiling and gently pull the band toward your chest until you feel an effective stretch through the belly of your hamstrings.
Tips: Avoid locking the knee into hyperextension; keep a micro-bend if needed. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds with calm breathing, then switch legs.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Pigeon Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Begin in a plank or tabletop position. Slide one knee forward behind your wrist and angle the shin diagonally across the mat. Extend the opposite leg straight back with the top of the foot resting on the floor.
Execution: Square your hips toward the floor and lower your pelvis. You can remain upright with hands on the mat or fold forward onto your forearms to deepen the stretch in the outer glute and hip of the front leg.
Tips: Keep your hips level and avoid tilting heavily to one side. Hold the stretch for 30 seconds while breathing deeply, then switch sides.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Quad Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall on one foot, lightly holding onto a wall or sturdy object for balance if needed.
Execution: Bend your opposite knee behind you, grasp the top of your foot or ankle with your hand, and gently pull your heel toward your glutes. Keep your knees close together and aligned.
Tips: Squeeze your glute and keep your pelvis tucked slightly to maximize the quadriceps stretch and avoid arching your lower back. Hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Runners Lunge Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Step forward into a deep lunge, placing both hands flat on the floor on either side (or to the inside) of your front foot.
Execution: Press through the ball of your back foot and extend your trailing leg straight back, allowing your hips to sink toward the floor. Keep your front knee stacked directly over the ankle.
Tips: Keep your chest lifted and spine long rather than rounding forward. Feel the stretch across the trailing hip flexor and front hamstring. Hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Standing IT Band Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand tall sideways next to a wall or sturdy support. Cross the outer leg (the one being stretched) behind the front leg, placing the foot flat on the floor.
Execution: Support yourself with your inner hand on the wall and gently push your hips toward the wall (away from the direction of your lean). Lean your torso in the opposite direction until you feel a distinct stretch along the outer hip and thigh.
Tips: Keep your pelvis facing forward without rotating. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then repeat on the other side.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Supported Calf Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place both palms flat on the wall at shoulder height.
Execution: Step one leg back into a staggered stance, keeping that trailing leg straight and pressing the heel firmly into the floor. Bend your front knee and lean your hips toward the wall until you feel a strong stretch in your back calf.
Tips: Ensure both feet point directly forward without turning outward. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.author: Davidgj32

exercises.name: Banded Scapular Retraction
exercises.description: Attach one end of resistance band to wall/upright/... at shoulder height. Insert arm into the loop, at the tricep. Step back until band is pulled straight. Pull back elbow and shoulder against the resistance of the band.
exercises.author: hurr99

exercises.name: Incline DB Y-Raise
exercises.description:
Set
an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit facing the bench, chest
against the pad, with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Position your feet firmly on the ground for stability and let your arms hang down naturally with a slight bend in your elbows.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Raise your arms forward and out to form a Y shape, keeping the movement controlled and your elbows slightly bent.
Lift until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor and in line with your ears.
Pause
briefly at the top of the movement to engage your shoulder muscles
fully, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Ensure
the movement is slow and controlled during both the ascent and descent
to maximize engagement of the deltoids and supporting muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.
exercises.author: Deflation

exercises.name: DB Wrist Extension
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on a bench and grasp two dumbbells with an overhand (pronated) grip. Rest your forearms across your thighs or knees with your wrists extending just past your knees.
Execution: Lower the dumbbells by allowing your wrists to flex fully downward toward the floor. Then raise the dumbbells by extending your wrists upward as high as comfortable, squeezing the forearm extensors at the top.
Tips: Keep your forearms stationary throughout the movement, isolating the wrist extension.
exercises.author: Deflation

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise from Waist Height
exercises.description:
Stand next to a cable machine with the pulley set to waist height.
Grab the opposite-side handle with the hand farthest from the
pulley, keeping your palm facing in.
Keep your core engaged, chest lifted, and shoulders relaxed. Maintain a slight bend in the elbow throughout the lift.
Lift your arm out to the side until your elbow reaches shoulder height, keeping your wrist aligned with your elbow.
Briefly pause at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to your side with control. Repeat for the desired reps.
exercises.author: Deflation

exercises.name: Shinbox IR Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor with both hips and knees bent at 90-degree angles.
Leg Placement:
Place one leg in front of you (external rotation) and the other leg out
to the side/behind you (internal rotation). The shins and knees should
remain flat on the ground.
The Movement:
Keeping your hips square, hinge your torso forward or tilt it laterally
(side-to-side) toward the front leg to deepen the stretch.
Target Areas:
Stretches the glutes and piriformis (front leg) and the hip flexors and
quads (back leg). Engages the core and obliques during lateral flexion.
Goal: Improves hip mobility, specifically internal and external rotation, and relieves lower back tension.
exercises.author: teus_ergaster

exercises.name: YTWL Exercise
exercises.description:
Purpose: Improves shoulder stability, posture, and scapular (shoulder blade) control. Often used in physical therapy and warm-ups.
Starting Position:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips (like a
deadlift) keeping your back flat, or lie face down on an incline bench.
Keep your thumbs pointing up throughout.
Y (Arms up):
Extend both arms straight forward and upward at a 135-degree angle from
your body, forming a "Y". Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the
top.
T (Arms out): Open your arms straight out to the sides, perpendicular to your body, forming a "T". Focus on pinching your shoulder blades.
W (Arms bent): Pull your elbows back, bending them to 90 degrees, and squeeze your shoulder blades to form a "W". Keep your wrists firm.
L (Arms rotated):
Start with elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate
your forearms outward (external rotation) like a goalpost, forming an
"L" or a gate.
Key Focus:
Movements should be slow and controlled. Always lead with the thumbs
and think about moving the shoulder blades, not just the arms.
exercises.author: teus_ergaster

exercises.name: Supine Hip Abduction
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your back (supine) on a mat, with your legs extended and
relaxed. Arms can be placed alongside your body or out to the sides for
stability.
The Movement:
Slightly lift one leg off the floor (keeping it straight or with a
slight bend). Move it laterally outward, away from the other leg, as if
stepping over a small obstacle.
Range of Motion:
Move the leg as far as comfortable without lifting your pelvis or
rotating your torso, feeling a stretch in the inner thigh and hip.
Return: Slowly bring the leg back to the starting position with controlled movement.
Goal: Improves lateral hip mobility (abduction) and strengthens the pelvic stabilizer muscles.
exercises.author: teus_ergaster

exercises.name: Decline Bench Leg Raise
exercises.description:
Setup: Lie on a decline bench with your head at the top and grip the handles.
The Start: Extend legs fully, keeping them slightly elevated to engage your core.
The Lift: Raise your legs toward the ceiling using your abs, not momentum.
The Squeeze: Pause and contract your lower abdominals at the top.
The Return: Lower your legs slowly to the starting position with control.
exercises.author: nishant0712

exercises.name: Overhead Barbell Press
exercises.description:
Setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Position: Rest the bar comfortably across your upper chest and front deltoids.
Press: Brace your core and press the bar straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Finish: Control the bar steadily back down to your upper chest.
exercises.author: nishant0712

exercises.name: Cable Rope Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Setup: Stand facing the cable, feet shoulder-width apart, with a slight forward lean.
Grip: Hold the rope with palms facing each other and elbows tucked tight to your ribs.
Execution: Push the rope down until arms are fully straight, pulling the ends apart at the bottom.
Control: Keep upper arms still and return to the start with a slow, controlled motion.
exercises.author: nishant0712

exercises.name: Clean and Press
exercises.description:
The First Pull: Lift the bar from the floor to knee-height by driving with the legs, keeping the angle of your back constant.
The "Power" Position: As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively shrug and extend your hips to create vertical momentum.
The Quick Elbow Turnover: In the catch phase, rotate your elbows rapidly under the bar to create a "shelf" on your front deltoids.
The Vertical Press: Press the bar in a straight line; your head should shift slightly forward once the bar clears your forehead to reach full lockout.
exercises.author: nishant0712

exercises.name: Weighted push-ups
exercises.description:
Setup: Begin in a standard plank position with a weight plate balanced securely on your upper back.
Alignment: Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, engaging your core to prevent your back from sagging.
Execution: Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle.
Ascent: Press through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
exercises.author: nishant0712

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Sit with your back and head firmly pressed against the backrest of the pec deck machine. Adjust the seat height so that the arm pads or handles are aligned with your mid-chest.
Execution: Grip the handles or place your forearms on the pads with a slight bend in your elbows. Bring your arms together in front of your chest in a smooth arc, squeezing your pectorals at peak contraction for 1–2 seconds.
Tips: Control the weight on the eccentric return, feeling a gentle stretch in your chest without letting your elbows travel excessively behind your shoulders.

exercises.name: Cable Pullback with Back Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Set the cable pulleys at hip to chest height and attach suitable handles. Grasp the handles, take a few steps back, slightly bend your knees, and hinge forward from the hips with a flat back, extending your arms forward.

Execution:
Pull the handles toward your torso while simultaneously extending your spine and driving your chest up. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at peak contraction. Slowly return under control to the hinged starting position with arms extended.

Tips:
Maintain core tension throughout and ensure the movement is controlled, combining horizontal pulling with spinal extension without jerking.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Alternating Leg Extension
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie on your back on an exercise mat with knees bent and feet hip-width apart resting on your heels. Place your arms by your sides for stability.

Execution:
Drive through your heels to raise your hips into a bridge until your thighs and torso form a straight line. Squeeze your glutes, then extend one leg straight out in line with your thigh while keeping your hips fully elevated. Return the foot to the floor and smoothly repeat with the opposite leg.

Tips:
Maintain a level pelvis and prevent your hips from dipping or twisting during the alternating extensions. Keep core and glutes continuously engaged.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Unilateral Lunges (Split Squats)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a staggered split stance with your front foot flat on the floor and your rear foot balanced on the ball of the foot. Place your hands on your hips and hold your torso upright.

Execution:
Lower your hips smoothly by bending both knees until your back knee hovers just above the floor and both knees form roughly 90-degree angles. Drive through the heel of the front foot to rise back up smoothly without pausing at the top. Perform all repetitions consecutively on one leg before switching sides.

Tips:
Maintain an upright posture and braced core throughout. Ensure your front knee tracks directly in line with your toes without collapsing inward.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Butterfly Superman
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie face down on an exercise mat with legs fully extended. Interlace your fingers behind your head with your elbows flared wide to the sides.

Execution:
Simultaneously lift your head, chest, and elbows off the floor by contracting your spinal erectors and upper back muscles. Retract your shoulder blades and raise your elbows as high as comfortably possible. Hold the peak contraction for 1 to 2 seconds, then slowly lower back down under control.

Tips:
Keep your gaze focused on the mat to maintain a neutral cervical spine rather than cranking your neck backward.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Lying Leg Circles
exercises.description:
Lay on the back and lift legs in perpendicular fashion, keeping the knees together.
Start making small circles in one direction with both of your knees with very small range of motion, focusing on abs and keeping your back in contact with the floor.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Kneeling Superman (Bird Dog)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Start on all fours on an exercise mat with hands directly beneath your shoulders and knees under your hips. Maintain a neutral spine and brace your core.

Execution:
Simultaneously reach one arm straight forward and extend the opposite leg straight back until both are parallel to the floor and aligned with your torso. Hold this static position for 2 to 3 seconds while maintaining complete core stability. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

Tips:
Do not allow your hips to tilt or rotate. Keep your neck neutral by looking down at the mat rather than looking forward.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Cat Plank
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin on all fours on an exercise mat with your hands directly under your shoulders and toes tucked. Lift your knees just an inch or two off the ground so you are supported on hands and toes.

Execution:
Actively push the floor away through your shoulders to round your upper and mid-back toward the ceiling, mimicking a cat arching its back. Tuck your pelvis slightly and draw your navel toward your spine, creating maximum contraction in your abs and serratus anterior. Hold this static shape for the target duration while maintaining steady breathing.

Tips:
Keep your knees hovering barely above the mat throughout; do not let them rise too high or touch down.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Seated Core Rotation (Russian Twist)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on an exercise mat with knees bent and heels initially resting on the floor. Lean your torso back at roughly a 45-degree angle until your abs engage. Lift your feet a few inches off the floor to balance on your sit bones.

Execution:
Rotate your torso smoothly from side to side, bringing your hands across to touch the floor beside each hip. Engage your obliques to control each turn and keep your hips stable.

Tips:
Maintain a tall, proud chest and neutral spine; avoid slouching or simply swinging your arms without rotating your torso.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge (Unilateral Hip Thrust)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on your back on a mat. Bend one knee and place that foot firmly on the floor close to your glutes. Extend the opposite leg straight out in line with your thigh or upward toward the ceiling. Place your arms by your sides for support.

Execution:
Drive through the heel of your working foot to elevate your hips until your torso and thigh form a straight line. Squeeze your glute firmly at the top for a brief pause. Slowly lower your hips back toward the floor under control without resting completely, then immediately repeat. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

Tips:
Keep your hips level throughout the entire movement and prevent your pelvis from tilting or dropping on the unsupported side.
exercises.author: cybro

exercises.name: Parallel Bar Support Hold
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand between parallel dip bars. Grasp the bars with a neutral grip and press yourself upward until your arms are fully extended and your feet are suspended off the floor.

Execution:
Maintain a static hold at the top of the dip position with straight arms (elbows locked without hyperextending). Actively depress your shoulders by pushing down into the bars, keeping your chest proud and your core and glutes braced. Hold this position steadily for the target duration.

Tips:
Do not allow your shoulders to shrug up toward your ears; maintain continuous scapular depression and a rigid body line throughout the hold.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Abduction (Fire Hydrant)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Start on all fours on a mat with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Place an optional mini-band just above your knees for added resistance. Engage your core to keep your back flat and stable.

Execution:
Keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle, raise one leg out to the side until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor. Focus on contracting your gluteus medius and keep your pelvis level without twisting your spine. Slowly lower your knee back toward the starting position without resting it on the floor. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching.

Tips:
Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back—do not rotate or shift your weight excessively to the opposite side.
exercises.author: treder

exercises.name: Tuck Planche
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor or parallettes, with fingers pointed forward or slightly turned out.

Execution:
Press forcefully into the floor with fully straightened arms and lean your shoulders forward past your wrists. Pull your knees tightly into your chest into a compact tucked position, lifting your entire lower body off the ground. Actively protract your shoulder blades to create an arched hollow upper back and brace your core intensely. Hold this isometric position steadily for time.

Tips:
Keep your elbows locked straight throughout the hold. Generate maximum pressing power from your anterior deltoids and serratus anterior.
exercises.author: ISSACS

exercises.name: Legend Plate-Loaded Chest Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Adjust the seat height on the plate-loaded chest press machine so that the handles align with your mid-chest. Sit with your back and head firmly against the backrest and grip the handles. Retract and depress your shoulder blades.

Execution:
Press the handles forward in a smooth, converging motion until your arms are extended without locking your elbows. Squeeze your pectorals firmly at peak contraction. Slowly lower the handles back under control until you feel a deep stretch in your chest, then smoothly begin the next repetition.

Tips:
Keep your shoulder blades pinned against the pad throughout each rep to keep tension strictly on the chest and protect the anterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Extreme Chest Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie face up on a flat bench holding light dumbbells, or stand alongside a sturdy door frame or rack post with your arm positioned at shoulder height against the surface.

Execution:
Slowly allow your arms to sink out and down into a deep chest fly position, producing an intense, sustained stretch across your pectorals. Breathe deeply into your ribcage and hold this position under control for 30 to 60 seconds without bouncing.

Tips:
The sensation should be a strong muscle stretch without sharp shoulder discomfort. Excellent as an end-of-workout stretch to improve flexibility and tissue recovery.

exercises.name: Extreme Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your back to a flat bench or waist-height bar. Place both hands behind you on the edge, palms facing down, or hold a sturdy post behind you.

Execution:
Carefully lower your hips or take a small step forward to guide your arms into extension behind your torso. Keep your chest high and shoulder blades drawn together until you feel a deep stretch in the front and lateral deltoids. Hold steadily for 30 to 60 seconds while taking slow, deep breaths.

Tips:
Do not let your shoulders roll forward or shrug up toward your ears. Perform post-workout to relieve tightness from heavy pressing.

exercises.name: Extreme Lat Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand facing a sturdy upright post or power rack. Grasp the upright overhead with one or both hands using a secure grip.

Execution:
Step back, hinge at your hips, and push your glutes backward while lowering your chest toward the floor. Shift your bodyweight back against your grip so you feel a deep stretch along the lateral side of your back, running from your armpit down to your hip. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds while breathing deeply into your ribs.

Tips:
Relax your neck and allow your lats to elongate with every exhalation; do not force or jerk the movement.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Chest Fly
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Place an upright bench centered between two cable pulleys adjusted to chest or shoulder height. Sit back against the backrest with your feet flat on the floor and grasp the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

Execution:
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide hugging motion, keeping a slight, rigid bend in your elbows. Squeeze your pectorals forcefully as your hands meet. Slowly open your arms back to the starting position under full control until you feel a comfortable stretch in your chest, then repeat.

Tips:
Keep your spine firmly supported against the backrest and maintain consistent elbow flexion throughout.
exercises.author: shushu

exercises.name: gym80 3008 Abdominal Crunch Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the gym80 3008 Abdominal Crunch machine. Adjust the seat and leg pads so that the machine's pivot axis aligns precisely with your lumbar spine. Rest your upper torso against the chest pad and lightly hold the handles.

Execution:
Exhale and curl your torso forward and down by flexing your spine through maximal contraction of your rectus abdominis. Pause and squeeze your abs tightly at peak contraction for one second. Slowly resist the weight as you return to the upright starting position without letting the stack slam.

Tips:
Initiate and drive the entire movement with your abdominal muscles; do not pull with your arms or push through your feet.

exercises.name: Barbell Silverback Shrug
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart holding a barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Soften your knees and hinge forward at the hips to roughly a 45-degree torso angle while keeping a flat back. The barbell hangs straight down with arms extended.

Execution:
Without bending your elbows, elevate and retract your shoulder blades upward and backward toward your spine. Squeeze your traps and rhomboids firmly at the top for one full second. Slowly lower the barbell back down under control to achieve a full stretch before the next repetition.

Tips:
Maintain a rigid spine throughout; do not use hip drive or knee bounce to heave the weight up. The bent-over angle shifts tension to the mid traps and rhomboids.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown (Inverted Lat Pulldown)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit at a lat pulldown station and adjust the thigh pads so your legs are firmly anchored. Grasp the bar with a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip. Sit tall with your chest lifted and a slight arch in your upper back.

Execution:
Pull the bar smoothly downward toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and slightly back. Retract your shoulder blades and squeeze your lower lats and biceps firmly at the bottom. Slowly guide the bar back to the starting position under full control until your lats are completely stretched.

Tips:
Do not lean excessively backward to swing the weight down; keep your torso stationary to maximize latissimus tension.
exercises.author: amaesc

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row with V-Grip
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit at a low cable row station with your feet planted securely on the footrests and knees slightly bent. Grasp the V-bar handles with a neutral grip, sit upright with a flat back, and lift your chest.

Execution:
Pull the V-handle smoothly into your lower abdomen by drawing your elbows back close to your sides. Retract your shoulder blades tightly at peak contraction. Slowly return the weight forward under control, allowing your arms to fully extend and feeling a stretch in your lats before beginning the next rep.

Tips:
Avoid excessive forward and backward torso swinging; maintain a stable torso angle to keep continuous tension on the lats and mid-back.
exercises.author: amaesc

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Band Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Anchor a resistance band overhead to a pull-up bar or high anchor point. Stand facing the anchor, grasp the band with both hands using an overhand grip, and step back until tension is established. Hinge slightly forward at your hips with a flat back and extend your arms overhead with a slight, locked bend in your elbows.

Execution:
Pull the band downward in a sweeping arc toward your thighs, driving the motion strictly through your lats. Squeeze your lats and rear delts firmly at the bottom for one full second. Slowly allow the band to return upward under control until you feel a complete stretch along your sides.

Tips:
Keep your elbows rigid; do not bend or extend at the elbow joint during the pull, as that shifts tension from the lats to the triceps.
exercises.author: amaesc

exercises.name: Dumbbell Spider Curl
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie face down on an incline bench set to approximately 45 degrees, with your upper chest resting comfortably near the top and toes braced on the floor. Hold a pair of dumbbells with an underhand (supinated) grip, arms hanging vertically toward the floor.

Execution:
Curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders by flexing your elbows while keeping your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to the floor. Squeeze your biceps forcefully at peak contraction for one full second. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down under complete control until your arms are fully extended.

Tips:
The prone chest support prevents torso swinging or momentum; focus entirely on strict elbow flexion and peak biceps recruitment.
exercises.author: amaesc

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your arms resting beside your hips for stability. Raise your legs with your hips and knees bent at approximately 90 degrees.

Execution:
Contract your abdominals to curl your pelvis off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest in a smooth, controlled motion. Pause briefly at the top to emphasize abdominal contraction. Slowly unroll your spine and lower your pelvis back to the floor under control without letting your feet touch down.

Tips:
Initiate the movement by rolling your pelvis rather than kicking your legs or pushing hard through your arms.
exercises.author: amaesc

exercises.name: Belt Squat Machine
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand on the foot platforms of the belt squat machine and fasten the dipping belt securely around your hips. Attach the belt chain to the machine's loading arm, position your feet shoulder-width apart, and hold the balance handles lightly.

Execution:
Release the safety lever and descend into a deep squat by hinging your hips and bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the platform or lower. Maintain an upright torso. Drive through your mid-foot and heels to return to standing, contracting your quads and glutes firmly at the top.

Tips:
Because the load is attached directly to the hips, the belt squat completely spares the spine and shoulders from axial compression while delivering heavy leg overload.

exercises.name: One-Arm Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand sideways to a cable tower with the pulley set to shoulder height. Reach across your chest with your outside hand to grasp the cable or single handle. Maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbow and keep your core braced.

Execution:
Pull the cable horizontally across your body in a wide arc until your arm extends straight out to your side, squeezing your rear deltoid and upper back firmly at full contraction. Slowly return the cable across your chest along the same path under complete control.

Tips:
Keep your torso stationary and hips squared forward; do not twist your torso to gain momentum.
exercises.author: Dulive

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin on all fours on an exercise mat with your hands directly beneath your shoulders and your knees directly beneath your hips. Start with a neutral, flat spine.

Execution:
Inhale deeply as you tilt your pelvis forward, allowing your belly to sink gently toward the floor while lifting your chest and gazing softly forward into Cow pose. Exhale slowly and fully as you tuck your tailbone, draw your navel toward your spine, and round your entire back toward the ceiling into an arched Cat pose, letting your head relax down. Flow between these two shapes for 8 to 12 breath cycles.

Tips:
Move articulately through each segment of your spine rather than forcing end-range hyperextension.

exercises.name: Controlled Articular Rotations for Neck (Neck CARs)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand or sit upright with tall posture. Pull your shoulder blades down and back, bracing your core lightly to isolate your cervical spine.

Execution:
Tuck your chin slowly toward your chest. Glide your chin along your right collarbone toward your right shoulder, gently tip your right ear back toward your right shoulder, and trace a smooth arc across the ceiling into extension without pinching your neck. Continue rolling over to your left shoulder, sweep your chin down the left collarbone, and return to center. Perform 3 slow, controlled rotations, then reverse direction.

Tips:
CARs require intentional muscle irradiation and maximum control throughout the pain-free range of motion; ensure only your neck moves while your shoulders and torso remain completely still.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing (Belly Breathing)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie comfortably on your back on a mat, optionally with your knees slightly bent and feet flat on the floor. Place one hand flat on your chest and the other on your upper abdomen just below your ribcage.

Execution:
Inhale slowly and deeply through your nose, expanding your abdomen outward so that the hand on your belly rises while the hand on your chest remains nearly still. Pause softly for 1 to 2 seconds at the top of the breath. Exhale slowly and completely through parted lips or nose, allowing your belly to sink downward. Repeat for 8 to 10 slow, relaxed breath cycles.

Tips:
Keep your neck, shoulders, and jaw relaxed; diaphragmatic breathing engages the parasympathetic nervous system and re-establishes healthy intra-abdominal pressure patterns.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Snatch
exercises.description:
Key Steps to Execute Correctly:
Setup: Place the dumbbell between your feet, with your shoulders above your hips, chest up, and back flat.
The Pull: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) to drive the dumbbell upward, keeping your elbow high and the dumbbell close to your body.
The Catch: Quickly flex your hips and knees to drop under the dumbbell and receive it overhead with your arm locked in position, landing in a half-squat stance.
Common Mistakes: Using your arms too much to lift the weight instead of your legs, having a low elbow during the pull phase, and misaligning your shoulder, elbow, and wrist in the final position. For beginners, it’s recommended to start with light loads, focus on technique, and perform 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 5 reps per arm.
exercises.author: Aleid

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand in a wide sumo stance with your feet well outside shoulder-width and your toes angled slightly outward. Keep your torso upright and clasp your hands in front of your chest.

Execution:
Shift your bodyweight onto one leg and squat deeply while keeping the opposite leg fully extended out to the side. As you descend, rotate the foot of the straight leg upward so your toes point to the ceiling with your heel anchored on the floor. Sink as low as your mobility allows while keeping the heel of your working foot flat on the ground and your chest proud. Drive through your working heel to return to center and smoothly descend onto the opposite side.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine (5-10 reps each side). Builds unilateral leg strength while dramatically improving adductor flexibility and ankle dorsiflexion.
exercises.author: jesusd

exercises.name: Limber 11 Mobility Routine
exercises.description:
The Limber 11 routine by Coach Joe DeFranco is a renowned lower-body warm-up and mobility circuit designed to optimize hip function, relieve tightness, and prepare the body for heavy lifting or athletics:

1. Foam Roll IT Band (10-15 passes each side)
2. Foam Roll Adductors (10-15 passes each side)
3. SMR Glutes with Lacrosse Ball (30 sec - 2 min each side)
4. Bent-Knee Iron Cross (5-10 reps each side)
5. Roll-Overs into V-Sits (10 reps)
6. Rocking Frog Stretch (10 reps)
7. Fire Hydrant Circles (10 forward / 10 backward each side)
8. Mountain Climbers (10 reps each leg)
9. Cossack Squats (5-10 reps each side)
10. Seated Piriformis Stretch (20-30 sec each side)
11. Rear-Foot-Elevated Hip Flexor Stretch (5-10 reps with 3s hold each side)
exercises.author: Pete-E automation probe

exercises.name: Foam Roll IT Band
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie on your side on an exercise mat with a foam roller positioned under the outside of your thigh just below your hip joint. Support your upper body with your forearms and cross your top leg over in front with your foot flat on the floor to regulate pressure.

Execution:
Slowly roll back and forth along the lateral aspect of your thigh from just below the hip down to just above the knee joint. Pause on tight or tender trigger points for several deep breaths to encourage tissue release. Complete 10 to 15 slow, deliberate passes per side.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Do not roll directly over the knee joint or hip bone; use your supporting limbs to manage the degree of bodyweight pressure.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: SMR Glutes with Lacrosse Ball
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on the floor and place a firm massage or lacrosse ball under one of your glutes. Support your torso with your hands behind you. For a deeper release, cross the ankle of the targeted leg over the opposite knee into a figure-four position.

Execution:
Shift your weight onto the ball and roll gently with small, controlled movements across the gluteus maximus, medius, and piriformis to identify tight knots or tender trigger points. When you find a tender spot, pause and maintain direct pressure for 20 to 30 seconds while taking slow, deep breaths until the tension dissipates. Spend 30 seconds to 2 minutes on each side.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Relax your breathing and consciously let the muscle sink into the ball; avoid rolling directly onto bony landmarks like the tailbone.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Iron Cross
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat. Extend your arms out to your sides in a "T" position at shoulder height with palms facing down. Lift your legs and bend both hips and knees to 90 degrees, shins parallel to the floor.

Execution:
Keeping both shoulders pinned flat to the floor, slowly lower your stacked knees down to the right side until they hover just above the floor or gently touch down. Engage your obliques to pull your knees back to the vertical starting position, then smoothly lower them to the left side. Perform 5 to 10 dynamic repetitions per side.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Keep both shoulder blades firmly anchored to the floor throughout the rotation to mobilize the lumbar spine safely.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Roll-Overs into V-Sits
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit tall on an exercise mat with your legs extended straight out in front of you.

Execution:
Round your spine and roll smoothly backward onto your upper back, lifting your hips and bringing your legs overhead into a rollover/plow position to dynamically stretch your posterior chain. Use controlled forward momentum to roll back up into a seated position, spreading your legs wide into a "V" straddle. As you sit up, reach your hands forward between your legs to deeply stretch your hamstrings and groin. Immediately roll back and repeat for 10 fluid repetitions.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Keep your neck relaxed and support your weight across your upper back and shoulders rather than your cervical spine.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant Circles
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Begin on all fours on an exercise mat with your hands beneath your shoulders and your knees beneath your hips. Keep your core braced and spine neutral.

Execution:
Keeping your working knee bent at 90 degrees, lift it out to the side like a fire hydrant and trace a large, smooth circle with your hip and knee. Complete 10 large circles in a forward direction, then immediately reverse and complete 10 circles in a backward direction. Repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Avoid twisting or tilting your pelvis; isolate the circular motion strictly to the hip capsule to activate the gluteus medius.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Seated Piriformis Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit tall on the edge of a chair or bench with feet flat on the floor. Cross the ankle of one leg over the opposite knee into a figure-four position, letting the bent knee open outward.

Execution:
Maintain an upright posture with a proud chest. Hinge forward at your hips, keeping your back flat, until you feel a deep, focused stretch in the glute and piriformis of the crossed leg. Hold the static stretch for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing smoothly, then switch sides.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Do not round your lower back to reach forward; hinging from the hips with a flat spine produces optimal stretch on the deep hip rotators.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a half-kneeling stance in front of a flat bench, box, or wall. Rest the top of your rear foot elevated on the surface behind you with a mat beneath your kneeling knee. Keep your front foot planted with knee at 90 degrees.

Execution:
Keep your torso completely vertical. Posteriorly tilt your pelvis and contract the glute on your rear leg, gently shifting your hips forward until you feel a strong stretch in the front of your rear hip and quad. Hold the stretch for 3 seconds, ease off slightly, and pulse through 5 to 10 dynamic repetitions before switching sides.

Tips:
Part of Joe DeFranco's Limber 11 routine. Avoid arching your lower back; engaging the glute is the key to safely opening the psoas and rectus femoris.
exercises.author: Pete-E automation

exercises.name: Step Jack (Low-Impact Jumping Jack)
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your feet together and your arms resting at your sides. Brace your core lightly.

Execution:
Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms outward and overhead in a wide arc. Step your right foot back to center and lower your arms. Immediately repeat the movement by stepping your left foot out to the opposite side as your arms swing overhead. Continue alternating sides at a brisk, rhythmic pace.

Tips:
The Step Jack delivers cardiovascular conditioning without the joint stress of high-impact jumping, making it ideal for warm-ups or low-impact workouts.
exercises.author: Anon#2

exercises.name: Slow Squat
exercises.description:
A tempo-based squat that uses controlled movement to increase muscle tension and improve lower-body stability.

Lower: Descend slowly for 3 seconds.
Pause: Hold at the bottom for 1 second.
Stand: Return to the starting position at a normal pace.
Form: Keep your chest up and weight in your heels.
exercises.author: Anon#2

exercises.name: Wide Push-Up
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Assume a high plank position on the floor with your hands placed noticeably wider than shoulder-width apart (roughly 1.5 times shoulder width) and fingers pointing slightly outward. Form a straight line from your head to your heels with your core and glutes braced.

Execution:
Lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled descent by bending your elbows out at roughly a 45- to 60-degree angle until your chest hovers just above the mat. Pause briefly at the bottom, then press through your palms to return forcefully to the starting plank position.

Tips:
The wide hand placement places greater emphasis on the outer chest and anterior deltoids while reducing triceps leverage. Do not allow your lower back to sag.
exercises.author: Anon#2

exercises.name: Standing Knee Raise
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides or held with elbows bent at 90 degrees in front of your chest. Engage your core.

Execution:
Raise one knee smoothly toward your chest until your thigh is at least parallel to the floor, balancing firmly on your standing leg. Lower the foot with control and immediately drive the opposite knee upward. Continue alternating legs in a steady, rhythmic marching tempo.

Tips:
Keep your chest tall and avoid leaning backward as the knee rises; drive the movement with your hip flexors and lower abdominals.
exercises.author: Anon#2

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description:
Begin in a half kneeling position with the
leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall
with a ball.
With both hands directly in front of
you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach
the wall behind you.
Exhale as you rotate, inhale
as you return to neutral and repeat.
exercises.author: amwang4

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Sit on a workout bench adjusted to an upright incline (roughly 75 to 85 degrees). Bring a pair of dumbbells to shoulder height with palms facing forward and elbows bent at 90 degrees. Plant your feet firmly on the floor and pin your upper back against the bench.

Execution:
Press the dumbbells smoothly and vertically overhead until your arms are extended without locking out your elbows. Bring the dumbbells close together at the top without banging them. Pause briefly, then lower the weights slowly under control back to ear/shoulder level.

Tips:
Maintain a firm core and keep your back supported by the bench; avoid hyperextending your lumbar spine to press heavy loads.
exercises.author: Cf

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart (or sit tall on a bench). Hold a single dumbbell at shoulder level with your elbow positioned directly below your wrist, palm facing forward or slightly turned inward. Place your non-working hand on your hip or extend it for balance.

Execution:
Press the dumbbell vertically overhead in a smooth, controlled motion until your arm is fully extended without locking the elbow. Keep your core braced tight to prevent your torso from leaning or twisting. Slowly lower the dumbbell under full control back to shoulder level. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

Tips:
The unilateral nature of this exercise engages your core for lateral stabilization and corrects strength disparities between shoulders.
exercises.author: evtimovgeorg

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Single-arm cable pushdown is a unilateral isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii. By working one arm at a time, it helps correct strength imbalances between sides while also engaging the core for stability.
Starting position:
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a single handle to the high pulley. Grab the handle with one hand using an overhand grip (pronated), with your elbow bent at approximately 90° and tucked close to your body. Keep your core braced and your back straight.
Execution:
Push the handle downward in a controlled motion by extending your elbow until your arm is fully extended. Hold the contraction for 1 second at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.author: evtimovgeorg

exercises.name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
exercises.description:
Starting position:
Stand directly over a kettlebell in a wide sumo stance with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes angled outward at roughly 30-45 degrees. Hinge your hips backward and bend your knees with a flat back to grasp the kettlebell handle with a firm double-overhand grip.

Execution:
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles by driving forcefully through your heels and glutes. Direct that upward momentum into a vertical pull, raising the kettlebell close to your torso while leading with your elbows flared high and wide until the bell reaches collarbone level. Lower the kettlebell smoothly back down along the same path and flow into the next rep.

Tips:
The power must be generated by the explosive hip extension of the posterior chain, with the upper back and shoulders smoothly guiding the weight upward.
exercises.author: wgerpott

exercises.name: Mentzer Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit at a lat pulldown station and adjust the thigh pad so your thighs are firmly secured. Grasp the bar with a close underhand (supinated) grip, shoulder-width or slightly narrower, with palms facing you.

Execution:
1. Keeping your chest high and torso nearly upright, pull the bar smoothly down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
2. Hold the peak contraction at the bottom for 1 to 2 seconds, squeezing your lats and biceps firmly.
3. Slowly resist the weight as you return the bar back up through a full range of motion until your arms are fully extended.

Cues:
Maintain an upright posture without excessive backward swinging; focus on a full stretch at the top and a hard squeeze at the bottom.
exercises.author: Mike Mentzer

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit at a lat pulldown machine and grasp a single D-handle with a neutral grip (palm facing inward). Keep your chest lifted, torso stable, and shoulder blades depressed.

Execution:
1. Pull the handle smoothly downward toward your upper chest and clavicle by driving your elbow down and tight to your ribcage.
2. Squeeze your latissimus dorsi firmly at the bottom of the movement for 1 second.
3. Slowly let the handle return overhead under full control until your arm is fully extended and you feel a complete lat stretch.
4. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other arm.

Cues:
Avoid twisting your torso or leaning to the side; keep your shoulders square and your core braced.
exercises.author: evtimovgeorg

exercises.name: Hip Airplane
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand on one leg, lightly touching a wall or sturdy support for balance if needed. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back while extending your non-working leg straight behind you, until your torso and back leg form a horizontal line.

Execution:
1. Slowly rotate your pelvis inward toward the standing leg (internal hip rotation), bringing your free hip down toward the floor.
2. Reverse the direction and rotate your pelvis outward and upward toward the ceiling (external hip rotation), opening your hips.
3. Return smoothly to the neutral starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps before switching sides.

Cues:
Drive the movement exclusively through the hip joint of the standing leg; keep the standing foot firmly rooted and prevent the standing knee from caving inward.
exercises.author: TobiasFalk

exercises.name: Reverse Clamshell
