exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side on an exercise mat with your hips and knees bent to approximately 90 degrees, stacking your legs directly on top of each other. Support your head comfortably on your bottom arm.

Execution:
1. Keeping your knees pressed together, lift your top foot and ankle upward toward the ceiling by internally rotating your hip.
2. Pause for a second at the top of the range of motion, feeling the contraction in your hip rotators and glute muscles.
3. Lower the foot slowly and under control back to the starting position.
4. Complete your repetitions and switch to the other side.

Cues:
Keep your pelvis completely steady and perpendicular to the floor; do not allow your hips to roll forward or backward.
exercises.author: TobiasFalk

exercises.name: Clamshell to Reverse Clamshell
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side with hips and knees flexed to 90 degrees and legs stacked. Elevate your top leg slightly so that it stays suspended throughout the exercise.

Execution:
1. Keeping your heels touching, open your top knee upward into external hip rotation (standard clamshell).
2. Lower the knee, touch your knees together, and simultaneously rotate your hip to lift your top foot upward (reverse clamshell).
3. Alternate continuously between external and internal hip rotation in a smooth, controlled rhythm.

Cues:
Keep your pelvis stable and square to the front; do not let your top leg rest on the bottom leg between reps.
exercises.author: TobiasFalk

exercises.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position: Grip a bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up) at shoulder-width.


Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion.


Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch.


Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second.


Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.
exercises.author: xWan

exercises.name: YTW Raises
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie facedown on an exercise mat (or bend forward at the hips with a flat back). Extend your arms outward with your thumbs pointing up toward the ceiling.

Execution:
1. Y-Raise: Lift your straight arms diagonally forward at approximately 45 degrees, forming a 'Y' shape with your torso. Squeeze your lower and middle traps, holding for 1 to 2 seconds.
2. T-Raise: Move your arms straight out to the sides perpendicular to your body, forming a 'T' shape. Retract your shoulder blades hard and pause.
3. W-Raise: Bend your elbows and draw them down toward your ribcage while rotating your forearms back, forming a 'W' shape. Contract your rhomboids and rear delts tightly.

Cues:
Move with deliberate control without shrugging your neck; initiate all movement by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
exercises.author: probablyforging

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise (GHR)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Position yourself on a Glute-Ham Developer (GHD). Rest your knees on the curved thigh pad and secure your ankles firmly between the rollers and footplate. Begin with your torso upright and aligned with your thighs.

Execution:
1. Lower your torso forward and downward under complete control by extending your knees, keeping a straight line from knees to head.
2. Actively contract your hamstrings and glutes, flexing at the knees to pull your body back up to the vertical starting position.
3. Keep your hips extended and spine neutral throughout the entire repetition.

Cues:
Avoid breaking at the hips; if needed, use a light push off the floor or an assistance band until sufficient hamstring strength is developed.
exercises.author: personal use

exercises.name: Easy Continuous Swim (Freestyle)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Enter the pool and push off smoothly from the wall into a streamlined horizontal body position at the water's surface.

Execution:
1. Swim freestyle at a relaxed, steady conversational pace without stopping at the walls.
2. Focus on smooth, long arm strokes and a calm, rhythmic breathing pattern.
3. Keep your flutter kick relaxed, compact, and driven from your hips rather than knees.
4. Maintain a continuous swim for the designated duration or distance.

Cues:
Prioritize efficiency and body line over speed; the goal is aerobic conditioning and feel for the water.

exercises.name: Kickboard Flutter Kick
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hold a kickboard with both hands with your arms extended out in front of you. Push off the pool wall into a horizontal prone position.

Execution:
1. Initiate a steady, compact flutter kick driven from your hips rather than bending excessively at the knees.
2. Keep your legs relatively straight with soft knees and relaxed, pointed toes.
3. Keep your face in the water looking at the pool bottom, lifting your head smoothly forward only when you need to inhale.
4. Maintain a continuous, propulsion-generating kicking cadence across the pool.

Cues:
Avoid bicycle-kicking; kick primarily from the glutes and core to keep your hips high in the water.

exercises.name: Bobbing Exhale Drill
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand in chest-deep water with feet shoulder-width apart, lightly touching the pool edge if needed for reassurance.

Execution:
1. Inhale deeply through your mouth above the surface.
2. Bend your knees to submerge your head fully underwater.
3. Exhale slowly, continuously, and completely through your nose and/or mouth while submerged; a gentle hum helps regulate the airflow.
4. Push off the bottom to break the surface, take a quick breath in through your mouth, and immediately sink back down to repeat.
5. Continue bobbing up and down in a calm, continuous rhythm.

Cues:
Train yourself so that 100% of your exhalation occurs underwater; the surface time is strictly for breathing in.

exercises.name: Wall-Hold Head Rotation Drill
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hold the pool wall or gutter with one hand, body floating horizontally at the surface, with a gentle flutter kick keeping your hips up.

Execution:
1. Place your face in the water looking directly down, exhaling steadily.
2. Rotate your head to the side—without lifting it up out of the water—so that one goggle stays submerged while the other clears the surface.
3. Take a quick breath in through your mouth, then rotate your face back down into the neutral face-down position.
4. Continue the rhythmic breathing cycles, then switch hands to practice on the opposite side.

Cues:
Rest your cheek and bottom ear directly on the water surface; rotate along the long axis of your spine without lifting your head.

exercises.name: Side-Kick Breathing with Kickboard
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Push off the wall on your side. Extend your bottom arm forward holding a kickboard, and rest your top arm flat along your side and hip.

Execution:
1. Maintain a continuous flutter kick while keeping your body balanced directly on your side.
2. Keep your head in a neutral position with your face turned toward the bottom of the pool.
3. When you need air, rotate your head slightly toward the ceiling (keeping your bottom ear rested on your arm in the water) to breathe.
4. Rotate your face back downward to neutral and continue across the pool before switching to your other side.

Cues:
Maintain body alignment on your side; rotate your head cleanly along your spine rather than lifting your forehead out of the water.

exercises.name: Stroke-and-Roll Drill
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Push off the wall in a streamline position and begin swimming freestyle with a steady flutter kick.

Execution:
1. Swim 3 to 4 standard freestyle strokes.
2. When initiating a breath, roll your entire torso and hips smoothly onto your back instead of just turning your neck.
3. Remain in the backstroke position for 2 to 3 calm, full breaths while keeping your legs kicking.
4. Roll smoothly back onto your stomach into freestyle and repeat the sequence.

Cues:
Rotate your body as a single synchronized unit from hips to shoulders, eliminating tension and fear of breathing.

exercises.name: Deep-Water Recovery Bobbing
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Position yourself in slightly deeper water where you cannot easily touch bottom. Remain relaxed and vertical in the water.

Execution:
1. Inhale calmly through your mouth above the surface.
2. Allow yourself to submerge gently and exhale smoothly, slowly, and completely through your nose and mouth underwater.
3. Use a gentle sculling motion with your hands or an easy kick to guide your head back above the surface.
4. Inhale quietly and sink back under in a calm, unhurried rhythm.

Cues:
Treat this as a restorative drill between demanding swim sets to calm your heart rate and reset your respiratory control.

exercises.name: Cool-Down Swim
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Remain in the pool immediately following your workout to transition into recovery.

Execution:
1. Swim at an easy, unhurried, recovery pace for 100 to 200 meters.
2. Freely alternate between freestyle, backstroke, or gentle breaststroke.
3. Focus on long glides, relaxed breathing, and releasing all muscular tension.

Cues:
Eliminate any focus on speed or technical drills; the sole purpose is to lower your heart rate and begin active recovery.

exercises.name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your back on an exercise mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Rest your arms comfortably by your sides.

Execution:
1. Engage your abdominal muscles and contract your glutes.
2. Tilt your pelvis backward (posteriorly) so that your lower back completely flattens down firmly against the floor.
3. Hold this flattened position under active tension for 5 seconds while breathing steadily.
4. Slowly release back to the neutral starting position and repeat.

Cues:
Focus on eliminating the space beneath your lower back; this exercise rebuilds pelvic motor control to counter excessive anterior pelvic tilt (hyperlordosis).
exercises.author: Raj

exercises.name: Seated Machine Low Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit upright at a chest-supported low row machine. Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your lower chest or upper abdomen. Place your feet firmly on the footrests and rest your chest against the support pad. Grasp the handles with a neutral grip.

Execution:
1. Pull the handles smoothly back toward your waist, driving your elbows back close to your sides.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the contraction, holding for 1 second.
3. Slowly extend your arms forward under control, allowing your back muscles to stretch fully without rounding your spine.

Cues:
Keep your chest glued to the pad throughout the movement; avoid swinging your torso back to move the weight.
exercises.author: lbroggi

exercises.name: Low Pulley Cable Row (Triangle Grip)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit upright at a low pulley cable row station and attach a close-grip triangle handle (V-bar). Place your feet securely on the footrests with your knees slightly bent. Grasp the handle with both hands, sit tall with your chest lifted, and depress your shoulders.

Execution:
1. Pull the triangle handle smoothly toward your lower abdomen and navel by driving your elbows backward close to your sides.
2. Retract your shoulder blades forcefully at peak contraction and hold for 1 second.
3. Slowly extend your arms forward under control, resisting the weight stack until your arms are nearly straight and lats are fully stretched.

Cues:
Avoid swinging your torso backward to heave the weight; maintain an upright, braced core throughout the set.
exercises.author: lbroggi

exercises.name: Seated Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit firmly in the hip abduction machine with your back flat against the backrest. Adjust the leg pads so they rest comfortably against the outside of your knees or thighs. Place your feet securely on the footrests.

Execution:
1. Push your legs outward against the resistance of the pads as far as your mobility comfortably allows.
2. Hold the peak abduction for 1 to 2 seconds, squeezing your outer glutes (gluteus medius and minimus) firmly.
3. Slowly bring your knees back together under full control without allowing the weight stack to slam down.

Cues:
Maintain a steady torso flat against the seat; avoid leaning forward or using momentum.
exercises.author: lbroggi

exercises.name: Seated Hip Adduction Machine
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit squarely in the hip adduction machine with your back flat against the backrest. Set the lever arms to a comfortable open position so the pads rest on the inside of your knees and thighs.

Execution:
1. Squeeze your thighs together against the pads until they meet in the center.
2. Hold the peak contraction firmly for 1 to 2 seconds, focusing on your inner thigh adductor muscles.
3. Slowly allow the pads to return to the starting position under control, feeling a gentle stretch before the next rep.

Cues:
Control the negative phase carefully to protect the groin; keep your hips grounded on the seat.
exercises.author: lbroggi

exercises.name: Adductor Side Plank (Copenhagen Plank)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side next to a flat bench. Place the inside of your top foot and ankle (or lower leg) on top of the bench. Position your bottom forearm on the floor directly beneath your shoulder. Keep your bottom leg resting underneath the bench.

Execution:
1. Press through your bottom forearm and the inside of your top foot to lift your hips off the floor.
2. Elevate your body until your torso, hips, and top leg form a straight, rigid line level with the bench.
3. Hover your bottom leg off the floor so it floats just beneath the bench.
4. Hold this isometric position for the prescribed time, then lower with control and switch sides.

Cues:
Do not let your hips sag toward the floor or rotate forward; engage your obliques and inner thighs actively throughout.
exercises.author: hurr99

exercises.name: Band Terminal Knee Extension (TKE)
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy post at knee height. Loop the other end behind the crease of one knee. Step back into a split stance facing the anchor, with the working banded leg forward and knee slightly bent.

Execution:
1. Drive your heel into the floor and straighten your knee backward against the elastic resistance into full extension.
2. Actively squeeze your quadriceps (especially the VMO) hard at lockout for 2 to 3 seconds.
3. Allow the knee to bend slightly forward under control against the band's pull.
4. Complete your reps, then switch to the other leg.

Cues:
Keep your hips square and torso upright; do not hyperextend violently, focus on a controlled quad squeeze.
exercises.author: Rehab Hero

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit in the seated leg curl machine with your back flat against the backrest. Adjust the back pad so your knees align with the machine's pivot axis. Position the lower roller pad against the back of your lower calves, just above your heels. Lower the thigh pad firmly across your quads to secure your legs.

Execution:
1. Grasp the machine handles for stability. Flex your knees to pull the roller pad down and back beneath the seat.
2. Squeeze your hamstrings forcefully at peak flexion, holding for 1 second.
3. Slowly extend your legs back upward under complete control, resisting the weight stack until your legs are nearly straight.

Cues:
Keep your toes pointed slightly upward (dorsiflexed) or neutral; do not lift your hips off the seat during the movement.
exercises.author: Me

exercises.name: Wall Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand facing a flat wall about arm's length away. Place your palms flat against the wall slightly wider than shoulder-width apart at chest height. Step your feet back so your body leans toward the wall in a straight diagonal line.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows at about a 45-degree angle to lower your chest toward the wall under control until your nose or chest nearly touches it.
2. Press firmly through your palms to push your body away from the wall back to the starting position.
3. Keep your core braced and your spine neutral throughout the movement.

Cues:
Avoid sagging your lower back or flaring your elbows wide; this serves as an excellent beginner regression for building pressing strength.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your back on the floor or an exercise mat with knees bent and feet flat. Hold a dumbbell in one hand directly over your chest with arm extended. Keep your opposite arm resting on the floor for lateral stabilization.

Execution:
1. Lower the dumbbell slowly, keeping your elbow at roughly a 45-to-60-degree angle from your torso, until your tricep touches the floor gently.
2. Pause briefly at the bottom without letting the weight rest entirely on the floor.
3. Drive the dumbbell straight back up to full extension by contracting your chest and triceps.
4. Complete your prescribed reps, then switch hands.

Cues:
Brace your core tightly to resist torso rotation; the floor naturally restricts excessive shoulder extension.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Pike Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet forward while pushing your hips high into the air, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body. Keep your hands shoulder-width apart, arms straight, and head between your shoulders.

Execution:
1. Bend your elbows to lower your head forward and down in a tripod trajectory until the crown of your head lightly grazes the floor just ahead of your hands.
2. Press aggressively through your palms and anterior deltoids to push back and up into the starting inverted-V position.
3. Keep your core tight and maintain straight legs or slightly bent knees depending on hamstring flexibility.

Cues:
Move diagonally forward on the descent and push straight back up; avoid flaring your elbows wide outward.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Incline Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on a sturdy elevated surface such as a bench, table, or step. Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight, rigid plank from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Lower your chest toward the edge of the elevated surface with control, keeping your elbows angled back at roughly 45 degrees.
2. Maintain active tension through your core and glutes to keep your hips aligned with your spine.
3. Press firmly away from the surface until your arms are extended back to the starting plank.

Cues:
Do not allow your lower back to sag or hips to hike; adjust the height of the incline to scale difficulty smoothly toward floor push-ups.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Inverted Table Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your back beneath a heavy, sturdy table. Reach up and grasp the edge of the tabletop with an overhand or neutral grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Rest your heels on the floor and brace your core and glutes into a rigid horizontal plank.

Execution:
1. Pull your chest upward toward the underside of the table by driving your elbows backward.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together tightly at the top of the movement and pause for 1 second.
3. Lower yourself back down with control until your arms are fully extended.

Cues:
Ensure the table is completely stable before beginning; bending your knees and placing feet flat on the floor decreases resistance if needed.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Place one knee and same-side hand onto a flat bench (or adopt a staggered hinge stance supporting yourself on a sturdy surface). Keep your torso flat and parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your free hand with your arm extended toward the floor.

Execution:
1. Pull the dumbbell upward toward your hip crease by driving your elbow straight back along your ribcage.
2. Squeeze your lat and retract your shoulder blade firmly at the top, pausing for 1 second.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbell back down under control until your arm is fully extended with a mild lat stretch.
4. Complete your reps, then repeat on the opposite side.

Cues:
Do not twist your torso or jerk the weight up with momentum; keep your shoulders square to the floor.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Doorframe Bodyweight Face Pull
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Loop a sturdy bath towel around a secure doorframe or vertical post. Grasp the ends of the towel firmly with both hands. Walk your feet toward the base of the doorframe and lean your torso back with straight arms, keeping your body in a rigid plank.

Execution:
1. Pull your face toward the towel by driving your elbows high and wide out to the sides.
2. At the peak of the pull, rotate your hands back level with your ears and squeeze your rear deltoids and scapular retractors firmly for 1 second.
3. Slowly lower your body back under control until your arms are fully extended.

Cues:
Position your feet further forward to increase resistance; keep your elbows high at ear level to target the posterior deltoids and upper back.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curls
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart (or sit on a flat bench) holding a pair of dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Keep your elbows close to your torso and shoulders back.

Execution:
1. Keeping your palms facing inward, flex your elbows to curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your biceps, brachialis, and forearm muscles hard at the top of the curl for 1 second.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to full extension under complete control.

Cues:
Keep your upper arms stationary against your ribs; do not swing the weights or lean back during the curl.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your back on an exercise mat with arms extended straight up toward the ceiling. Lift your legs and bend your hips and knees to 90 degrees (tabletop position) with shins parallel to the floor. Press your lower back firmly into the floor by bracing your core.

Execution:
1. Slowly lower your right arm overhead toward the floor behind you while simultaneously extending your left leg straight out just above the floor.
2. Keep your lower back completely flat against the floor throughout the entire movement (anti-extension).
3. Return your arm and leg to the starting tabletop position under control.
4. Repeat with the left arm and right leg, alternating sides smoothly.

Cues:
Only lower your limbs as far as you can maintain full contact between your lumbar spine and the floor.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Forearm Plank
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie prone on an exercise mat. Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows directly beneath your shoulders and forearms parallel. Tuck your toes onto the floor.

Execution:
1. Engage your core and lift your hips, thighs, and knees off the floor until your body forms a straight, rigid line from head to heels.
2. Actively squeeze your glutes, quadriceps, and abdominal wall.
3. Keep your neck neutral and eyes focused directly between your forearms.
4. Hold this isometric position for the prescribed duration while maintaining steady, continuous breathing.

Cues:
Do not allow your hips to sag toward the floor or pike high in the air; maintain active posterior pelvic tilt.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position on an exercise mat. Place your wrists directly under your shoulders and your knees directly beneath your hips with a neutral spine.

Execution:
1. Slowly extend your right arm straight forward and your left leg straight back until both are parallel to the floor.
2. Keep your thumb pointing up and kick your back heel back without rotating your hips or hyperextending your lumbar spine.
3. Pause for 1 to 2 seconds at full extension, maintaining anti-rotational core stability.
4. Slowly lower your hand and knee back to the starting tabletop position.
5. Repeat on the opposite side (left arm and right leg) and alternate smoothly.

Cues:
Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back; keep your pelvis level and avoid twisting your torso.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie on your side on an exercise mat with your legs straight and feet stacked or staggered for balance. Rest on your lower forearm with your elbow placed directly beneath your shoulder.

Execution:
1. Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight diagonal line from head to feet.
2. Keep your top hand on your hip or extend it upward toward the ceiling.
3. Hold this rigid isometric position for the prescribed duration while breathing steadily.
4. Lower your hips under control and repeat on the opposite side.

Cues:
Do not let your hips sag toward the floor or roll forward; actively push through your supporting forearm to keep your shoulder stable.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your legs extended straight and together, and your arms reached overhead in line with your ears.

Execution:
1. Engage your core and press your lower back completely flat against the floor (posterior pelvic tilt).
2. Simultaneously lift your shoulder blades, head, and straight legs about 4 to 6 inches off the floor, creating a shallow curved 'banana' shape with your body.
3. Maintain full-body tension, keeping your toes pointed and glutes squeezed.
4. Hold this isometric position for the prescribed duration while breathing shallowly but continuously.
5. Lower back down to the floor under control.

Cues:
If your lower back arches off the floor at any point, regress by tucking your knees or bringing your arms forward beside your hips.
exercises.author: Vasco Custom

exercises.name: Band Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Secure a resistance band to an overhead anchor point such as a pull-up bar or door anchor. Stand facing the anchor with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Grasp the band handles or loop with an overhand or neutral grip, pinning your elbows tight against your ribs.

Execution:
1. Extend your elbows smoothly downward to pull the band straight down until your arms are fully locked out beside your thighs.
2. Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom for 1 to 2 seconds.
3. Slowly allow your elbows to flex back up under control until your forearms reach roughly 90 degrees.

Cues:
Keep your upper arms locked in place against your torso; do not swing your elbows forward or shrug your shoulders.
exercises.author: G. Johnson

exercises.name: Serratus Wall Slide
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand facing a smooth wall with feet hip-width apart. Place your forearms vertically against the wall with both elbows and wrists in firm contact, elbows roughly at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart.

Execution:
1. Actively press your forearms into the wall to protract your shoulder blades (spreading them wide across your upper back).
2. Slowly slide your forearms upward along the wall in a slight 'V' shape until your elbows reach eye or forehead level.
3. Pause at the top for 1 to 2 seconds, maintaining continuous outward and upward pressure to activate the serratus anterior.
4. Slide your forearms back down to the starting position under control.

Cues:
Maintain constant pressure against the wall throughout; do not arch your lower back as your arms slide up.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Staggered-Stance Good Morning
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Rest a barbell across your upper back (trapezius) as if preparing to squat. Take a half-step forward with one leg into a staggered (kickstand) stance. Keep the front leg nearly straight and the rear knee slightly bent for balance.

Execution:
1. Hinge forward at the hips while pushing your glutes backward, keeping your chest open and spine neutral.
2. Lower your torso until you feel a deep stretch in the hamstrings of your front working leg, stopping when your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
3. Drive your hips forward and contract your glutes and hamstrings to return smoothly to the upright starting position.
4. Complete all repetitions on one leg, then switch feet and repeat.

Cues:
Keep the load predominantly on the front heel and hip; do not round your lumbar spine at any point during the hinge.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Kneel on an exercise mat facing away from a wall, bench, or couch. Place your rear knee close to the base of the wall/bench, resting your shin vertically and foot laces-down against the support. Step your other foot forward into a 90-degree lunge position.

Execution:
1. Brace your core and actively squeeze the glute of your rear leg into a posterior pelvic tilt.
2. Slowly raise your torso up to vertical until you feel a profound stretch through the hip flexors and quadriceps of your back leg.
3. Hold this upright stretch for the prescribed time while breathing deeply and steadily.
4. Carefully ease out of the stretch and switch legs.

Cues:
Do not hyperextend your lumbar spine to get upright; keep your ribs down and glutes clenched to target the hip flexor accurately.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Long Lunge Pulse Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Step forward into an exaggerated long lunge stance. Lower your hips until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your rear knee hovers just above the floor. Optionally hold a band taut overhead with arms straight.

Execution:
1. Keep your torso tall, hips squared forward, and core engaged.
2. Gently pulse your hips up and down through a small, controlled 1-to-2-inch range of motion.
3. Maintain steady rhythmic pulses for the prescribed duration or repetitions.
4. Push off the front foot to return to standing, then repeat on the opposite leg.

Cues:
Keep the pulsing smooth and controlled rather than jerky; focus on lengthening the hip flexors and strengthening the adductors dynamically.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Front Split Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Begin in a half-kneeling position on an exercise mat. Place your hands on yoga blocks or the floor on both sides of your hips for balance and weight support.

Execution:
1. Slowly slide your front heel forward while extending your rear leg and hip straight behind you.
2. Lower your pelvis toward the floor under control, keeping your hips square to the front.
3. Stop at the point of deep, manageable muscular tension in your hamstrings and hip flexors.
4. Hold this stretch statically for the designated time (20 to 30 seconds) while maintaining calm, deep diaphragmatic breaths.
5. Carefully press into your hands to ease yourself out of the split, then repeat on the other side.

Cues:
Never bounce or force yourself beyond your current range of motion; support your body weight with your hands or place a block beneath your front thigh.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Squat Sky Reach Stretch
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lower your hips into a deep bodyweight squat. Grasp your right ankle or foot with your opposite (left) hand to anchor yourself.

Execution:
1. While maintaining the deep squat position, rotate your torso and chest toward the right side.
2. Reach your right arm up and back toward the ceiling, following your hand with your eyes.
3. Pause at the top of the rotation for 1 to 2 seconds, feeling the stretch through your thoracic spine, groin, and chest.
4. Return smoothly to the neutral deep squat position.
5. Complete repetitions on that side, then switch hands and rotate to the left.

Cues:
Keep both heels pinned flat to the floor and push your knees out; drive the twist from your mid-back (thoracic spine) rather than your neck.
exercises.author: Croak6728

exercises.name: Explosive Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a standard push-up position on the floor with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a rigid plank from head to heels.

Execution:
1. Lower your chest with control until it is just an inch above the floor.
2. Explosively drive through your palms and chest with maximum power, pushing your upper body fast enough that your hands leave the floor entirely.
3. Land softly with slightly bent elbows, absorbing the impact smoothly, and immediately descend into the next repetition.

Cues:
Maintain a rigid core throughout the jump and landing; do not let your lower back sag upon impact.
exercises.author: ege

exercises.name: Russian Push-Ups
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Begin in a standard push-up position on an exercise mat with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers facing forward, and core tightly braced in a straight line.

Execution:
1. Lower your chest toward the floor as in a standard push-up.
2. At the bottom of the movement, rock your weight backward and lower your elbows and forearms flat onto the floor into an elbow plank.
3. Rock forward forcefully back onto your hands, lifting your elbows off the ground.
4. Press straight up through your chest and triceps to lockout at the top position.

Cues:
Maintain a rigid plank line throughout the rock back and forward; do not let your hips sag when transitioning onto the forearms.
exercises.author: ege

exercises.name: Elbow Lever
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Kneel on the floor and place your hands on the mat with fingers pointing backward or turned outward. Lean your torso forward and tuck both elbows firmly into your lower abdomen or against your anterior pelvic bones (iliac crests).

Execution:
1. Lean your center of mass forward past your hands until your head lowers slightly and your feet naturally float off the floor.
2. Actively contract your erector spinae, glutes, and core to extend your legs straight, bringing your entire body horizontal and parallel to the ground.
3. Balance steadily on your hands with your elbows acting as a fulcrum.
4. Hold this static hold for time, breathing shallowly, then lower your feet back down under control.

Cues:
Keep your hands grounded and shift forward until the balance point is found; avoid collapsing the shoulders.
exercises.author: ege

exercises.name: Planche Lean Hold
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a straight-arm high plank position with your hands on the floor roughly shoulder-width apart, fingers pointed slightly outward to reduce wrist strain.

Execution:
1. Press hard through the floor to protract your scapulae (rounding your upper back) and tuck your pelvis into a hollow-body shape.
2. Keeping your elbows fully locked straight, slowly lean your shoulders as far forward as possible beyond your wrists.
3. Bear weight on your toes and hands, holding this forward-leaning isometric position for the prescribed duration.
4. Shift your shoulders back to neutral to rest.

Cues:
Never allow your elbows to bend or lower back to arch; forward lean distance directly scales shoulder loading.
exercises.author: ege

exercises.name: Arch Hang
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Transition from a dead hang into an active hang by depressing your shoulder blades away from your ears.

Execution:
1. Keeping your elbows completely locked straight, retract your shoulder blades hard and extend your thoracic spine.
2. Pull your chest upward toward the ceiling, tilting your torso back to roughly a 45-to-90-degree angle relative to the ground to form a shallow arc.
3. Squeeze your lats and lower traps forcefully at peak arch, holding the isometric position for 2 to 5 seconds.
4. Lower slowly and under control back to an active hang.

Cues:
Do not bend your elbows to pull yourself up; the movement must be driven purely by scapular retraction and lat engagement.
exercises.author: wintercyan

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart and a few inches away from your glutes. Rest your arms flat along your sides.

Execution:
1. Engage your core and drive firmly through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling.
2. Raise your hips until your thighs, pelvis, and torso form a straight line from knees to shoulders.
3. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of the movement and hold for 1 to 2 seconds.
4. Lower your hips back down under control until they lightly touch the floor, then immediately begin the next rep.

Cues:
Avoid overextending or hyperextending your lumbar spine at the top; the extension should come solely from your hip joints.
exercises.author: dvdfernandez95

exercises.name: Isometric Leg Extension
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit on the leg extension machine with your back firmly against the backrest, ensuring your knee joints align with the machine's pivot axis. Position the shin pad against your lower shins just above the ankles. Grip the side handles to anchor your hips into the seat.

Execution:
1. Extend your knees to lift the padded lever to the target angle (typically between 45 to 60 degrees of flexion, or just short of full extension).
2. Hold this position statically against the resistance for the prescribed duration, maintaining maximal contraction in the quadriceps.
3. Lower the weight slowly and under control once the hold is complete.

Cues:
Breathe steadily throughout the hold and avoid bearing down (Valsalva maneuver). Keep your hips pressed firmly into the seat and do not allow your knees to shift during the contraction.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Isometric Bench Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Lie flat on a bench with your eyes directly beneath the barbell. Retract and depress your shoulder blades, plant your feet firmly on the floor, and grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over your chest with arms extended.

Execution:
1. Lower the barbell with control to the target height (such as 1 to 2 inches off the chest or at your sticking point). Alternatively, press up against immovable safety pins set in a power rack.
2. Hold the bar completely motionless at this position for the prescribed duration, generating maximal tension across the chest, anterior deltoids, and triceps.
3. Press the bar back up to the starting lockout position (or carefully rack the bar) once the time expires.

Cues:
Maintain full-body tightness and continuous drive through your feet. Do not let the bar rest on or bounce off your ribcage during free-weight holds.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Isometric Cable Overhead Press
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand centered between low cable pulleys holding single-grip handles, or in front of a low dual-cable stack. Bring the handles up to shoulder level with an overhand grip, elbows positioned directly beneath your wrists. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and brace your core and glutes firmly.

Execution:
1. Press the cable handles upward until your hands reach forehead level or just short of full overhead lockout.
2. Hold this overhead position completely motionless against the continuous cable tension for the prescribed duration, maximally contracting your anterior deltoids and triceps.
3. Lower the handles slowly and under control back to shoulder height once the hold is finished.

Cues:
Keep your ribcage down and avoid arching your lower back. The constant multi-directional pull of the cables demands intense shoulder and core stability throughout the isometric hold.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Isometric Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand upright beside or centered between low cable pulleys. Grasp the handle with a slight bend in your elbow. Brace your core and maintain a tall, stable posture with a very subtle forward torso lean.

Execution:
1. Raise your arm out to the side in the scapular plane until your elbow reaches approximately shoulder height (parallel to the floor).
2. Hold this abducted position completely motionless against the continuous cable resistance for the prescribed duration, maintaining intense contraction in the lateral deltoid.
3. Lower the arm slowly and with full control once the time expires.

Cues:
Do not shrug your shoulder toward your ear; keep your upper traps relaxed. Maintain the fixed, slight bend in your elbow throughout the entire isometric hold rather than letting the arm drop.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Isometric Dumbbell Preacher Curl
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit at a preacher bench and adjust the seat so the top of the angled pad fits snugly into your armpits. Rest the back of your upper arm flush against the pad, holding a dumbbell in an underhand (supinated) grip.

Execution:
1. Flex your elbow to curl the dumbbell up to the mid-range point (elbow flexed at approximately 90 degrees), where mechanical leverage creates peak tension.
2. Hold this position completely static against gravity for the prescribed time, sustaining maximal contraction in the biceps and brachialis.
3. Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control once the hold duration is reached.

Cues:
Keep your arm and chest pinned against the pad without leaning back or shifting your shoulder. Keep your wrist firm and breathe steadily throughout the hold.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Isometric Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit at a lat pulldown machine and adjust the thigh pad so your legs are firmly secured. Grasp the wide bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width. Sit tall with chest proud, shoulder blades retracted and depressed, and a slight backward lean in your torso.

Execution:
1. Pull the bar down smoothly to just below your chin or upper chest level.
2. Hold this fully contracted position completely motionless for the prescribed duration, driving your elbows downward and squeezing your lats and mid-back with maximum effort.
3. Release and guide the bar upward with slow control once the hold is complete.

Cues:
Do not let the weight stack suddenly yank your arms upward at the end of the set. Keep your chest elevated and avoid rounding your shoulders forward during the hold.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Single-Arm Isometric Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Stand facing or slightly angled to a high pulley cable machine. Grasp a single-handle attachment with one hand in an overhand or neutral grip. Pin your upper arm securely against the side of your torso with your elbow bent at about 90 degrees. Hinge slightly forward at the hips and brace your core.

Execution:
1. Push down by extending your elbow until the arm reaches near full extension (or the targeted mid-range angle).
2. Hold this contracted position completely static against the cable resistance for the prescribed time, focusing on peak contraction of the triceps.
3. Allow the handle to return slowly and under control back to the 90-degree start position, then repeat on the opposite arm.

Cues:
Keep your elbow pinned to your side without allowing it to drift forward, backward, or outward during the hold. Keep your shoulder depressed and stationary.
exercises.author: HexoctusEngineering

exercises.name: Boxing Training
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Assume a balanced boxing stance in front of a heavy bag or open floor space (orthodox: left foot forward; southpaw: right foot forward). Keep your knees slightly bent, weight bouncing lightly on the balls of your feet, hands held up protecting your chin, and elbows tucked close to your ribs.

Execution:
1. Throw rhythmic, explosive punch combinations integrating jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts against the heavy bag or into the air (shadow boxing).
2. Rotate your hips, shoulders, and core with each strike to generate power through kinetic chain sequencing.
3. Maintain active footwork by circling the bag, pivoting, and resetting into your defensive guard immediately after every combination.

Cues:
Always wrap your hands and wear proper boxing gloves when hitting a heavy bag. Keep your wrists straight upon impact and exhale sharply with every punch.
exercises.author: SAH

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.description:
Starting Position:
Sit or stand tall with relaxed shoulders. Interlace your fingers together in front of your chest, or make loose fists with both hands held in front of you with elbows comfortably bent.

Execution:
1. Roll your wrists in slow, smooth circular motions through their full comfortable range of motion in a clockwise direction.
2. After the designated time (e.g., 15 to 30 seconds), reverse the motion and rotate counter-clockwise.
3. Focus on fluid movement, feeling the gentle activation and stretching through the wrist flexors and extensors.

Cues:
Keep the movement smooth and pain-free; never force the wrist into sharp angles. This is an ideal warm-up prior to pressing, handstands, front squats, or pull-ups to prepare the wrists for load.
